definition_zh: 向上；往上；以上；朝上游；向更高处、更高水平
definition_en: towards a higher place, level or amount
core_image: 一只手指着楼梯上方的台阶，视线跟着一级一级抬上去
scene: 电梯显示屏上的数字一格一格往上跳，停在顶层时门才打开。She turned her eyes upwards to the top of the tower.
sceneCN: 这里 upwards 是「向上、朝上」（第 1 个义项：朝更高的地方）；句意为她抬眼望向塔顶。手指与视线一同抬高的方向，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 副词：向上、往上；以上；向更高水平

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「向上的、上升的」，ups 去掉尾缀就是它
副词，义为「向上、起来」，是 upwards 的词干
反义词，意为「向下」
加 -ly 构成，义为「向上地」，常见于 upwardly mobile

senses.title: Towards a higher place
senses.titleCN: 朝上：朝更高的地方
senses.definition: towards a higher position in space
senses.definitionCN: 朝空间中更高的位置
senses.example: She turned her eyes upwards to the top of the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 她抬眼望向塔顶。
senses.why: The base word up already names the direction; the suffix only points the movement onwards.
senses.whyCN: 词干 up 本身已经指明方向，后缀只是让这个方向继续延伸。

senses.title: A larger amount
senses.titleCN: 以上：数量超过某个整数
senses.definition: more than a stated number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 超过所说的数字或数量
senses.example: Upwards of three hundred people attended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 参加会议的有三百人以上。
senses.why: A quantity climbing up the number line behaves like a body climbing stairs.
senses.whyCN: 数量沿数轴往上爬，就像身体沿楼梯往上走。

senses.title: Towards a higher level
senses.titleCN: 向更高水平：地位或数值上升
senses.definition: towards a higher standard, rank or price
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高的标准、等级或价格
senses.example: Prices have moved steadily upwards this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年物价稳步上涨。
senses.why: The spatial direction is borrowed for abstract scales; higher on a chart is more.
senses.whyCN: 空间方向被借到抽象尺度上：图表里越高就是越多。

senses.title: Up the river
senses.titleCN: 朝上游：往河的内陆方向
senses.definition: along a river towards its source, away from the sea
senses.definitionCN: 沿河朝源头方向、远离大海
senses.example: The boat moved slowly upwards along the narrow river.
senses.exampleCN: 小船沿着狭窄的河道慢慢向上游行驶。
senses.why: Rivers flow down to the sea, so walking inland means walking up the water.
senses.whyCN: 河水向下流向大海，所以往内陆走就是往水的上方走。

intro.en: Upwards joins the old adverb up to the direction suffix -weard, which survives in towards and forwards.
intro.cn: upwards 由古老的副词 up 加上方向后缀 -weard 构成，同款后缀还留在 towards 与 forwards 里。

items.en: Old English had uppweard, built from upp, up, plus the direction suffix -weard, turned towards.
items.cn: 古英语已有 uppweard，由 upp「向上」加方向后缀 -weard「朝向」构成。

items.en: The Norse form upp reinforced the northern dialects, giving the hard p still heard today.
items.cn: 古诺斯的 upp 强化了北方方言，留下今天仍能听到的清晰辅音。

items.en: Middle English wrote upward, still used in American spelling and in the adverb of direction.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 upward，这一形式仍用于美式拼写和方向副词。

items.en: The southern -s form won as the British adverb, while the adjective kept the short form upward.
items.cn: 带 s 的南方形式成为英式副词的标准形式，而形容词保留了短的 upward。

items.en: Today upwards of a number means more than it, a phrase fixed in nineteenth century commercial writing.
items.cn: 如今 upwards of 加数字表示「超过」，这个说法在十九世纪商业文书中固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the -wards family; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of rising.
note.cn: 形近组收同一组 -wards 方向词；近义组收表示上升的副词。

entries.definition: Towards the back; the same -wards ending.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向后」，同样带 -wards 尾缀。

entries.definition: Towards the front; another direction of the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向前」，同一词族的另一个方向。

entries.definition: In the direction of; the suffix here marks a target.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「朝向」，这里的尾缀标记目标。

entries.definition: At a later time; the same suffix used for time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「之后」，同款尾缀用在了时间上。

entries.definition: The same direction, usual as an adjective or in American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或美式副词，义为「向上的」，方向相同。

entries.definition: High up in the air; a more literary way to say upwards.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在高处」，更文学化的说法。

entries.definition: Towards the sky; upward with a picture attached.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「朝天空」，是带画面的向上。

entries.definition: At a higher position than something else, often static.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……上方」，多指静态位置。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on the direction suffix and on the phrase upwards of that appears in real news copy.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借方向后缀与真实新闻里常见的 upwards of 搭配。

normal.en: upwards is up plus a suffix that means turned towards.
normal.cn: upwards 就是 up 加上一个意为「朝向」的后缀。

normal.en: Upwards of fifty means more than fifty, not exactly fifty.
normal.cn: upwards of fifty 指超过五十，而不是正好五十。

normal.en: Stairs, prices and ages can all go upwards.
normal.cn: 楼梯、价格和年龄都可以往上走。

normal.en: The British write upwards, Americans often write upward.
normal.cn: 英式写 upwards，美式常写 upward。

normal.en: Looking upwards is a body movement before it is a metaphor.
normal.cn: 抬头向上首先是身体动作，然后才是比喻。

abstract.en: Every upward movement in the word is a number line: a place, a sum, a rank, each one higher.
abstract.cn: 这个词里每一种向上都是同一条数轴：位置、数量、等级，一个比一个高。

abstract.en: The suffix quietly says which way; the stem says how far, and the two are enough for a whole direction.
abstract.cn: 后缀悄悄说明朝哪边，词干说明朝哪里去，两者合起来就够表示一个完整方向。

abstract.en: When a word can climb stairs and prices at once, it is really describing one habit of the mind: rising.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能爬楼梯又能涨价格，它其实在描述心智的一个习惯：上升。

examples.en: The path climbs upwards through a narrow valley.
examples.cn: 小路穿过狭窄的山谷一路向上。

examples.en: Upwards of two thousand visitors came on the first day.
examples.cn: 第一天来的游客有两千以上。

examples.en: He glanced upwards at the darkening sky.
examples.cn: 他抬头看了看渐渐暗下来的天空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆往兹」——阿婆往兹（兹）边上一抬头，就是往上

root: 由古英语 upp「向上」加方向后缀 -weard 构成，古英语作 uppweard，中古英语作 upward，南部的 -s 形式固定为英式副词 upwards；同族词有 up、upward、forwards、towards。

sensesIntro.en: Upwards moves between space, number, scale and river, always in the same direction.
sensesIntro.cn: upwards 在空间、数量、尺度与河道之间移动，方向始终一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip climbs from one step to the next, never pointing down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指从一级台阶抬到下一级，从不下指。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: eyes and feet move to a higher place.
branches.cn: 空间线：眼睛和双脚移向更高的地方。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: amounts and levels climb above their old values.
branches.cn: 数量线：数量与水平爬过原来的数值。

branches.en: RIVER LINE: the boat heads inland, away from the sea.
branches.cn: 河道线：小船朝内陆驶去，远离大海。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the head tilts back to see the top.
branches.cn: 身体线：头向后仰去看顶部。

branches.en: CONTRAST: upwards of is a floor, not a ceiling.
branches.cn: 对照线：upwards of 给的是下限，不是上限。

intro.en: Upwards is a stem plus a direction suffix, then a plural-looking s; each part is real and old.
intro.cn: upwards 由词干、方向后缀和看似复数的 s 组成，每一部分都有真实的老来源。

latinIntro.en: No Latin is involved here; the word is Germanic through and through.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词与拉丁语无关，从头到尾都是日耳曼来源。

items.example: It is the core of upwards.

items.meaning: of the manner, later just an adverb
items.example: It marks the southern adverb form.
items.exampleCN: 它标记南方的副词形式。

items.example: It shows the suffix at work.
items.exampleCN: 它展示了这个后缀的作用。

items.example: It is the reverse of upwards.
items.exampleCN: 它是 upwards 的反向词。

items.example: It uses down instead of up.
items.exampleCN: 它把 up 换成了 down。

definition_zh: 紧急的；急迫的；迫切的；亟待处理的
definition_en: needing immediate attention or action
core_image: 一封信被封上红色加急标签，快递员一路按着喇叭冲进院子
scene: 深夜办公室的灯还亮着，桌上摊着一份标红的文件，秘书站在门口不知该不该打断会议。The doctor received an urgent call and left at once.
sceneCN: 这里 urgent 是「紧急的」（第 1 个义项：需要立刻处理）；句意为医生接到一个紧急电话，立刻离开了。红色加急标签催促着人马上动手，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：紧急的、急迫的；迫切的；催得很急的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「紧迫、紧急」，加 -cy 构成
加 -ly 构成，义为「紧急地、迫切地」
动词，义为「催促、力劝」，是 urgent 的同源动词
名词，义为「催促、劝告」，是 urge 的动名词

senses.title: Needing quick action
senses.titleCN: 急需处理：必须马上动手
senses.definition: requiring immediate attention or action
senses.definitionCN: 需要立刻关注或采取行动
senses.example: The doctor received an urgent call and left at once.
senses.exampleCN: 医生接到一个紧急电话，立刻离开了。
senses.why: Latin urgere means to press or push; something urgent presses on you until you move.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 urgere 意为「压、推」；紧急之事就是这样一直压着你，直到你动起来。

senses.title: Sounding insistent
senses.titleCN: 催促的语气：说得急而不容拖延
senses.definition: expressed with insistence, asking someone to act at once
senses.definitionCN: 带着不容拖延的语气，要求别人立即行事
senses.example: Her letter was an urgent plea for help.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信是一封急切的求助呼吁。
senses.why: The pressure of the verb passes into the voice: the words themselves push the reader.
senses.whyCN: 动词的压迫感进入声音：字句本身在推着读者走。

senses.title: A pressing need
senses.titleCN: 迫切的需要：缺得很急
senses.definition: a strong and immediate need for something
senses.definitionCN: 对某物强烈而即时的需求
senses.example: The village is in urgent need of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄急需干净的水。
senses.why: A need that presses is one that cannot wait for next month.
senses.whyCN: 会「压迫」的需求，就是等不到下个月的那种需求。

senses.title: Important and pressing
senses.titleCN: 重要而急迫：事情本身分量重
senses.definition: important enough that delay would cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 重要到一旦拖延就会造成损害
senses.example: Finding shelter became urgent as the storm grew.
senses.exampleCN: 随着暴风雨加剧，找到避难所变得紧迫起来。
senses.why: Urgency here is not noise but weight: the matter presses because the cost of delay is high.
senses.whyCN: 这里的紧迫不是喧闹而是分量：拖延代价高，事情才压得紧。

intro.en: Urgent comes from the Latin verb urgere, to press or drive on, through its present participle urgens.
intro.cn: urgent 来自拉丁语动词 urgere「压、驱赶」，取其现在分词 urgens。

items.en: The verb urgere meant to push, press or drive something forward.
items.cn: 动词 urgere 意为推、压、把某物向前赶。

items.en: Its present participle urgens described whatever is pressing at this very moment.
items.cn: 它的现在分词 urgens 描述此刻正在施压的东西。

items.en: Old French took the participle as urgent, still carrying the pressure of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 古法语把这一分词借作 urgent，仍带着拉丁动词的压迫感。

items.en: English borrowed urgent in the fifteenth century for matters that would not wait.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 urgent，用来指不容等待的事情。

items.en: Modern usage pairs it with need, action and care, all situations where delay costs something.
items.cn: 现代用法把它和 need、action、care 搭配，都是拖延会付出代价的情形。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the urg- stem and its Latin family; the near-meaning group holds synonyms about haste and necessity.
note.cn: 形近组沿 urg- 词干及其拉丁词族；近义组收表示急切与必要的近义词。

entries.definition: To press someone to act; the verb behind urgent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「催促、力劝」，是 urgent 背后的动词。

entries.definition: The quality of being urgent; the noun built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「紧迫性」，由 urgent 构成。

entries.definition: In an urgent manner; the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「紧急地」，是它的副词形式。

entries.definition: Medical help for problems that cannot wait.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「急诊服务」，指不能等待的医疗。

entries.definition: Needing action now; literally weighing on you.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「紧迫的」，字面上就是压在你身上。

entries.definition: Absolutely necessary; stronger and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必须的」，更正式也更绝对。

entries.definition: So important that failure would be serious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「关键的、危急的」，失败后果严重。

entries.definition: Happening without delay, without the sense of pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「立即的」，但不含压力感。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pressing image of the Latin verb and real collocations such as urgent need.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用拉丁动词的「压」意象，以及 urgent need 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Urgent shares a root with urge: both push somebody to move.
normal.cn: urgent 与 urge 同根，都在推动某人行动。

normal.en: An urgent call is one you answer before you finish your tea.
normal.cn: 紧急电话就是茶没喝完就得接的那种电话。

normal.en: In urgent need means the need is pressing right now.
normal.cn: in urgent need 指此刻就急得压人。

normal.en: Urgent care is the clinic you go to when waiting is not an option.
normal.cn: urgent care 就是不能等时去的那种诊所。

normal.en: Mark urgent on an envelope and the postman hurries.
normal.cn: 在信封上写 urgent，邮差就会加快脚步。

abstract.en: The whole word is a hand on your back: urgency is pressure whose source you may not even see.
abstract.cn: 整个词就是一只推着你后背的手：紧迫感来自一种你甚至看不见的压力。

abstract.en: Something is urgent when the cost of waiting exceeds the cost of acting.
abstract.cn: 一件事之所以紧急，是因为等待的代价超过了行动的代价。

abstract.en: Urgency is a comparison in time, not a size: the small thing that must be done now outranks the big thing that can wait.
abstract.cn: 紧迫是时间上的比较而非体量：必须现在做的小事，压过可以等的大事。

examples.en: There is an urgent need for more nurses in the region.
examples.cn: 该地区急需更多护士。

examples.en: He sent an urgent message asking us to postpone the meeting.
examples.cn: 他发来紧急消息，要求我们推迟会议。

examples.en: The repairs are urgent because the roof leaks badly.
examples.cn: 修理很紧急，因为屋顶漏得很厉害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿真急」——饿了真急，得马上找饭吃：紧急的

root: 源自拉丁语动词 urgere「压、驱赶」的现在分词 urgens，经古法语 urgent 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 urge、urgency、urgently。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of urgent move from the call that must be answered to the need, the plea and the weight of the matter.
sensesIntro.cn: urgent 的四个义项从必须接的电话，走到需求、诉求与事情本身的分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red label on an envelope, and a hand pushing you towards the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：信封上的红色标签，以及一只把你推向门口的手。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the thing must be done at once.
branches.cn: 时间线：这件事必须立刻完成。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: the words themselves push the reader.
branches.cn: 声音线：字句本身在推动读者。

branches.en: NEED LINE: what is missing is missing badly.
branches.cn: 需求线：缺的东西缺得很厉害。

branches.en: WEIGHT LINE: delay would cause real harm.
branches.cn: 分量线：拖延会造成真实损害。

branches.en: CONTRAST: important can wait, urgent cannot.
branches.cn: 对照线：重要的可以等，紧急的不能等。

intro.en: Urgent is a Latin participle stripped of its ending and used as an English adjective.
intro.cn: urgent 是一个去掉词尾的拉丁分词，直接充当英语形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are clear: the verb urgere and the participle ending -ens, -entis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁构件很清楚：动词 urgere 与分词词尾 -ens、-entis。

items.example: It is the root of urgent.
It turns the verb into an adjective.
It forms insurgent from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 它和同一动词构成 insurgent。

items.example: It forms surge from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 它和同一动词构成 surge。

items.example: It shows the word in a fixed phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它展示了这个词的固定搭配。

definition_zh: 我们（宾格）；我们（口语里作表语）；咱们
definition_en: the speaker together with other people, used as the object form of we
core_image: 一圈人彼此搭着肩膀，手往自己身上和身边同伴指过去
scene: 老师站在讲台上环视全班，用手指着自己的胸口又划向所有学生。Please wait for us outside the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 us 是「我们（宾格）」（第 1 个义项：动作的接受者）；句意为请在门口等我们。手指从自己划向同伴的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 代词：我们（宾格）；咱们

derivatives.zh: 代词，义为「我们」的主格形式
限定词，义为「我们的」，用在名词前
代词，义为「我们的（东西）」，独立使用
代词，义为「我们自己」，反身形式
古旧说法，义为「朝向我们这边」，现已罕用

senses.title: The object form
senses.titleCN: 宾格我们：动作落到我们身上
senses.definition: the object form of we, used after a verb or a preposition
senses.definitionCN: we 的宾格形式，用在动词或介词之后
senses.example: Please wait for us outside the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 请在门口等我们。
senses.why: English keeps a separate shape for we as a target; us is that shape, worn down by centuries of speech.
senses.whyCN: 英语为作为「接受者」的 we 保留了另一个形状，us 就是这个形状，被数百年的口语磨损得极短。

senses.title: The speaker and others
senses.titleCN: 说话人加上身边的人
senses.definition: the speaker together with one or more other people, excluding the listener
senses.definitionCN: 说话人和一个或多个其他人，不含听话人
senses.example: They invited us but not our neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们邀请了我们，却没邀请我们的邻居。
senses.why: The group is drawn around the speaker alone; the listener stands outside the circle.
senses.whyCN: 这个圈子只围着说话人画，听话人站在圈外。

senses.title: Including the listener
senses.titleCN: 包括听话人在内
senses.definition: a warm or informal use that draws the listener into the group
senses.definitionCN: 一种亲切或口语的用法，把听话人拉进群里
senses.example: Come on, let us give it one more try.
senses.exampleCN: 来吧，咱们再试一次。
senses.why: Add the listener and we becomes us in a friendly sense, the tone of a shared task.
senses.whyCN: 把听话人加进来，we 就成了亲切的 us，共用一件事的口吻。

senses.title: After a preposition
senses.titleCN: 介词后面：介词宾语
senses.definition: the form required after most prepositions such as with, for or to
senses.definitionCN: 跟在 with、for、to 等多数介词后必须使用的形式
senses.example: There is no need to worry about us.
senses.exampleCN: 没有必要为我们担心。
senses.why: Grammar fixes the shape here: prepositions never take the subject form we.
senses.whyCN: 语法在这里锁定了形状：介词后从不接主格 we。

senses.title: In informal agreement
senses.titleCN: 口语句尾：跟着附和一句「我们也是」
senses.definition: a short reply in speech, meaning the same is true of us
senses.definitionCN: 口语里的简短回答，意为「我们也一样」
senses.example: They are coming, and so are we, all of us.
senses.exampleCN: 他们要来，我们也来，我们全体都来。
senses.why: The tiny word does a lot of social work: it turns a statement about them into one about us.
senses.whyCN: 这个小词承担了社交工作：把关于他们的陈述变成关于我们。

intro.en: Us is the worn-down object form of the old Germanic pronoun we, sharing a root with German uns and Dutch ons.
intro.cn: us 是古老的日耳曼语代词 we 被磨短的宾格形式，与德语 uns、荷兰语 ons 同源。

items.en: Old English used us beside the dative form usic, both meaning we as an object.
items.cn: 古英语用 us 表示宾格，另有与格 form usic，意思都是作为宾语的我们。

items.en: The Germanic form uns appears in German as uns and in Dutch as ons, unchanged in sense.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 uns 见于德语 uns 与荷兰语 ons，意义不变。

items.en: Middle English lost the dative ending, leaving us to cover both object roles.
items.cn: 中古英语丢掉了与格词尾，us 于是同时承担两种宾语角色。

items.en: The final s softened to a voiced sound in unstressed speech, though the strong form kept it sharp.
items.cn: 在非重读语流里末尾的 s 变成浊音，而重读形式仍然保持清音。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as let us and all of us froze the word in daily use.
items.cn: let us、all of us 等固定搭配把这个词冻在日常生活里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pronoun family; the near-meaning group gathers other pronouns of person and group.
note.cn: 形近组收同一代词族；近义组收其他表示人称与群体的代词。

entries.definition: The subject form of the same pronoun.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「我们」，同族代词的主格。

entries.definition: The possessive form used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「我们的」，名词前的所有格。

entries.definition: The possessive pronoun used alone.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「我们的（东西）」，独立使用。

entries.definition: The reflexive form for a plural we.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「我们自己」，复数的反身形式。

entries.definition: The same object role, but only for the speaker.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「我（宾格）」，只指说话人一人。

entries.definition: The person or people spoken to, not spoken of.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「你、你们」，指听话人。

entries.definition: Other people as the object, outside both circles.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「他们（宾格）」，画外的一方。

entries.definition: All people, including speaker and listener.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「每个人」，包括说话人与听话人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pronoun family and the real phrases us often appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用代词一族与该词真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: We does the action, us receives it: They called us.
normal.cn: we 做动作，us 承受动作：打电话的是他们，被呼叫的是我们。

normal.en: Let us in speech often becomes let’s, with the us folded away.
normal.cn: 口语里 let us 常缩成 let’s，us 被折没了。

normal.en: All of us is a crowd, one of us is a single member.
normal.cn: all of us 是一群人，one of us 其中一员。

normal.en: Us is two letters but the shortest word for company.
normal.cn: us 只有两个字母，却是一个表示同伙的最短的词。

normal.en: After a preposition, English insists on us, never we.
normal.cn: 介词之后英语只认 us，从不写 we。

abstract.en: Us is a boundary word: it marks where the speaker’s circle ends and everyone else begins.
abstract.cn: us 是一个边界词：它标出说话人的圈子到哪儿结束、别人从哪儿开始。

abstract.en: The word shrinks as the group grows: the more people it covers, the shorter the sound.
abstract.cn: 这个词越短反而覆盖的人越多：越被磨小的声音，指的人越广。

abstract.en: Every use of us is a small act of alliance, deciding who stands inside.
abstract.cn: 每一次说 us 都是一次小小的结盟，决定谁站在圈内。

examples.en: Please wait for us outside the gate.
examples.cn: 请在门口等我们。

examples.en: They invited us to dinner on Saturday.
examples.cn: 他们邀我们周六去吃晚饭。

examples.en: Most of us had never seen snow before.
examples.cn: 我们大多数人以前从没见过雪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊死」——啊，死也要一起去：我们

root: 源自古英语代词 us（宾格/与格），与德语 uns、荷兰语 ons 同属日耳曼语形式 uns；同族词有 we、our、ours、ourselves。

sensesIntro.en: Us covers the plain object form, the circle around the speaker, the friendly inclusion and a few fixed grammar slots.
sensesIntro.cn: us 覆盖了普通宾格、说话人的圈子、亲切的包容，以及几个固定语法位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle drawn around the speaker and some companions, with the listener possibly inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：以说话人为中心画一个圈，圈里是若干同伴，听话人可能在圈内也可能在圈外。

branches.en: GRAMMAR LINE: the form used after verbs and prepositions.
branches.cn: 语法线：动词和介词之后使用的形式。

branches.en: BOUNDARY LINE: the speaker plus others, not the listener.
branches.cn: 边界线：说话人加若干他人，不含听话人。

branches.en: WARMTH LINE: the listener is drawn inside the circle.
branches.cn: 亲切线：听话人被拉进圈内。

branches.en: SOCIAL LINE: a short reply that agrees for the whole group.
branches.cn: 社交线：为整组人表示同意的简短回答。

branches.en: CONTRAST: we acts, us is acted upon.
branches.cn: 对照线：we 发动作，us 受动作。

intro.en: Us has no affixes; it is a single pronoun stem inherited whole from Old English.
intro.cn: us 没有词缀，是从古英语整块继承下来的代词词干。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin in this word; the pronoun is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里没有拉丁成分，整个代词属于日耳曼语。

items.example: It is the subject partner of us.
items.exampleCN: 它是 us 的主格搭档。

items.example: It forms himself and herself too.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 himself 与 herself。

definition_zh: 消失；突然不见；使（某物）消失；灭绝、不复存在
definition_en: to disappear suddenly and completely
core_image: 一只兔子被人一晃，转眼连影子都不见了
scene: 魔术师掀开黑色幕布，台上那只鸟扑扇了两下就不见了。The coin vanished from his hand before we could blink.
sceneCN: 这里 vanish 是「消失、突然不见」（第 1 个义项：突然且彻底地不见）；句意为那枚硬币在我们眨眼之前就从他手里消失了。鸟连影子都没留下，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：消失、突然不见；使消失；灭绝、不复存在

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「消失的、正在逐渐消失的」，如 vanishing point
形容词，义为「已消失的、不复存在的」
名词，义为「虚荣、空虚」，与 vanish 同源于拉丁语 vanus「空的」
形容词，义为「迅速消逝的」，同源且更书面
名词短语，义为「消失点、尽头」

senses.title: To disappear suddenly
senses.titleCN: 突然消失：转眼不见
senses.definition: to disappear suddenly and completely from sight
senses.definitionCN: 突然且彻底地从视野中消失
senses.example: The coin vanished from his hand before we could blink.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚硬币在我们眨眼之前就从他手里消失了。
senses.why: Latin vanus means empty; what vanishes leaves empty space where it stood.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vanus 意为「空的」；消失之物站过的地方就空了下来。

senses.title: To disappear by magic
senses.titleCN: 被变没了：靠手法让东西不见
senses.definition: to make something disappear as if by magic, or to disappear that way
senses.definitionCN: 像变戏法一样使某物消失，或那样消失
senses.example: The magician made the silk scarf vanish in a flash.
senses.exampleCN: 魔术师一下子让那条丝巾消失不见了。
senses.why: Magic borrows the word for the most literal emptiness: the object is gone and the hand is shown empty.
senses.whyCN: 魔术借这个词表达最字面的「空」：物件没了，手心也摊开是空的。

senses.title: To stop existing
senses.titleCN: 不存在了：彻底消失、灭绝
senses.definition: to cease to exist, often gradually and on a large scale
senses.definitionCN: 不再存在，常指逐渐、大范围地消失
senses.example: Many small languages may vanish within this century.
senses.exampleCN: 许多小语种可能在本世纪内消失。
senses.why: The empty place is no longer a spot on stage but a whole category that is gone.
senses.whyCN: 这个空位不再只是舞台上的一块地方，而是一整个类别不复存在。

senses.title: To fade from use
senses.titleCN: 淡出使用：渐渐从日常里退场
senses.definition: to disappear from common use or from memory
senses.definitionCN: 从常用范围或记忆中淡出
senses.example: The old custom has almost vanished from the countryside.
senses.exampleCN: 这项旧风俗在乡间已几乎消失。
senses.why: Nothing dramatic is needed; the word covers quiet absence as well as sudden loss.
senses.whyCN: 不必有戏剧性场面；这个词既指突然丢失，也指安静的缺席。

senses.title: To become zero
senses.titleCN: 归零：数值一下子消掉
senses.definition: to drop suddenly to nothing, said of amounts or chances
senses.definitionCN: 指数量或机会突然降到零
senses.example: All our savings vanished in one bad deal.
senses.exampleCN: 所有积蓄在一次糟糕的交易中化为乌有。
senses.why: A number that disappears leaves the same empty place as an object that disappears.
senses.whyCN: 一个消失的数字留下的空位，和消失的物件完全相同。

intro.en: Vanish goes back to Latin vanus, empty, through the verb evanescere, to pass away.
intro.cn: vanish 上溯到拉丁语 vanus「空的」，经由动词 evanescere「逝去」而来。

items.en: The adjective vanus meant empty, hollow or without substance.
items.cn: 形容词 vanus 意为空的、虚的、没有实质的。

items.en: The verb evanescere meant to pass away or fade from sight, built with the prefix e- meaning out.
items.cn: 动词 evanescere 意为逝去、从视野中淡出，由表示向外的前缀 e- 构成。

items.en: Old French esvanir shortened the word and kept the sense of disappearing completely.
items.cn: 古法语 esvanir 缩短了这个词，保留了彻底消失的意思。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, spelling it variously before settling on vanish.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，拼法几经变化才定成 vanish。

items.en: Modern English extended it from objects disappearing to languages, customs and sums of money.
items.cn: 现代英语把它从物件消失扩展到语言、风俗与金钱。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of emptiness; the near-meaning group holds verbs of going out of sight.
note.cn: 形近组沿表达「空」的拉丁词干；近义组收表示离开视野的动词。

entries.definition: Emptiness turned into pride; same Latin vanus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「虚荣」，同出拉丁 vanus「空的」。

entries.definition: Fading quickly away, closer to the Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迅速消逝的」，更接近拉丁动词形式。

entries.definition: The act of disappearing; used in vanishing point.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「消失（的）」，见于 vanishing point。

entries.definition: A rare noun for the state of being gone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，罕用，义为「消失的状态」。

entries.definition: The plain word for going out of sight, without the suddenness.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不见了」，最普通的说法，不带突兀感。

entries.definition: To grow weaker and less visible by degrees.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「渐渐褪去」，一点一点变淡。

entries.definition: To turn into vapour, or to melt away like vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「蒸发」，像汽一样散去。

entries.definition: To break up and pass into nothing or into a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「溶解、消散」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the empty-space core and phrases such as vanish into thin air.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「空出位置」的核心意象与 vanish into thin air 这类搭配。

normal.en: Vanish shares a root with vanity: both come from a Latin word for empty.
normal.cn: vanish 与 vanity 同根，都出自拉丁语「空的」。

normal.en: Vanish into thin air is the phrase for a disappearance with no explanation.
normal.cn: vanish into thin air 指毫无解释地不见。

normal.en: A magician makes things vanish, but the hand is simply faster than the eye.
normal.cn: 魔术师让东西消失，其实只是手比眼快。

normal.en: Languages and customs vanish slowly, coins vanish at once.
normal.cn: 语言与风俗消失得慢，硬币却是立刻就没了。

normal.en: Vanish from sight means the eye loses it, not that it never existed.
normal.cn: vanish from sight 指眼睛看不见了，而不是它从未存在。

abstract.en: The word keeps pointing at a hole: something stood here, and now only the outline remains.
abstract.cn: 这个词一直指着那个洞：刚才这里还有东西，如今只剩下轮廓。

abstract.en: Disappearance is a change in the viewer, not always in the thing: vanish describes what the eye reports.
abstract.cn: 消失有时是观看者的变化而非事物的变化：这个词记录的是眼睛的报告。

abstract.en: A word built on emptiness can describe magic, extinction and debt with one motion of the hand.
abstract.cn: 一个以「空」为根的词，用一个挥手的动作就能讲魔术、灭绝与破产。

examples.en: The sun vanished behind the clouds.
examples.cn: 太阳消失在云层后面。

examples.en: He vanished into the crowd before anyone could stop him.
examples.cn: 还没人拦住他，他就消失在人群里了。

examples.en: The keys seem to have vanished from the table.
examples.cn: 钥匙好像从桌上消失了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇泥石」——哇，泥石流一来，房子瞬间不见了：消失

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 vanus「空的」及其动词 evanescere「逝去」，经古法语 esvanir 于十四世纪进入英语；同族词有 vanity、evanescent。

sensesIntro.en: Vanish runs from a coin leaving a hand, through magic and extinction, to habits and savings that empty out.
sensesIntro.cn: vanish 从手里飞走的硬币，经魔术与灭绝，到淡出的风俗与归零的存款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object leaves and the place where it stood is suddenly empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：物件离场，它待过的地方突然空了。

branches.en: SIGHT LINE: the eye loses the object at once.
branches.cn: 视觉线：眼睛一下子抓不到物件。

branches.en: STAGE LINE: the hand is shown empty on purpose.
branches.cn: 舞台线：手心故意摊开给人看是空的。

branches.en: EXISTENCE LINE: whole languages and customs quietly go.
branches.cn: 存在线：整门语言与风俗悄然退场。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: the amount falls to zero.
branches.cn: 数值线：数字一下落到零。

branches.en: CONTRAST: vanish is sudden, fade is gradual.
branches.cn: 对照线：vanish 突兀，fade 渐缓。

intro.en: Vanish carries a Latin root for emptiness plus English verb endings; its relatives hide in common words.
intro.cn: vanish 带一个表示「空」的拉丁词根和英语动词词尾，它的亲属藏在常见词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is vanus, empty, with the verb evanescere behind the first syllable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 vanus「空的」，开头的 e- 则来自动词 evanescere。

items.example: It carries the core of vanish.
items.exampleCN: 它承载 vanish 的核心义。

items.example: It forms evanescere, to pass out of sight.
It uses the word in art.

definition_zh: 蒸气；水汽；雾气；（物理上）气态物质；美式拼作 vapor
definition_en: a mass of tiny drops or gas, such as water in the air, that can be seen or felt
core_image: 一壶开水冒着白气，气一碰到窗玻璃就凝成水珠
scene: 清晨的湖面浮着一层薄薄的白气，太阳一照便慢慢散开。Thick vapour rose from the hot spring and hid the rocks behind it.
sceneCN: 这里 vapour 是「蒸气、水汽」（第 1 个义项：水变成的气体或细小水滴）；句意为温泉升起浓重的水汽，把后面的岩石遮住了。水壶上升腾又凝成珠的白气，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：蒸气、水汽；雾气；气态物质（英式拼写，美式为 vapor）

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「汽化、使蒸发」
名词，义为「雾化器、蒸发器」
形容词，义为「雾状的、含汽的、缥缈的」
动词，义为「蒸发」，同源于拉丁语 vapor 与 ex-

senses.title: Water in the air
senses.titleCN: 水汽：从水面升起的白气
senses.definition: tiny drops or invisible gas from water, often visible as mist
senses.definitionCN: 水形成的细小水滴或气体，常以雾状可见
senses.example: Thick vapour rose from the hot spring and hid the rocks behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 温泉升起浓重的水汽，把后面的岩石遮住了。
senses.why: Latin vapor named steam or exhalation; the word has always pictured something rising off a wet surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vapor 指蒸汽或呼气；这个词一直带着从湿面上腾起的画面。

senses.title: A gas in science
senses.titleCN: 气态：物理上区别于液体固体的状态
senses.definition: the gaseous state of a substance that is liquid or solid at room temperature
senses.definitionCN: 常温下是液体或固体的物质的气态形式
senses.example: At this pressure the fuel turns into vapour before it burns.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个压力下，燃油在燃烧前就变成气态。
senses.why: Science sharpened the old picture into a term: vapour is a substance in its gas phase.
senses.whyCN: 科学把旧画面锐化成一个术语：vapour 是物质处在气态阶段。

senses.title: Mist on glass
senses.titleCN: 玻璃上的雾气：冷凝的一层水膜
senses.definition: condensed droplets that cloud a cold surface
senses.definitionCN: 凝在冷表面上形成一层模糊水膜的小水珠
senses.example: The bathroom mirror was covered in vapour after the hot shower.
senses.exampleCN: 热水澡后浴室的镜子上蒙了一层水汽。
senses.why: The same vapour that rises goes back to liquid on a cold surface; the word covers both the rising and the settling.
senses.whyCN: 升起的水汽在冷面上变回液体；这个词既指升腾也指凝结。

senses.title: Figurative haze
senses.titleCN: 缥缈：像雾一样抓不住的东西
senses.definition: something vague and fleeting, compared to mist
senses.definitionCN: 像雾一样模糊而短暂的东西
senses.example: His plans melted into vapour as the money ran out.
senses.exampleCN: 钱一花完，他的计划就化作一阵虚无。
senses.why: Mist can hide things without destroying them; the metaphor borrows this to describe hopes and promises.
senses.whyCN: 雾能遮住东西却不破坏它；比喻借这一点来形容希望与承诺。

intro.en: Vapour comes from the Latin noun vapor, steam or exhalation, and keeps its American and British spellings side by side.
intro.cn: vapour 来自拉丁语名词 vapor「蒸汽、呼气」，英式与美式两种拼写至今并存。

items.en: Latin vapor meant steam, exhalation or a light mist rising from something wet.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vapor 指蒸汽、呼出的气，或从湿物上腾起的薄雾。

items.en: Old French took the word as vapour, keeping the meaning of rising steam.
items.cn: 古法语借作 vapour，保留了升腾蒸汽之义。

items.en: English adopted the French form in the late Middle Ages for steam and cloudy air.
items.cn: 英语在中山后期借入法语形式，用于蒸汽与浑浊的空气。

items.en: American usage dropped the u under Noah Webster´s influence, giving vapor, while Britain kept vapour.
items.cn: 美式在韦伯斯特影响下删去 u，写成 vapor，英国则保留 vapour。

items.en: In physics the word settled down as the gas phase of a substance that is normally liquid or solid.
items.cn: 在物理学里，这个词定型为常温液或固体的气态阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the vapor- family; the near-meaning group holds clouds of damp air.
note.cn: 形近组收 vapor- 词族；近义组收表示潮湿空气与云的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蒸气」，同一名词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: The verb for turning into vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「汽化」，由本词加 -ize 构成。

entries.definition: Full of vapour or mist, or figuratively vague.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「雾状的、缥缈的」。

entries.definition: To pass off as vapour; uses the same Latin base.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「蒸发」，用同一个拉丁词基。

entries.definition: Water vapour at high temperature, often visible as a white jet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蒸汽」，高温水蒸气，常呈白色喷射状。

entries.definition: Fine droplets hanging in the air, lighter than fog.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薄雾」，比雾更轻。

entries.definition: Thick cloud near the ground that cuts visibility down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「浓雾」，贴近地面、遮挡视线的云团。

entries.definition: Any substance in the air-like state, a wider scientific term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气体」，更宽泛的科学术语。

normalIntro.en: The hooks rely on the kettle picture and on real phrases such as water vapour.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依靠水壶画面的意象以及 water vapour 这样的真实搭配。

normal.en: Vapour and vapor are the same word; only the u differs.
normal.cn: vapour 与 vapor 是同一个词，只差一个 u。

normal.en: Water vapour is invisible; what you see above a kettle is condensed droplets.
normal.cn: 水蒸气本身不可见，水壶上方看到的是凝结成的小水珠。

normal.en: A vapour trail is the white line a jet leaves across the sky.
normal.cn: vapour trail 是飞机在天空留下的白线。

normal.en: Add -ize and vapour becomes the verb vaporize, to turn into gas.
normal.cn: 加上 -ize，vapour 就变成动词 vaporize「汽化」。

normal.en: Mist on a cold mirror is vapour going back to liquid water.
normal.cn: 冷镜子上的水汽，就是汽又变回了液态水。

abstract.en: Vapour is matter in its most fugitive form: present, yet ready to be gone.
abstract.cn: 汽是物质最易逃逸的形态：明明在场，却随时准备消失。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a physical cloud to a mental one, because mist already hides things.
abstract.cn: 这个词很自然地从物理的雾走到心里的雾，因为雾本来就会遮东西。

abstract.en: Water crosses three names in one day: ice, water, vapour; the last one is the one that travels.
abstract.cn: 水一天里走过三个名字：冰、水、汽；最后那个才是会旅行的。

examples.en: Water vapour rises from the sea and forms clouds.
examples.cn: 水汽从海面升起，聚成云。

examples.en: A cloud of vapour hung over the boiling pot.
examples.cn: 沸腾的锅上方悬着一团水汽。

examples.en: The cold window was soon covered with vapour.
examples.cn: 冰冷的窗户很快蒙上了一层水汽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为泼」——水被熬得为泼（蒸发）出去，只剩气：蒸气

root: 源自拉丁语名词 vapor「蒸汽、呼气」，经古法语 vapour 进入英语；美式拼作 vapor；同族词有 vaporize、vaporous、evaporate。

sensesIntro.en: Vapour starts as visible steam, narrows into a scientific gas phase, and ends up as figurative mist.
sensesIntro.cn: vapour 从看得见的蒸汽出发，缩成一个科学上的气态术语，最后化作比喻的雾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white air lifts off hot water and turns back into drops on cold glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：白气从热水上升起，又在冷玻璃上变回水珠。

branches.en: AIR LINE: visible vapour above hot water.
branches.cn: 空气线：热水上方可见的水汽。

branches.en: SCIENCE LINE: a substance in its gas state.
branches.cn: 科学线：物质的气态形式。

branches.en: GLASS LINE: drops settle on cold surfaces.
branches.cn: 玻璃线：水珠凝在冷表面上。

branches.en: METAPHOR LINE: plans that melt into haze.
branches.cn: 比喻线：计划化成一片迷雾。

branches.en: CONTRAST: vapour is invisible, mist is what you see.
branches.cn: 对照线：水汽本身不可见，雾是你看见的东西。

intro.en: Vapour is a whole Latin noun; its English relatives come from adding standard endings.
intro.cn: vapour 是一个完整的拉丁名词，英语亲属词都由标准词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is vapor, with the verb evaporare formed from ex- plus vapor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 vapor，动词 evaporare 由前缀 ex- 加 vapor 构成。

items.example: It is the whole base of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词的完整词基。

items.example: It shows the word in use.
It is the most common pairing.

definition_zh: 变量；可变因素；可变物；形容词：可变的、多变的、不稳定的
definition_en: something that can change, or likely to change
core_image: 温度计里的液柱一天里上上下下，数字始终不肯稳住
scene: 实验台上摊着记录表，同一组数据每隔一小时就微微变动一次。Weather is the hardest variable to control in an outdoor experiment.
sceneCN: 这里 variable 是「变量、可变因素」（第 1 个义项：会变的东西）；句意为天气是户外实验中最难控制的可变因素。液柱上下不定的样子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：变量；可变因素；可变物
形容词：可变的、多变的；不稳定的

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「变化、不同」，是本词的动词形式
名词，义为「可变性、变化幅度」
副词，义为「多变地、不定地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不变的、恒定的」
形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同根

senses.title: A quantity that changes
senses.titleCN: 变量：数学里可取的数值会变
senses.definition: a letter or symbol that can take different numerical values
senses.definitionCN: 可以取不同数值的字母或符号
senses.example: In the equation, x is the variable and two is the constant.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，x 是变量，二则是常数。
senses.why: Latin variare means to change; a variable is simply the name for something allowed to change.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为变化；变量就是「允许变化之物」的名字。

senses.title: A factor in an experiment
senses.titleCN: 实验因素：会影响结果的一项条件
senses.definition: a condition or factor that can differ and so affect a result
senses.definitionCN: 会变化并因此影响结果的条件或因素
senses.example: Weather is the hardest variable to control in an outdoor experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 天气是户外实验中最难控制的可变因素。
senses.why: Science isolates one changing factor at a time, and the word names that chosen factor.
senses.whyCN: 科学一次只隔离一个变化因素，这个词就指那个被选出的因素。

senses.title: Something able to change
senses.titleCN: 可变的东西：性质本身会变动
senses.definition: a thing or quality that is capable of changing
senses.definitionCN: 本身具有变化能力的事物或性质
senses.example: Rainfall in this valley is highly variable from year to year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的降雨量逐年变化很大。
senses.why: The noun and the adjective share one idea: capacity for change, not a fixed state.
senses.whyCN: 名词与形容词共有一个想法：具备变化的能力，而非固定状态。

senses.title: Changeable in character
senses.titleCN: 多变的：形容性格或天气靠不住
senses.definition: likely to change suddenly, used of weather, mood or moody people
senses.definitionCN: 容易突然改变，用于天气、情绪或反复无常的人
senses.example: She has a variable temper, sunny one hour and cold the next.
senses.exampleCN: 她脾气多变，一小时和颜悦色，下一小时就冷若冰霜。
senses.why: The abstract capacity for change becomes a judgement about reliability.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的变化能力，变成了对可靠性的判断。

senses.title: Not constant in cost
senses.titleCN: 可变的成本：随业务量上下浮动
senses.definition: changing with the level of activity, said of costs or prices
senses.definitionCN: 随活动量上下浮动，用于成本或价格
senses.example: Fuel is a variable cost that rises with every extra delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 燃油是一项可变成本，每多送一趟就上涨。
senses.why: Business reuses the mathematical idea: some numbers follow output instead of staying put.
senses.whyCN: 商业沿用了数学的想法：有些数字随产量走，而不是原地不动。

intro.en: Variable comes from Latin variare, to change, through the adjective variabilis and Old French.
intro.cn: variable 来自拉丁语动词 variare「变化」，经形容词 variabilis 与古法语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective varius described things spotted, mixed or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述斑驳的、混杂的或多种多样的事物。

items.en: From it came the verb variare, to make different or to alter.
items.cn: 由它派生动词 variare，意为使不同、改变。

items.en: The adjective variabilis meant able to change, built with the suffix -bilis meaning capable.
items.cn: 形容词 variabilis 意为「能变化的」，由后缀 -bilis「能……的」构成。

items.en: Old French passed the word on with the same sense of being changeable.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词传下来，仍保留「会变的」意思。

items.en: In modern mathematics variable became a noun naming the symbol allowed to change.
items.cn: 在现代数学里，variable 变成名词，指允许变化的那个符号。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the vari- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for change and for what is fixed.
note.cn: 形近组沿 vari- 词干；近义组收表示变化以及固定不变的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, to change or differ.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」，是本词背后的动词。

entries.definition: Of several different kinds; the adjective of variety.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，属 variety 一支。

entries.definition: A range of different kinds of the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、品种」。

entries.definition: A change or difference in amount or form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化、变异」。

entries.definition: Able to change, plainer and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易变的」，更通俗不带术语味。

entries.definition: Likely to shift or fall; carries a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不稳定的」，带警示意味。

entries.definition: Staying the same; the natural opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「恒定的、常数」，天然的反义词。

entries.definition: Something that affects a result, whether it changes or not.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「因素」，不论变与不变。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the vari- root and real pairs such as variable cost and independent variable.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用 vari- 词根以及 variable cost、independent variable 这样的真实搭配。

normal.en: Vary is the verb, variable is the thing that can vary.
normal.cn: vary 是动词，variable 是那个会变的东西。

normal.en: In maths the variable is the letter, the constant is the number.
normal.cn: 数学里变量是字母，常数是数字。

normal.en: An independent variable is the one you change on purpose.
normal.cn: independent variable 是你故意去改的那个量。

normal.en: Variable costs rise and fall with how much you produce.
normal.cn: variable cost 随产量上下浮动。

normal.en: Add in- and invariable means the opposite: never changing.
normal.cn: 加上 in-，invariable 就是反面：从不改变。

abstract.en: A variable is a slot rather than a value: the name stays, the content keeps moving.
abstract.cn: 变量是一个槽位而不是一个数值：名字不动，内容一直换。

abstract.en: To call something variable is to say its future cannot be read off its present.
abstract.cn: 说某物「可变」，等于说它的未来无法从现状读出。

abstract.en: Every experiment is a bargain: hold most things still so that one thing may move.
abstract.cn: 每个实验都是一笔交易：让大多数东西不动，好让一样东西动起来。

examples.en: Researchers recorded each variable twice a day.
examples.cn: 研究人员每天记录每个变量两次。

examples.en: The results were affected by several variables beyond our control.
examples.cn: 结果受到了几个我们无法控制的可变因素影响。

examples.en: The quality of the soil is highly variable across the farm.
examples.cn: 这片农田的土质差异很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞额波」——威（风）瑞（气）额波一波波变来变去：变量

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 varius「斑驳的、多样的」及其动词 variare「改变」，经 variabilis 与古法语 variable 进入英语；同族词有 vary、various、variety、variation。

sensesIntro.en: Variable moves from a symbol in an equation, to a factor in a lab, to weather, temper and costs.
sensesIntro.cn: variable 从方程里的符号，走到实验室的因素，再到天气、脾气与成本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of liquid in a thermometer that will not stay at one mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计里的液柱不肯停在同一刻度上。

branches.en: MATHS LINE: the letter that may take any value.
branches.cn: 数学线：可以取任何值的字母。

branches.en: LAB LINE: the factor you watch or control.
branches.cn: 实验线：你观察或控制的因素。

branches.en: CHARACTER LINE: rainfall and tempers that shift.
branches.cn: 性质线：会变的雨量和脾气。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: costs that follow output.
branches.cn: 金钱线：随产量走的成本。

branches.en: CONTRAST: variable is the slot, constant is the fixed number.
branches.cn: 对照线：variable 是槽位，constant 是固定数。

intro.en: Variable is the Latin root vari- plus a suffix meaning capable, then an English-looking vowel.
intro.cn: variable 是拉丁词根 vari- 加上表示「能……的」后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is varius, variare and variabilis; all three are attested forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁链条是 varius、variare、variabilis，三者都是可考的实有形式。

items.example: It is the root of variable.

definition_zh: 变化；变动；差异；变体、变奏；变异
definition_en: a change in amount, level or form, or a different version of something
core_image: 同一首歌被唱了五遍，每一遍的音高都略有不同
scene: 气象站的记录本上，同一个月的降雨量每年都不一样。There is a wide variation in temperature between day and night in the desert.
sceneCN: 这里 variation 是「差异、变化幅度」（第 2 个义项：程度上的不同）；句意为沙漠里昼夜温差很大。同一首歌每遍音高略异，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：变化、变动、差异；变体、变奏；变异

collocations.zh: 主题变奏、略加改动的版本

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「变化、不同」，是本词的动词形式
名词或形容词，义为「变体、变种」
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」
名词，义为「可变性、波动幅度」
形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」

senses.title: The act of changing
senses.titleCN: 变化：某物在改变的过程
senses.definition: the act or process of changing
senses.definitionCN: 正在改变的动作或过程
senses.example: Careful measurement showed a slight variation in pressure overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细测量显示夜间气压有细微变化。
senses.why: Latin variare means to change, and -atio names the act; the word is the process itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为改变，-atio 命名这一行为；这个词就是过程本身。

senses.title: A difference in amount
senses.titleCN: 差异：程度上的不一样
senses.definition: a difference in amount, level or degree between things
senses.definitionCN: 事物之间在数量、水平或程度上的不同
senses.example: There is a wide variation in temperature between day and night in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠里昼夜温差很大。
senses.why: Once difference is measured, the word shifts from process to size: the amount of difference.
senses.whyCN: 差异一旦被测量，这个词就从过程变成幅度：差了多少。

senses.title: A changed version
senses.titleCN: 变体：稍加改动的版本
senses.definition: a thing that differs slightly from another of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类事物略有不同的版本
senses.example: The chef offered a vegetarian variation of the same dish.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师给同一道菜提供了素食版本。
senses.why: The same base appears in a new shape; the family resemblance stays visible.
senses.whyCN: 同一个底子换了一个形状出现，家族的相似仍然看得见。

senses.title: A musical form
senses.titleCN: 变奏：把一个主题反复改写
senses.definition: a repeated melody altered in rhythm, key or harmony
senses.definitionCN: 把一段旋律在节奏、调性或和声上反复改写
senses.example: The pianist played a set of variations on a folk tune.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家演奏了一组民谣主题变奏。
senses.why: Music makes the idea audible: one theme, many dresses.
senses.whyCN: 音乐让这个概念可以被听见：同一个主题，换很多件衣服。

senses.title: Biological difference
senses.titleCN: 变异：同种生物个体间的差别
senses.definition: differences between individuals of the same species, often inherited
senses.definitionCN: 同种生物个体之间的差别，常由遗传造成
senses.example: Genetic variation is what allows a population to adapt.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传变异使得一个种群能够适应环境。
senses.why: Living things copy themselves imperfectly, so each generation carries small differences that selection can use.
senses.whyCN: 生物复制自身时并不完美，于是每一代都带着细微差别，供自然选择使用。

intro.en: Variation is the Latin verb variare plus the noun ending -atio, a way of naming a process.
intro.cn: variation 是拉丁动词 variare 加名词词尾 -atio，用来给一个过程命名。

items.en: The verb variare meant to make different or to shift between forms.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为使不同，或在各形式之间变换。

items.en: The noun variatio named the act of changing, with the ending -atio for an action.
items.cn: 名词 variatio 指改变的行为，词尾 -atio 表示动作。

items.en: Old French passed on variacion, still meaning a change or difference.
items.cn: 古法语传下 variacion，仍指变化或差异。

items.en: English took variation in the fourteenth century for changes in weather, price and form.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 variation，用于天气、价格与形式的变化。

items.en: Modern usage adds music and biology, giving the word a technical life beside its everyday one.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了音乐与生物学，使这个词在日常生活之外又有了术语的生命。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group gathers words for difference and change.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示差异与变化的词。

entries.definition: The verb, to differ or change by degrees.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」，是它的动词形式。

entries.definition: A form that differs from the standard one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变体」，与标准形式不同。

entries.definition: A range of kinds, rather than one change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」，不是单次变化。

entries.definition: Something that is able to change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: The plain noun for becoming different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化」，最普通的说法。

entries.definition: Rising and falling again and again, like a level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「波动」，反复起落。

entries.definition: The gap between two things, without motion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「差别」，不含运动感。

entries.definition: One form of something that exists in several forms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本」，几个形式中的一个。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on the vari- family and on phrases like variation on a theme.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依靠 vari- 词族与 variation on a theme 这类搭配。

normal.en: Vary is the verb, variation is the change itself.
normal.cn: vary 是动词，variation 是变化本身。

normal.en: A variation on a theme is the same tune in new clothes.
normal.cn: variation on a theme 就是同一段旋律换了衣服。

normal.en: Genetic variation is why siblings are not identical.
normal.cn: 遗传变异是兄弟姐妹不完全相同的原因。

normal.en: Seasonal variation explains why prices move with the calendar.
normal.cn: 季节变化解释了价格为何跟着日历走。

normal.en: A wide variation means the numbers are far apart.
normal.cn: wide variation 指数字彼此差距很大。

abstract.en: Variation is difference with a memory: it tells you what the same thing looks like elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 变化是一种带记忆的差别：它告诉你同一事物在别处长什么样。

abstract.en: One process, several versions, many notes: the word carries all three without changing shape.
abstract.cn: 一个过程、几个版本、许多音符：这个词不变形就能承载三者。

abstract.en: Without variation there is no selection; difference is what time can work on.
abstract.cn: 没有差异就没有选择；时间能作用的正是差别。

examples.en: There is a wide variation in rainfall across the region.
examples.cn: 这个地区的降雨量差异很大。

examples.en: The design is a variation on a chair she made last year.
examples.cn: 这个设计是她去年做的一把椅子的变体。

examples.en: Small variations in temperature can change the result.
examples.cn: 温度的细微变化就可能改变结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞一起」——威（风）瑞（雨）一起变，变化就来了：变化

root: 源自拉丁语动词 variare「改变」的名词形式 variatio，经古法语进入英语；同族词有 vary、variant、variety、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Variation covers a process, a measured gap, a new version, a piece of music and a fact of biology.
sensesIntro.cn: variation 涵盖一个过程、一个测得的差距、一个新版本、一段音乐和一条生物学事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same tune sung five times, each time a little different.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一首歌被唱了五遍，每遍都略有不同。

branches.en: PROCESS LINE: change happening over time.
branches.cn: 过程线：随时间发生的变化。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: how far the values sit apart.
branches.cn: 幅度线：数值之间差多少。

branches.en: FORM LINE: the same thing in a new dress.
branches.cn: 形式线：同一样东西换的新装。

branches.en: LIFE LINE: inherited differences in a species.
branches.cn: 生命线：种群中可遗传的差别。

branches.en: CONTRAST: variation is measured, difference is simply noticed.
branches.cn: 对照线：variation 要被测量，difference 只需被察觉。

intro.en: Variation is a root plus an action-noun ending; the whole vari- family shares that stem.
intro.cn: variation 是词根加表动作的名词词尾，整个 vari- 家族共用这个词干。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are variare, to change, and -atio, the action noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁构件是 variare「改变」和表示动作名词的 -atio。

items.example: It shows the word in use.

definition_zh: 多样性、变化；种类、品种；（同一类的）若干不同事物；综艺节目
definition_en: a range of different kinds of the same thing, or one particular kind
core_image: 一个装满各色水果的篮子，每一样都不同，却都属于水果
scene: 菜市场的摊位上摆着十几种番茄，大小颜色各不相同。The shop sells a wide variety of teas from the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里 variety 是「种类」（第 2 个义项：某一类中的一种）；句意为这家店出售山上产的各种茶叶。满篮各色果实互不相同的样子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：多样性、变化；种类、品种；综艺节目

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，是本词的形容词形式
动词，义为「变化、不同」
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」
名词，义为「变体、变种」
形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」

senses.title: A range of kinds
senses.titleCN: 多样性：许多不同种类的集合
senses.definition: many different kinds of the same general thing
senses.definitionCN: 同一大类下许多不同的种类
senses.example: The market offers a wide variety of fruit in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天市场上水果种类很多。
senses.why: Latin varius means spotted or mixed; variety is the pattern of many kinds together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的；variety 就是多种东西并置的图案。

senses.title: One kind among many
senses.titleCN: 种类：其中的某一个品种
senses.definition: a particular kind within a larger group, often a plant or product
senses.definitionCN: 较大类别中的某一具体种类，常指植物或产品
senses.example: The shop sells a wide variety of teas from the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售山上产的各种茶叶。
senses.why: The collective word narrows to a single item: this variety here, not the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合名词收窄为单个个体：是这一个品种，不是全部。

senses.title: Lack of sameness
senses.titleCN: 不单调：避免千篇一律
senses.definition: the quality of not being all the same, valued as interest
senses.definitionCN: 不一模一样的性质，被视为有趣可贵
senses.example: A little variety in the menu keeps the children interested.
senses.exampleCN: 菜单上有点变化能让孩子们保持兴趣。
senses.why: Here the word judges rather than lists: sameness is dull, variety is good.
senses.whyCN: 这里的这个词在做评价而不是在列举：单调乏味，多样才好。

senses.title: A music hall show
senses.titleCN: 综艺：由多种节目拼成的演出
senses.definition: a show of separate acts such as singing, dance and comedy
senses.definitionCN: 由歌唱、舞蹈、滑稽戏等独立节目拼成的演出
senses.example: The theatre still puts on a variety show every winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院每到冬天仍上演综艺节目。
senses.why: A show of many acts is variety made visible: one stage, many kinds.
senses.whyCN: 多种节目同台就是可见的多样性：一个舞台，许多门类。

senses.title: A biological subspecies
senses.titleCN: 生物变种：人工培育或自然分化的品种
senses.definition: a group of plants or animals differing slightly from the species, such as a cultivated breed
senses.definitionCN: 与物种略有差异的动植物群体，如栽培品种
senses.example: This variety of apple ripens earlier than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 这个苹果品种比其他的成熟得早。
senses.why: Growers keep a stable set of traits and give it a name, and that named set is the variety.
senses.whyCN: 栽培者把一组稳定性状固定下来并给它命名，这个被命名的群体就是品种。

intro.en: Variety comes from Latin varietas through French, built on varius, meaning spotted or of many colours.
intro.cn: variety 经由法语来自拉丁语 varietas，词根 varius 意为斑驳的、多色的。

items.en: The adjective varius described skins, stones or animals marked with several colours.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述带多色斑纹的皮、石头或动物。

items.en: The noun varietas named diversity and difference, with the ending -tas for a state.
items.cn: 名词 varietas 指多样与差异，词尾 -tas 表示状态。

items.en: French carried variété into everyday use for the many kinds of a thing.
items.cn: 法语把 variété 带入日常使用，表示同一事物的许多种类。

items.en: English borrowed variety in the sixteenth century, first for diversity, then for a kind.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 variety，先表多样性，后表某一品种。

items.en: In the nineteenth century variety halls gave the word its show business sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪的杂耍剧院给了这个词演艺行业的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds words for range and for a single kind.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示范围与单一品种的词。

entries.definition: Of several kinds; the adjective of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同词干的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb, to differ or change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」。

entries.definition: A change or a changed version.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化、变体」。

entries.definition: Something that changes; the technical cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」，技术性的近亲。

entries.definition: Difference among things, often used of people and species.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性」，常用于人群与物种。

entries.definition: The spread from one end to the other of a set.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「范围」，一套东西从头到尾的跨度。

entries.definition: A group of different things to choose from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可供挑选的一组」，强调可挑选。

entries.definition: One kind of animal kept by people, closer to a single variety.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「品种」，更接近单个品种。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the basket-of-fruit core and phrases like a wide variety of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「一篮果子」的意象与 a wide variety of 这类搭配。

normal.en: A variety of teas means many different teas, not one.
normal.cn: a variety of teas 指许多不同的茶，不是一种。

normal.en: Variety is the opposite of sameness in food, music and life.
normal.cn: variety 在食物、音乐和生活中都是「单调」的反面。

normal.en: A new variety of rice may ripen earlier than the old one.
normal.cn: 一个新稻种可能比旧的成熟得早。

normal.en: A variety show strings separate acts onto one stage.
normal.cn: variety show 把各种独立节目串在一个舞台上。

normal.en: Add variety to a routine and the routine stops feeling like a routine.
normal.cn: 给日常加点变化，日常就不再像日常。

abstract.en: The word holds both the whole and one piece of it: a variety of things, and the variety you picked.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装下整体与一片：诸多种类，以及你选中的那一种。

abstract.en: Diversity is a pattern, not a list: it needs to be seen from above.
abstract.cn: 多样性是一种图案而非清单：它需要从上方看才成形。

abstract.en: Sameness repeats, variety remembers: a varied diet and a varied life both stay alive longer.
abstract.cn: 单调只是重复，多样带着记忆：多样的饮食与多样的生活都活得更久。

examples.en: The library offers a variety of books for young readers.
examples.cn: 这家图书馆为小读者提供各种图书。

examples.en: We stayed at home for a variety of reasons.
examples.cn: 我们待在家里，原因有好几种。

examples.en: This variety of tomato grows well in cool weather.
examples.cn: 这个番茄品种在凉爽天气里长得很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我瑞爱提」——我瑞（锐）意爱提各种花样：多样性

root: 源自拉丁语名词 varietas（词根 varius「斑驳的、多样的」），经法语 variété 于十六世纪进入英语；同族词有 various、vary、variation、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Variety can mean many kinds together, one kind by itself, the pleasure of change, a stage show or a plant breed.
sensesIntro.cn: variety 可以指多种并存、单一品种、变化带来的趣味、综艺演出或植物品种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of fruit where every piece is a different kind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只篮子，里面每个果子都是不同种类。

branches.en: SET LINE: many kinds seen together.
branches.cn: 集合线：许多种类放在一起看。

branches.en: ITEM LINE: one particular breed or kind.
branches.cn: 个体线：某一个具体品种。

branches.en: PLEASURE LINE: change that keeps things interesting.
branches.cn: 趣味线：让人保持新鲜的变化。

branches.en: STAGE LINE: many acts in one show.
branches.cn: 舞台线：一场演出里许多节目。

branches.en: CONTRAST: variety is the whole basket, a kind is one fruit.
branches.cn: 对照线：variety 是整篮，a kind 是一个果子。

intro.en: Variety is a Latin state noun; its family supplies the adjective, verb and technical forms.
intro.cn: variety 是拉丁语状态名词，它的家族还提供形容词、动词与技术形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are varius, varietas and the adjective varius giving various.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁构件是 varius、varietas，而 various 直接来自 varius。

definition_zh: 各种各样的；不同的、好几个的；多方面的
definition_en: of several different kinds or several different people or things
core_image: 一排货架上摆着颜色形状各不相同的盒子，标签却写着同一类商品
scene: 聚会结束后，桌上留下了各色各样的杯子，高矮粗细都不相同。Various guests arrived through the evening, each with a different story.
sceneCN: 这里 various 是「各种各样的」（第 1 个义项：种类不止一种）；句意为整晚陆续来了各种各样的客人，每人都有不同的故事。一排彼此不同的盒子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：各种各样的；不同的、好几个的；多方面的

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「以各种方式、不同地」
名词，义为「多样性、种类」，是本词的名词形式
动词，义为「变化、不同」
名词，义为「多样性」，较少使用
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」

senses.title: Of several kinds
senses.titleCN: 各种各样的：种类不止一个
senses.definition: of more than one kind, used before a plural noun
senses.definitionCN: 不止一种，用在复数名词前
senses.example: Various guests arrived through the evening, each with a different story.
senses.exampleCN: 整晚陆续来了各种各样的客人，每人都有不同的故事。
senses.why: Latin varius means spotted or mixed; various names a set whose members do not match.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的；various 指成员彼此不一致的一组。

senses.title: Several and different
senses.titleCN: 好几个不同的：数量不定但都算在内
senses.definition: several different people or things, not exactly numbered
senses.definitionCN: 几个不同的人或物，数量不确切
senses.example: We met at various times during the year.
senses.exampleCN: 我们这一年里在不同时间见过几次。
senses.why: The word avoids giving a number; it counts only as far as several and no further.
senses.whyCN: 这个词回避给出具体数目：只数到「好几个」为止。

senses.title: From many sides
senses.titleCN: 多方面的：原因、来源各不相同
senses.definition: coming from many different sources or aspects
senses.definitionCN: 来自许多不同来源或方面
senses.example: The delay was due to various reasons, some of them personal.
senses.exampleCN: 延误有种种原因，其中一些是私人的。
senses.why: Each member of the set has its own origin; the word holds them side by side.
senses.whyCN: 这一组的每个成员各有来源，这个词把它们并排放着。

senses.title: Many-sided in skill
senses.titleCN: 多样化的：本事不止一样（较少用）
senses.definition: having many different abilities or forms, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 具有多种才能或形态，较旧的文学用法
senses.example: He is a various man, at home in both music and mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个多才之人，音乐和数学都能应付。
senses.why: The older sense applies the diversity to a single person, not to a group.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的含义把多样性用在一个人身上，而不是一群人身上。

intro.en: Various is the English form of Latin varius, spotted or mixed, with an adjective ending added on the way.
intro.cn: various 是拉丁语 varius「斑驳的、混杂的」在英语里的形态，途中加上了形容词词尾。

items.en: The adjective varius described things of mixed colour, uneven or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述颜色混杂、不齐整或多种多样的事物。

items.en: Its plural varii was used for several different people, close to the modern sense.
items.cn: 其复数 varii 用于指若干不同的人，很接近现代含义。

items.en: English formed various from the Latin stem, first meaning changeable or diverse.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词干造出 various，最初意为易变的或多样的。

items.en: Modern usage settles it before plural nouns, meaning several different.
items.cn: 现代用法把它固定在复数名词前，表示好几个不同的。

items.en: The word now shares its family with variety, variable and vary, all from the same Latin stem.
items.cn: 它如今与 variety、variable、vary 共用一个家族，全部出自同一拉丁词干。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds quantifiers for a loose plurality.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示不确切多数的限定词。

entries.definition: The noun for many kinds or one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」。

entries.definition: The verb, to differ or change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」。

entries.definition: Made varied, not all alike; close to various in sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，意义接近 various。

entries.definition: Able to change, or a symbol that varies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: More than two but not many, without the sense of unlike.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「几个」，不强调彼此不同。

entries.definition: Not the same as one another, the core of various.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不同的」，是 various 的核心义。

entries.definition: Of mixed kinds put together, often in a box or pack.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「什锦的、搭配好的」。

entries.definition: Many in number, with no emphasis on variety.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「众多的」，不强调种类。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the prefix habit of various and real collocations such as for various reasons.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用 various 只修饰复数的习惯，以及 for various reasons 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Various always sits before a plural noun: various reasons, never various reason.
normal.cn: various 总在复数名词前：various reasons，不能接单数。

normal.en: Various means more than one, but it refuses to say how many.
normal.cn: various 表示不止一个，却不肯说有几个。

normal.en: For various reasons is a polite way to avoid listing the reasons.
normal.cn: for various reasons 是避免一一列举的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Varied describes a thing, various describes a group of things.
normal.cn: varied 形容一样东西，various 形容一组东西。

normal.en: The same root gives variety, vary and variable.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还给出 variety、vary 与 variable。

abstract.en: Various is a quiet way of saying that a group refuses to be summed up in one word.
abstract.cn: various 是一个低调的说法：这一组无法用一个词概括。

abstract.en: The word is plural by nature; it draws its meaning from the gaps between members.
abstract.cn: 这个词天生带复数性：它的意思来自成员之间的差异。

abstract.en: Say various and you admit you have not checked everything, only that the pieces differ.
abstract.cn: 说 various 就等于承认你并未逐一核对，只确认了它们互不相同。

examples.en: Various people offered to help with the move.
examples.cn: 有好几个人主动提出帮忙搬家。

examples.en: The delay was caused by various problems with the engine.
examples.cn: 延误差是由发动机的种种问题造成的。

examples.en: Books on the subject are available in various languages.
examples.cn: 这个主题的书有各种语言的版本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我瑞爱死」——各式各样的东西我瑞（锐）意爱死：各种各样的

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 varius「斑驳的、多种的」，经英语自造词 various 进入使用；同族词有 variety、vary、variation、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Various ranges from many kinds before a plural noun, to an unnumbered several, many sources, and an older sense of many-sided.
sensesIntro.cn: various 从复数名词前的「多种」，到不确切的好几个、多来源，以及较旧的「多才」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf of boxes, same category, every shape and colour different.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排货架上的盒子同属一类，却个个形状颜色不同。

branches.en: KIND LINE: the members are not alike.
branches.cn: 种类线：成员彼此并不相同。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: several, with no exact number.
branches.cn: 计数线：好几个，不给具体数字。

branches.en: ORIGIN LINE: causes and sources differ.
branches.cn: 来源线：原因与出处各异。

branches.en: ABILITY LINE: one person with many sides.
branches.cn: 才能线：一个人有多面。

branches.en: CONTRAST: various refuses both one word and a fixed number.
branches.cn: 对照线：various 既不肯概括，也不肯给数。

intro.en: Various is a Latin stem with an English adjective ending; the whole vari- family shares the stem.
intro.cn: various 是拉丁词干加英语形容词词尾，整个 vari- 家族共用该词干。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is varius; the plural varii already meant several different people.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 varius，其复数 varii 已经表示「若干不同的人」。

definition_zh: 变化；变动；使不同；各不相同；（随情况）改变
definition_en: to change, or to differ from one another
core_image: 同一把尺子量十个人，每量一次读数都不一样
scene: 山脚下是春天的花，爬到半山就只见残雪，山顶则冻得人发抖。Prices vary from shop to shop along the same street.
sceneCN: 这里 vary 是「各不相同、有差异」（第 2 个义项：彼此不同）；句意为同一条街上各家店铺的价格各不相同。尺子每次读数都不一样，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：变化、变动；使不同；各不相同

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」
形容词，义为「各种各样的」
形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」
名词，义为「变化、差异」
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」

senses.title: To change over time
senses.titleCN: 变化：随时间而改变
senses.definition: to change in amount, level or form over time
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、水平或形式上随时间改变
senses.example: The water level varies with the season.
senses.exampleCN: 水位随季节变化。
senses.why: Latin variare means to make different; the verb follows whatever the changing thing does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为使不同；这个动词跟着变化者一起走。

senses.title: To differ from one another
senses.titleCN: 各不相同：彼此有差别
senses.definition: to be different between individual cases
senses.definitionCN: 在各个个体之间有所不同
senses.example: Prices vary from shop to shop along the same street.
senses.exampleCN: 同一条街上各家店铺的价格各不相同。
senses.why: Here nothing changes over time; the differences exist side by side in one moment.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有随时间而变化，差别在同一时刻并排存在。

senses.title: To change deliberately
senses.titleCN: 主动改变：故意换个做法
senses.definition: to make something different on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意使某物不同
senses.example: He never varies his route to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他上班路线从不改变。
senses.why: The subject is a person here, and the change is a choice rather than a natural drift.
senses.whyCN: 这里的主语是人，变化是一种选择而不是自然漂移。

senses.title: To depend on something
senses.titleCN: 随……而变：跟着另一个因素走
senses.definition: to change according to another factor
senses.definitionCN: 随另一个因素改变
senses.example: Crop yields vary according to rainfall and soil.
senses.exampleCN: 作物产量随降雨与土壤而变化。
senses.why: The verb leaves the subject to someone else: yields follow the rain, and the rain decides.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把主导权交给别人：产量跟着雨水走，由雨水决定。

intro.en: Vary is the direct Latin verb variare, to make different, taken into English without an ending change.
intro.cn: vary 就是拉丁语动词 variare「使不同」几乎原样进入英语。

items.en: The adjective varius meant spotted, mixed or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的、多种多样的。

items.en: The verb variare meant to make different, to alternate or to diversify.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为使不同、交替变换、使多样化。

items.en: Old French variier softened the Latin verb and gave it a French shape.
items.cn: 古法语 variier 让拉丁动词软化，并赋予它法语形态。

items.en: English shortened it to vary in the fourteenth century, meaning to undergo change.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把它缩短为 vary，意为经历变化。

items.en: Modern English uses it both for changing and for differing, two sides of one Latin idea.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它表「变化」也表「不同」，这是同一个拉丁观念的两面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of shifting and differing.
note.cn: 形近组沿 vari- 家族；近义组收表示变化与不同的动词。

entries.definition: Of many kinds, the adjective of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同词干。

entries.definition: Many kinds or one kind; the noun of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」，同词干。

entries.definition: Something that changes, or a symbol for it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: A change or difference in amount or form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化、差异」。

entries.definition: The plain verb for becoming different.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改变」，最普通。

entries.definition: To be unlike, only the side of comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不同」，只表示比较的一面。

entries.definition: To rise and fall again and again, like a level.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「波动」，反复起落。

entries.definition: To move from one position or state to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「转移」，从一个位置或状态移到另一个。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the two faces of vary, changing and differing, with real phrases from news and shops.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用 vary 变化与不同这两面，搭配取自新闻与店铺的真实说法。

normal.en: Vary with time, differ from place to place: one word for both.
normal.cn: 随时间变叫 vary，各地不同也叫 vary：一个词两面用。

normal.en: Prices vary widely means the range is large.
normal.cn: prices vary widely 指差价范围很大。

normal.en: Vary in size means the sizes are not all the same.
normal.cn: vary in size 指大小并不一样。

normal.en: Opinions vary is a polite way of saying nobody agrees.
normal.cn: opinions vary 是「谁都不一致」的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Varied is the adjective, variety the noun, varying the participle.
normal.cn: varied 是形容词，variety 是名词，varying 是分词。

abstract.en: Vary needs two reference points: a thing at two times, or two things at one time.
abstract.cn: vary 需要两个参照点：一样东西的两个时刻，或同一时刻的两样东西。

abstract.en: Change is motion, difference is structure; vary describes both with one shape.
abstract.cn: 变化是运动，差异是结构；vary 用一个形状描述两者。

abstract.en: A life without vary is a line, not a landscape.
abstract.cn: 没有变化的生活是一条线，不是一片风景。

examples.en: Prices vary widely between the two markets.
examples.cn: 两个市场的价格差别很大。

examples.en: Her mood varies with the weather.
examples.cn: 她的心情随天气变化。

examples.en: The recipes vary only in the amount of sugar used.
examples.cn: 这些食谱只是在用糖量上不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞」——威（风）瑞（雨）一来，天气就变：变化

root: 直接来自拉丁语动词 variare「使不同、变换」，经古法语 variier 于十四世纪进入英语；同族词有 various、variety、variable、variation。

sensesIntro.en: Vary covers change over time, difference between cases, deliberate change and dependence on a factor.
sensesIntro.cn: vary 涵盖随时间变化、个体间差异、主动改变与随因素而变四种情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ruler measuring ten people, with ten different readings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子量十个人，十次读数都不同。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the same thing is different later.
branches.cn: 时间线：同一样东西后来不同了。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: different cases at one moment.
branches.cn: 空间线：同一时刻的各个个体不同。

branches.en: WILL LINE: a person chooses to change.
branches.cn: 意志线：人主动选择改变。

branches.en: CAUSE LINE: one factor pulls another along.
branches.cn: 因果线：一个因素带着另一个走。

branches.en: CONTRAST: change is one thing twice, vary also covers two things once.
branches.cn: 对照线：变化是一样东西的两次，vary 也含两样东西的一次。

intro.en: Vary is a bare Latin verb stem; its English relatives come from adding endings to the same root.
intro.cn: vary 是不带前缀的拉丁动词词干，英语亲属词都在同一词根上加词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is variare from varius; the English verb drops the ending entirely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是出自 varius 的 variare，英语动词整个去掉了词尾。

items.example: It forms varied and the past tense.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 varied 与过去式。

items.example: It is shared by the whole family.

definition_zh: 巨大的；广阔的；浩瀚的；大量的、极多的
definition_en: extremely large in area, amount or degree
core_image: 站在沙丘顶端望出去，地平线一直退到眼睛看不见的地方
scene: 夜里没有一盏灯，抬头只看见铺满星星的天。A vast plain stretched away in every direction.
sceneCN: 这里 vast 是「广阔的、浩瀚的」（第 1 个义项：面积极大）；句意为一片广阔的平原向四面八方伸展开去。地平线退到看不见的地方，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：巨大的、广阔的、浩瀚的；大量的

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「极大地、远远地」，如 vastly improved
名词，义为「广阔、浩瀚」
名词，书面说法，义为「广袤」，较少使用

senses.title: Enormous in area
senses.titleCN: 面积巨大：眼睛望不到边
senses.definition: extremely large in area or extent
senses.definitionCN: 面积或范围极大
senses.example: A vast plain stretched away in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 一片广阔的平原向四面八方伸展开去。
senses.why: Latin vastus meant empty and desolate; the emptiness itself is what takes the breath away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vastus 意为空旷荒芜；正是这种空旷让人屏息。

senses.title: Enormous in amount
senses.titleCN: 数量巨大：多到难以清点
senses.definition: extremely large in number or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 数量或数目极大
senses.example: A vast amount of data was collected over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间收集了海量的数据。
senses.why: The word moves from space to quantity: numbers can also open out like a plain.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从空间移到数量：数字也能像平原一样铺开。

senses.title: Great in degree
senses.titleCN: 程度巨大：差别或优势悬殊
senses.definition: very great in degree, used of differences and advantages
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上非常大，用于差别与优势
senses.example: There is a vast difference between the two plans.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案之间差别巨大。
senses.why: Here the size is abstract: not metres but distance in quality or outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里的大小是抽象的：量的是质量或结果上的距离，而非米数。

senses.title: The great majority
senses.titleCN: 绝大多数：人群中的绝大部分
senses.definition: used with majority to mean almost all
senses.definitionCN: 与 majority 连用，表示几乎全部
senses.example: The vast majority of students passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 绝大多数学生通过了考试。
senses.why: A crowd can be vast too; the same word measures people.
senses.whyCN: 人群也可以是 vast；同一个词也能量人。

intro.en: Vast comes from Latin vastus, empty and desolate, which already described land that stretched out bare.
intro.cn: vast 来自拉丁语 vastus「空旷荒芜的」，本已形容光秃秃铺展开的土地。

items.en: The adjective vastus meant empty, waste or desolate, applied to ruined land.
items.cn: 形容词 vastus 意为空旷的、荒废的、荒凉的，用于被毁坏的土地。

items.en: Its verb vastare meant to lay waste, and lies behind English waste and devastate.
items.cn: 其动词 vastare 意为摧残荒废，是英语 waste 与 devastate 的来源。

items.en: Old French vaste kept the sense of wide and unoccupied space.
items.cn: 古法语 vaste 保留了辽阔空旷的意思。

items.en: English borrowed vast in the fifteenth century for enormous extent.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 vast，表示范围极大。

items.en: Modern usage extends it from land to amounts and differences, while the sense of emptiness fades.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从土地扩展到数量与差别，同时「空旷」的感觉渐渐淡去。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of waste and emptiness; the near-meaning group holds words for great size.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「荒废、空」的拉丁词干；近义组收表示巨大的词。

entries.definition: By a very large amount; the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「极大地」，是本词的副词形式。

entries.definition: The quality of being vast; the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广阔」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: To lay waste or ruin; uses the Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毁坏」，出自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Empty or unused land; a distant English cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「荒地、浪费」，英语里的远亲。

entries.definition: Very large in size, plainer and more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，更日常。

entries.definition: So large it cannot be measured; close in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边的」，语气接近。

entries.definition: Larger than normal, with a hint of shock.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「庞大的」，带惊奇感。

entries.definition: Having no limits, stressing no edge rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边无际的」，强调没有边界。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the empty-plain core and real collocations like vast majority.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「空旷平原」意象与 vast majority 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Vast majority means almost all, not merely most.
normal.cn: vast majority 指几乎全部，不只是大多数。

normal.en: Vast came from a Latin word for empty land.
normal.cn: vast 来自拉丁语中表示空地的词。

normal.en: Vast difference is a huge gap, not a big object.
normal.cn: vast difference 指巨大差距，不是巨大物件。

normal.en: Vaster and vastest exist, though writers often use more vast.
normal.cn: vaster 与 vastest 存在，但作家常用 more vast。

normal.en: Vastly improved means improved by a very large amount.
normal.cn: vastly improved 指改善幅度极大。

abstract.en: Vast began as emptiness and became size: the feeling of distance is older than the measure of it.
abstract.cn: vast 从「空」长成「大」：对距离的感受比测量更古老。

abstract.en: Something vast makes the viewer small, which is why the word always carries a trace of awe.
abstract.cn: 巨大之物让人显小，所以这个词总带一丝敬畏。

abstract.en: The same word measures land, data and differences, because largeness is a comparison, not a substance.
abstract.cn: 同一个词量土地、数据与差别，因为「大」是比较，不是实体。

examples.en: Vast areas of the country remain uninhabited.
examples.cn: 这个国家的大片地区仍无人居住。

examples.en: She spent a vast amount of time on the research.
examples.cn: 她在这项研究上花了大量时间。

examples.en: The vast majority of customers were satisfied.
examples.cn: 绝大多数顾客表示满意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇死他」——哇，他一个人管那么大一片地：广阔的

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 vastus「空旷荒芜的」及其动词 vastare「荒废」，经古法语 vaste 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 devastate、waste。

sensesIntro.en: Vast starts with land that has no edge, then measures quantities, differences and the bulk of a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: vast 从望不到边的土地开始，然后用来量数量、差别与人群的绝大部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horizon that keeps moving back as you look at it.
core.cn: 核心意象：你越看，那条地平线退得越远。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: land and water without visible edge.
branches.cn: 空间线：看不见边际的陆地与水面。

branches.en: QUANTITY LINE: numbers or data in huge bulk.
branches.cn: 数量线：成堆的数字与数据。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: a gap that feels like distance.
branches.cn: 程度线：像距离一样的悬殊。

branches.en: CROWD LINE: nearly all the people counted.
branches.cn: 人群线：被计数的人几乎全部。

branches.en: CONTRAST: huge is a size, vast is a stretch.
branches.cn: 对照线：huge 指尺寸，vast 指铺展。

intro.en: Vast is a whole Latin stem; its English relatives take -ly and -ness, while devastate keeps the Latin verb.
intro.cn: vast 是完整的拉丁词干，英语亲属词接 -ly 与 -ness，而 devastate 保留拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pair is the adjective vastus and the verb vastare, both about emptiness and ruin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的一对是形容词 vastus 与动词 vastare，都与空旷和毁坏有关。

items.example: It shows the old root in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语里展示这个老词根。

definition_zh: 蔬菜；植物（总称，较旧用法）；形容词：植物的、蔬菜的；植物人（口语，多用于 be a vegetable）
definition_en: a plant or part of a plant eaten as food, such as a carrot or cabbage
core_image: 菜篮里横着一根带泥的胡萝卜，叶子还挂着水珠
scene: 厨房案板上摊着刚洗好的青菜、辣椒和番茄，水还在滴。She grows most of her own vegetables in a small garden.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetable 是「蔬菜」（第 1 个义项：可食用的植物或其部分）；句意为她大部分的蔬菜都种在自己的小园子里。菜篮里那根带泥的胡萝卜，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：蔬菜；植物（总称）
形容词：蔬菜的、植物的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「素食者」，由本词加 -arian 构成
名词，义为「植被、草木」，同源于拉丁语 vegetare「生长」
动词，义为「生长；无所事事地过日子」
形容词，义为「植物的」，较书面

senses.title: Food from plants
senses.titleCN: 蔬菜：可吃的植物或其部分
senses.definition: a plant or part of a plant used as food, such as cabbage or carrot
senses.definitionCN: 可食用的植物或其部分，如甘蓝、胡萝卜
senses.example: She grows most of her own vegetables in a small garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她大部分的蔬菜都种在自己的小园子里。
senses.why: Latin vegetare means to grow; a vegetable is simply the part of a growing plant that reaches the table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vegetare 意为生长；蔬菜就是生长中的植物里走上餐桌的那一部分。

senses.title: Plants in general
senses.titleCN: 植物：较旧的总称，常带科学色彩
senses.definition: a plant or plant life in general, in older or scientific writing
senses.definitionCN: 笼统指植物，见于较早或科学性的文字
senses.example: The museum has a large collection of fossils of ancient vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏了大量古代植物的化石。
senses.why: The older sense covers the whole kingdom; the kitchen sense pulled one part of it away.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的含义覆盖整个界，厨房用法把其中一部分拽了出来。

senses.title: Of plants
senses.titleCN: 植物的：作定语说明来源
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean made from or of plants
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示由植物制成或与植物有关
senses.example: The soup was cooked in vegetable oil rather than butter.
senses.exampleCN: 汤是用植物油而不是黄油煮的。
senses.why: As a modifier the word labels a source, not a kind of plant.
senses.whyCN: 作修饰语时，这个词标的是来源，而不是某种植物。

senses.title: A person without response
senses.titleCN: 植物人：口语里形容毫无反应的人
senses.definition: in informal medical talk, a person alive but unable to respond or move
senses.definitionCN: 口语医疗说法，指活着却无法回应或活动的人
senses.example: He was no longer ill, but he lay as a vegetable for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病已不是问题，却像植物人一样躺了多年。
senses.why: The metaphor is blunt: only growth remains, all communication gone.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很直接：只剩生长，一切交流都消失了。

intro.en: Vegetable comes from Latin vegetabilis, able to grow, from the verb vegetare, to be lively.
intro.cn: vegetable 来自拉丁语 vegetabilis「能生长的」，出自动词 vegetare「有生气、生长」。

items.en: The verb vegere meant to be active or lively, applied to anything growing and powered.
items.cn: 动词 vegere 意为有活力、活跃，用于正在生长、有生机的东西。

items.en: Its frequentative vegetare meant to animate or make grow, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 其反复态 vegetare 意为使有生气、使生长，是整个词族的根。

items.en: The adjective vegetabilis meant capable of growth, applied to plants and soil.
items.cn: 形容词 vegetabilis 意为能生长的，用于植物与土壤。

items.en: Old French used vegetable for anything that grew, and English borrowed it in that sense.
items.cn: 古法语用 vegetable 指一切会生长之物，英语即以此义借入。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the kitchen sense had pushed the general one aside in daily speech.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，厨房里的用法在日常语言中把笼统的含义挤到了一边。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the grow- family; the near-meaning group holds plant foods and words for plants.
note.cn: 形近组沿「生长」词族；近义组收植物性食物与泛指植物的词。

entries.definition: A person who avoids meat; built on vegetable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「素食者」，由本词构成。
