entries.definition: Plant life as a whole, the old general sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「植被」，即较旧的笼统含义。

entries.definition: To grow as a plant, or to live without activity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「生长」，也指无所事事地活着。

entries.definition: A learned adjective for plant life.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「植物的」，书面色彩。

entries.definition: One common vegetable, with its own round picture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卷心菜」，单一蔬菜，画面自成一格。

entries.definition: The seed-bearing part, a kitchen partner and rival.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水果」，含籽的部分，厨房里的伙伴与对手。

entries.definition: Farm products sold together, fruit and vegetables at once.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农产品」，把果蔬一起算。

entries.definition: Plants grown for harvest, seen as a field or yield.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「作物」，从田野与产量的角度看。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the growing-plant root and the kitchen sense that now dominates.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「生长植物」的词根，以及如今占主导的厨房含义。

normal.en: Vegetable comes from a Latin verb meaning to grow.
normal.cn: vegetable 出自一个意为「生长」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Vegetables are eaten; a vegetarian eats no meat.
normal.cn: 蔬菜是吃的，而 vegetarian 是不吃肉的人。

normal.en: Vegetation is the old, wide sense: all of the plants.
normal.cn: vegetation 是旧的宽泛指：所有植物。

normal.en: Vegetable oil is oil pressed from plants, not from butter.
normal.cn: vegetable oil 是从植物压榨的油，不是黄油。

normal.en: A vegetable garden grows food, a flower garden grows beauty.
normal.cn: 菜园种食物，花园种美。

abstract.en: The word once meant anything that grows, and now means what we pick and cook.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指一切会生长之物，如今指我们采摘下锅的东西。

abstract.en: It marks a boundary humans drew, not one nature keeps: tomato is a fruit in botany and a vegetable in the kitchen.
abstract.cn: 它标的是人划的界线而非自然的：番茄在植物学是果实，在厨房是蔬菜。

abstract.en: From life to food to mere survival, the same root covers growth, harvest and the loss of speech.
abstract.cn: 从生命到食物再到只剩生存，同一个词根覆盖成长、收获与失语。

examples.en: Eat more fresh vegetables and less fried food.
examples.cn: 多吃新鲜蔬菜，少吃油炸食物。

examples.en: They planted vegetables behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们在屋后种了蔬菜。

examples.en: The dish is cooked with vegetable oil and garlic.
examples.cn: 这道菜用植物油和大蒜烹制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威治特波」——威（为）治特（吃）吧，多吃蔬菜：蔬菜

root: 源自拉丁语 vegetabilis「能生长的」，出自 vegetare「使生长」，经古法语 vegetable 进入英语；同族词有 vegetarian、vegetation、vegetate。

sensesIntro.en: Vegetable moves from the whole plant kingdom to the kitchen, then to a modifier and an old blunt figure of speech.
sensesIntro.cn: vegetable 从整个植物界走进厨房，再成为修饰语，最后化作一句直白的旧比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a muddy carrot from the garden, leaves still beaded with water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根带泥的胡萝卜，叶子还挂着水珠。

branches.en: KITCHEN LINE: the edible part of a plant.
branches.cn: 厨房线：植物可食的部分。

branches.en: BOTANY LINE: the whole plant world, an older use.
branches.cn: 植物学线：整个植物界，较旧用法。

branches.en: LABEL LINE: vegetable oil names a source.
branches.cn: 标签线：vegetable oil 标的是来源。

branches.en: LOSS LINE: life without response, a blunt metaphor.
branches.cn: 丧失线：只剩生命而无反应，直白比喻。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a vegetable is food, vegetable oil is a material.
branches.cn: 对照线：vegetable 是食物，vegetable oil 是原料。

intro.en: Vegetable keeps its Latin adjective ending; English relatives use -arian, -ation and -ate.
intro.cn: vegetable 保留了拉丁形容词词尾，英语亲属词则用 -arian、-ation、-ate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is vegere, vegetare and vegetabilis, all about life and growth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁链条是 vegere、vegetare、vegetabilis，都与生命和生长有关。

items.example: It shows the word as a modifier.

definition_zh: 车辆；交通工具；（思想、信息的）传播媒介、手段；载体
definition_en: a machine with wheels or an engine used for transport, or a means of expressing something
core_image: 一辆车停在站台边，门一开，车上的人和想法一起下车
scene: 早高峰的马路上一排车缓缓挪动，尾灯连成一条红线。No vehicle is allowed on this narrow path.
sceneCN: 这里 vehicle 是「车辆」（第 1 个义项：有轮或有发动机的运输工具）；句意为这条窄路上不允许车辆通行。站台边停着的那辆车，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：车辆、交通工具；传播媒介、手段；载体

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「车辆的、车辆使用的」
名词短语，义为「车辆交通」

senses.title: A machine for transport
senses.titleCN: 车辆：能载人载货的机器
senses.definition: a machine with wheels or an engine used to carry people or goods
senses.definitionCN: 有轮或发动机、用来载人或载货的机器
senses.example: No vehicle is allowed on this narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 这条窄路上不允许车辆通行。
senses.why: Latin vehiculum named a plain means of carrying, and the road sense grew from it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vehiculum 原指一种朴素的「搬运手段」，道路上的含义由此长出来。

senses.title: A means of expression
senses.titleCN: 表达手段：让思想能走动的载体
senses.definition: a way or medium through which ideas or feelings are expressed
senses.definitionCN: 使思想或感情得以表达的方式或媒介
senses.example: The novel served as a vehicle for her views on education.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说成了她表达教育观点的载体。
senses.why: What carries goods also carries ideas; the word moves from wheels to words.
senses.whyCN: 能载货的东西也能载思想；这个词从车轮走到了文字。

senses.title: A medium of transmission
senses.titleCN: 传播媒介：把信息或物质送到别处
senses.definition: a substance or channel that carries something to another place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物带到别处的物质或渠道
senses.example: Water is a common vehicle for disease in crowded cities.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的城市里，水常是疾病的传播媒介。
senses.why: The word is neutral about what is carried: people, ideas or germs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对载着什么保持中立：可以是人、思想或病菌。

senses.title: A medium in art and science
senses.titleCN: 溶剂、调色媒介：科学艺术里承载别物的东西
senses.definition: a liquid in which a substance is carried, as in paint or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 承载其他物质的液体，如颜料或药物里的媒介
senses.example: The pigments are held in an oil vehicle before the paint dries.
senses.exampleCN: 颜料在干之前由油性媒介承载。
senses.why: In a workshop the word returns to its plainest sense: something liquid does the carrying.
senses.whyCN: 在作坊里，这个词回到最朴素的意思：由一种液体来承担搬运。

intro.en: Vehicle comes from Latin vehiculum, a means of carrying, built from the verb vehere, to carry.
intro.cn: vehicle 来自拉丁语 vehiculum「搬运手段」，出自动词 vehere「运载」。

items.en: The verb vehere meant to carry or convey, said of riders, ships and carts.
items.cn: 动词 vehere 意为运载，用于骑手、船只和车。

items.en: Its noun vehiculum named any means of transport, not only a machine.
items.cn: 其名词 vehiculum 指任何运输手段，不只是机器。

items.en: French kept véhicule for carts and carriages, and English borrowed that sense.
items.cn: 法语保留 véhicule 指车马，英语借入的就是这一含义。

items.en: With the motor car the street sense tightened into vehicles on wheels.
items.cn: 随着汽车出现，日常含义收窄为带轮子的车辆。

items.en: At the same time the older sense of a carrier widened again into ideas and media.
items.cn: 与此同时，「承载物」的旧义又扩展开来，用于思想与媒介。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the veh- carrying stem; the near-meaning group holds transport words and carriers.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「运载」的 veh- 词干；近义组收交通与承载相关的词。

entries.definition: Of or for vehicles; the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「车辆的」，是本词的形容词形式。

entries.definition: A blood vessel; sounds close but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「血管」，音近但不同根。

entries.definition: To carry something across; formed with con-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「运送、传达」，同一拉丁词根加 con-。

entries.definition: A journey by sea; from the same carrying verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航行」，出自同一个运载动词。

entries.definition: A passenger road vehicle, the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小汽车」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: The whole system of moving people and goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运输」，指整套运送系统。

entries.definition: A channel for ideas or messages, the abstract sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「媒介」，即抽象的含义。

entries.definition: One that carries, used of people, bags or germs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「携带者」，用于人、袋子或病菌。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the carrying root and the double life of the word as transport and as medium.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「运载」词根，以及这个词作为交通工具与媒介的双重身份。

normal.en: Vehicle comes from a Latin verb meaning to carry.
normal.cn: vehicle 出自一个意为「运载」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Motor vehicle is the formal term in law and insurance.
normal.cn: motor vehicle 是法律与保险里的正式说法。

normal.en: A vehicle for change is a means, not a machine.
normal.cn: a vehicle for change 指手段，不是机器。

normal.en: Convey and voyage share the same root as vehicle.
normal.cn: convey 与 voyage 和 vehicle 同根。

normal.en: The plural is vehicles, with the k sound kept before the s.
normal.cn: 复数是 vehicles，k 音在 s 前仍然保留。

abstract.en: Everything in the word is about being carried: a body, an idea, a germ, a colour.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的全是「被载着」：身体、想法、病菌、颜色。

abstract.en: A vehicle changes the reach of what it carries; the idea is the same size, the audience is not.
abstract.cn: 交通工具改变的是所载之物的抵达范围；想法没变大，听众变大了。

abstract.en: The oldest sense was any means; modern life narrowed it to wheels and then quietly reopened it.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义是任何手段；现代生活把它收窄到车轮，又悄悄打开。

examples.en: All vehicles must stop at the red light.
examples.cn: 所有车辆必须在红灯前停下。

examples.en: The film became a vehicle for young actors.
examples.cn: 这部电影成了年轻演员展示自己的载体。

examples.en: Mosquitoes are a vehicle for several diseases.
examples.cn: 蚊子是几种疾病的传播媒介。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为爱扣」——为爱扣上车门，一路载着走：车辆

root: 源自拉丁语名词 vehiculum「运输手段」（动词 vehere「运载」），经法语 véhicule 进入英语；同族词有 convey、voyage、vehicular。

sensesIntro.en: Vehicle begins as anything that carries, narrows to cars, then widens back to ideas, germs and paint.
sensesIntro.cn: vehicle 起初指一切运载之物，收窄为车辆，又扩回思想、病菌与颜料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cart at the platform, doors open, passengers and their plans getting off together.
core.cn: 核心意象：站台边的一辆车，门一开，乘客和他们的计划一起下来。

branches.en: ROAD LINE: machines with wheels or engines.
branches.cn: 道路线：有轮或发动机的机器。

branches.en: ART LINE: a story that carries a point of view.
branches.cn: 艺术线：承载观点的小说或影片。

branches.en: CHANNEL LINE: water or insects carrying disease.
branches.cn: 渠道线：带病的水或昆虫。

branches.en: PAINT LINE: the liquid that holds pigment.
branches.cn: 颜料线：承载颜料的媒介。

branches.en: CONTRAST: transport is the system, a vehicle is one machine in it.
branches.cn: 对照线：transport 是系统，vehicle 是其中一台机器。

intro.en: Vehicle is a Latin noun; its relatives mostly come from the same carrying verb with other prefixes.
intro.cn: vehicle 是拉丁名词，亲属词多由同一运载动词加不同前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is vehere, to carry, giving vehiculum and also vector and convehere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 vehere「运载」，派生出 vehiculum，也派生出 vector 与 convehere。

items.example: It is the core of vehicle.
It names the thing that carries.
It is the same journey idea.
items.exampleCN: 它带有同样的旅程观念。

items.structure: French noun from the same verb

definition_zh: 经由；经过（某地）；通过、借助（某人或某手段）
definition_en: by way of a place, or by means of a person or method
core_image: 一条路线在纸上转弯，绕过一座山，最后才到达目的地
scene: 邮件在三个城市之间转了一圈，最后才落到桌上。We flew to Rome via Zurich.
sceneCN: 这里 via 是「经由某地」（第 1 个义项：路线经过某地）；句意为我们先飞到苏黎世，再转去罗马。那条绕过山再到的路线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 介词：经由、经过；通过、借助

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「高架桥」，与 via 同源于拉丁语 via「道路」
动词，义为「偏离」，同源于拉丁语 via
形容词，义为「明显的」，字面义为「在路上迎面遇上」，同根
形容词，义为「琐碎的」，字面义为「三岔路口的」，同根

senses.title: By way of a place
senses.titleCN: 经由某地：路线经过而不停留
senses.definition: travelling through a place on the way to another
senses.definitionCN: 在前往另一地途中经过某地
senses.example: We flew to Rome via Zurich.
senses.exampleCN: 我们先飞到苏黎世，再转去罗马。
senses.why: Latin via is a road; the preposition simply names the road taken without claiming a stop.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 via 就是道路；这个介词只说走的是哪条路，并不表示停下来。

senses.title: By means of
senses.titleCN: 通过、借助：靠某种手段完成
senses.definition: by means of a particular method, person or service
senses.definitionCN: 通过某种方法、人或服务实现
senses.example: We sent the documents via email to save time.
senses.exampleCN: 为了省时间，我们通过电子邮件发了文件。
senses.why: The road becomes a figure of speech: the channel that carries the action.
senses.whyCN: 道路变成了比喻：承载这个动作的通道。

senses.title: Through an intermediary
senses.titleCN: 经某人转手：不直接对接
senses.definition: through a person or office acting in between
senses.definitionCN: 通过居间的人或机构
senses.example: The message reached him via his assistant.
senses.exampleCN: 消息通过他的助理传到了他那里。
senses.why: The route now runs through a person rather than through a town.
senses.whyCN: 路线这次穿过的是一个人，而不是一座城镇。

senses.title: Through a route or medium
senses.titleCN: 通过某一路径或媒介：抽象通道
senses.definition: through a particular route, path or medium
senses.definitionCN: 通过特定路径或媒介
senses.example: Data travels via underground cables to the other building.
senses.exampleCN: 数据经地下电缆传到另一栋楼。
senses.why: A cable is a road for electricity, and the word applies without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 电缆是电的道路，这个词不再变形就直接用上了。

intro.en: Via is the Latin noun for road, taken whole into English and pressed into service as a preposition.
intro.cn: via 是拉丁语里表示「道路」的名词，整块进入英语后被用作介词。

items.en: The noun via meant a road, way or street, and also a method.
items.cn: 名词 via 意为道路、路径，也可指方法。

items.en: In phrases such as via Appia the ablative already worked as by way of, a road name in use.
items.cn: 在 via Appia 这类短语里，这个夺格形式已经带有「经……路」的意味。

items.en: English borrowed via in the eighteenth century as a preposition of route.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 via，用作表路线的介词。

items.en: Rail, aviation and postal writing spread it through travel timetables.
items.cn: 铁路、航空与邮政文书把它普及到旅行时刻表里。

items.en: Modern usage adds the abstract sense, so documents now travel via email.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了抽象含义，于是文件可以通过邮件旅行。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin road root; the near-meaning group holds prepositions of route and means.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁「道路」词根；近义组收表示路线与手段的介词。

entries.definition: A road carried over a valley; literally a road leader.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「高架桥」，字面即「引路之桥」。

entries.definition: To leave the road; hence to stray.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「偏离」，字面即离开道路。

entries.definition: Literally lying in the road, hence plain to see.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显的」，字面即「在路中遇到」。

entries.definition: Of a crossroads, hence common and slight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「琐碎的」，由「三岔路口」引申为常见而轻微。

entries.definition: By way of, inside and out the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「穿过」，从一头进、另一头出。

entries.definition: By means of, or past a point on a route.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「靠、经」，也可指路过某点。

entries.definition: In every part, stronger than via.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「遍及」，比 via 更强。

entries.definition: Following the length of a road or river.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「沿着」，顺着路或河的长度走。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal road and the modern habits of travel and mail.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用字面上的「道路」，以及现代出行与邮件的习惯。

normal.en: Via is Latin for road, and roads explain the word.
normal.cn: via 是拉丁语的「道路」，道路解释了它。

normal.en: Fly via Paris means Paris is on the way, not the destination.
normal.cn: fly via Paris 指巴黎在途中，不是目的地。

normal.en: Send it via email means the message takes a digital road.
normal.cn: send it via email 指消息走了一条数字的路。

normal.en: Obvious, deviate and trivial all come from the same road word.
normal.cn: obvious、deviate、trivial 都出自同一个「道路」词。

normal.en: Via does not mean in: you do not stop there for long.
normal.cn: via 不等于 in：你不在那里久留。

abstract.en: Via names the path rather than the place: it tells you how the thing got here.
abstract.cn: via 命名的是路径而非地点：它告诉你东西是怎么过来的。

abstract.en: Anything that moves needs a road, so the word stretches to cables, satellites and people.
abstract.cn: 凡会动的东西都需要一条路，于是这个词扩展到电缆、卫星和人。

abstract.en: To name the route is already to hint at the motive, which is why the same word covers means.
abstract.cn: 说出路线已经在暗示成因，所以同一个词也能表示手段。

examples.en: We returned home via the coast road.
examples.cn: 我们沿着海边公路回家。

examples.en: Please send your application via the website.
examples.cn: 请通过网站提交申请。

examples.en: He learned the news via a friend in the office.
examples.cn: 他从办公室的一位朋友那里得到这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外啊」——外啊，外面这条路经过咱们这儿：经由

root: 直接来自拉丁语名词 via「道路、方法」，十八世纪起在英语中作介词使用；同根词有 viaduct、deviate、obvious、trivial。

sensesIntro.en: Via travels from a real road, to a method, to a person in between, to an abstract channel.
sensesIntro.cn: via 从真实的道路出发，走到方法、居间的人，再到抽象的通道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on a map that bends around a hill before reaching the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一条线绕过小山，才到目的地。

branches.en: ROUTE LINE: a place passed on the way.
branches.cn: 路线线：途中经过的地点。

branches.en: METHOD LINE: the means by which it is done.
branches.cn: 方法线：办成事所借助的手段。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: a message relayed by someone else.
branches.cn: 人际线：由别人转达的消息。

branches.en: CABLE LINE: an abstract path or medium.
branches.cn: 线路线：抽象的路径或媒介。

branches.en: CONTRAST: via names the way, in names the place.
branches.cn: 对照线：via 说路，in 说地。

intro.en: Via has no affixes, but the Latin noun it comes from hides inside several English words.
intro.cn: via 没有词缀，但构成它的拉丁名词藏在好几个英语词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun via, road, survives in viaduct, deviate, obvious and trivial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 via「道路」残留在 viaduct、deviate、obvious、trivial 里。

items.example: It forms deviate, to leave the road.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 deviate，即离开道路。

items.example: It forms obvious, in the way.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 obvious，即在路中遇到。

items.example: It forms trivial, of three roads.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trivial，即三岔路口的。

definition_zh: 受害者；牺牲品、殉难者；遇难者；（事故、疾病的）受害者
definition_en: a person harmed, injured or killed as the result of a crime, accident or other event
core_image: 一队被牵去献祭的牲畜，脖子上系着彩带，走在前头
scene: 火灾过后，邻居们围在被烧黑的门口，不知道该说什么。The victims of the flood are still waiting for help.
sceneCN: 这里 victim 是「受害者」（第 1 个义项：在灾难或罪案中受到伤害的人）；句意为洪水的受害者仍在等待救援。被牵去献祭的牲畜，就是这个词最早的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：受害者；牺牲品、殉难者；遇难者

collocations.zh: 装可怜、摆出受害者姿态

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「使受害、迫害」，由本词加 -ize 构成
名词，义为「受害、迫害」
形容词，义为「无受害者的」，如 victimless crime
名词，义为「受害者身份」

senses.title: One harmed by another
senses.titleCN: 受害者：被罪案或他人伤害的人
senses.definition: a person harmed by a crime or by someone else’s action
senses.definitionCN: 被犯罪或他人行为伤害的人
senses.example: The victims of the flood are still waiting for help.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水的受害者仍在等待救援。
senses.why: Latin victima was the animal led to sacrifice; the modern sense keeps the picture of someone taken and harmed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 victima 是被牵去献祭的牲畜；现代含义仍保留「被夺去并受伤害」的画面。

senses.title: One killed or injured
senses.titleCN: 遇难者：在事故或灾害中伤亡的人
senses.definition: a person killed or injured in an accident or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 在事故或灾害中死亡或受伤的人
senses.example: Road victims have fallen since the speed limit changed.
senses.exampleCN: 限速改变后，道路事故的死伤者减少了。
senses.why: No agent is needed here; the harm comes from events, not from a criminal.
senses.whyCN: 这里不需要施害者：伤害来自事件，而不是罪犯。

senses.title: One suffering from illness
senses.titleCN: 病人：受疾病折磨的人
senses.definition: a person suffering from a disease or condition
senses.definitionCN: 受某种疾病或状况折磨的人
senses.example: Many victims of the disease do not know they have it.
senses.exampleCN: 许多患这种病的人并不知道自己有。
senses.why: Illness is treated as an outer force that takes prisoners, much like an accident.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被当成一种抓走人的外部力量，与事故相似。

senses.title: A sacrifice
senses.titleCN: 牺牲品：为了别的目的而被舍弃的人或物
senses.definition: someone or something given up for another purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为别的目的被舍弃的人或物
senses.example: The old building became a victim of the redevelopment plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老建筑成了重建计划的牺牲品。
senses.why: Buildings cannot feel pain, yet the pattern holds: something old is given up for something new.
senses.whyCN: 建筑不会感到疼痛，但模式仍在：旧的东西为新的东西被舍弃了。

senses.title: A self-chosen role
senses.titleCN: 装出的受害者：把自己当成被亏待的人
senses.definition: a role taken on by someone who claims unfair treatment
senses.definitionCN: 某人自称受到不公而摆出的姿态
senses.example: He always plays the victim when the plan goes wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 计划一出错，他就摆出受害者的姿态。
senses.why: The word turns ironic here: the person chooses the role instead of receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词带了反讽：角色是自己选的，而不是被强加的。

intro.en: Victim comes from Latin victima, a beast offered in sacrifice, and has kept the sense of being taken and harmed.
intro.cn: victim 来自拉丁语 victima「祭献用的牲畜」，一直保留着「被夺去并受伤害」的意思。

items.en: Victima named the animal led to the altar, chosen and given up.
items.cn: victima 指被牵上祭坛的牲畜，被选中并被舍弃。

items.en: The word belonged to the language of sacrifice, with its sense of a life taken.
items.cn: 这个词属于献祭的语言，含「夺走一条生命」的意思。

items.en: French kept victime for a creature sacrificed or killed, sacred or not.
items.cn: 法语保留 victime，指被献祭或被杀的生命，不论是否神圣。

items.en: English took victim in the fifteenth century, widening it to anyone who suffers harm.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 victim，扩展到任何受到伤害的人。

items.en: Modern usage applies it to crime, disaster, disease and, ironically, to a chosen pose.
items.cn: 现代用法把它用于罪案、灾害、疾病，甚至反讽地指一种自愿摆出的姿态。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the victim- family; the near-meaning group holds words for those who suffer or are lost.
note.cn: 形近组沿 victim- 家族；近义组收表示受难者与损失的词。

entries.definition: To make someone a victim, often unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使受害、迫害」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: The act of treating someone as a victim.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受害、被迫害」。

entries.definition: Having no harmed party, as in some crimes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无受害者的」。

entries.definition: The state of being a victim.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受害者身份」。

entries.definition: One who endures pain or illness, often long term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受苦者、患者」，多为长期。

entries.definition: One killed or wounded in fighting or an accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤亡者」，多用于战争与事故。

entries.definition: One who lived through the same event, the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幸存者」，同一事件的另一面。

entries.definition: The one aimed at, before any harm is done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标」，伤害尚未发生前的一方。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the sacrifice picture and the phrase fall victim to.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「献祭」的画面与 fall victim to 这一搭配。

normal.en: Victim once meant the animal led to the altar.
normal.cn: victim 原本指被牵上祭坛的牲畜。

normal.en: Fall victim to a scam means the trick caught you.
normal.cn: fall victim to a scam 指你被这个骗局抓住了。

normal.en: Victims of a flood are harmed by weather, not by a criminal.
normal.cn: 洪水的受害者是被天气所害，而不是被罪犯。

normal.en: Victimize is the verb: to make someone a victim.
normal.cn: victimize 是动词：使某人成为受害者。

normal.en: Playing the victim is a choice of role, not a fact.
normal.cn: playing the victim 是一种角色选择，不是事实。

abstract.en: The word began in sacrifice, and every later use keeps the shape of a life given up for something else.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于献祭，此后每种用法都保留着「为别的东西交出生命」的形状。

abstract.en: A victim is defined by what happened to them, which is why the word is passive in grammar and in feeling.
abstract.cn: 受害者是由遭遇定义的，所以这个词在语法和情感上都是被动的。

abstract.en: Naming someone a victim gives them sympathy but takes away agency, a tension the word never resolves.
abstract.cn: 称某人为受害者，给了他同情却拿走了主动性，这个矛盾这个词从未解决。

examples.en: The charity helps victims of domestic violence.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构帮助家庭暴力的受害者。

examples.en: Many small shops fell victim to the rise in rents.
examples.cn: 许多小店成了租金上涨的牺牲品。

examples.en: She was the victim of a cruel joke.
examples.cn: 她是一个恶作剧的受害者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克提姆」——维克（围）克（制）提（他）姆（母亲）受害了：受害者

root: 源自拉丁语名词 victima「祭献用的牲畜」，经法语 victime 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 victimize、victimization、victimhood。

sensesIntro.en: Victim stretches from the sacrificed animal to crime, accidents, illness, lost buildings and a chosen pose.
sensesIntro.cn: victim 从被献祭的牲畜，延伸到罪案、事故、疾病、被拆的建筑与自愿摆出的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an animal led to the altar with ribbons on its neck.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头脖子系着彩带、被牵向祭坛的牲畜。

branches.en: CRIME LINE: harmed by another person.
branches.cn: 罪案线：被他人所害。

branches.en: DISASTER LINE: injured by events.
branches.cn: 灾害线：被事件所伤。

branches.en: ILLNESS LINE: struck by disease.
branches.cn: 疾病线：被病痛击中。

branches.en: FIGURE LINE: a building given up, a role worn on purpose.
branches.cn: 比喻线：被舍弃的建筑，故意披上的角色。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a victim receives harm, a target is only aimed at.
branches.cn: 对照线：受害者已受到伤害，目标只是被瞄准。

intro.en: Victim is a complete Latin noun; English relatives add -ize, -ization, -hood and -less.
intro.cn: victim 是完整的拉丁名词，英语亲属词加 -ize、-ization、-hood、-less。

latinIntro.en: The single Latin form is victima, a ritual word without a clear further root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式只有一个 victima，是礼仪用语，更早的词根并不明确。

definition_zh: 没有价值的；无用的；不值钱的；毫无意义的
definition_en: having no value, use or importance
core_image: 一张被水泡烂的纸币摊在桌上，数字还在，却没人肯收
scene: 旧箱子里翻出一堆受潮的邮票，颜色都糊在一起了。The painting turned out to be worthless, a copy made last year.
sceneCN: 这里 worthless 是「不值钱的」（第 1 个义项：没有市场价值）；句意为这幅画原来不值钱，是去年做的仿品。被水泡烂的钞票，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：没有价值的、无用的；不值钱的；毫无意义的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「价值」，是 worthless 的词干
名词，义为「无价值、无用」
形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，加 -y 构成的反向词
形容词，义为「值得做的」，由 worth 与 while 合成

senses.title: Having no money value
senses.titleCN: 不值钱：卖不出价钱
senses.definition: having no financial value, or almost none
senses.definitionCN: 没有或几乎没有金钱价值
senses.example: The painting turned out to be worthless, a copy made last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画原来不值钱，是去年做的仿品。
senses.why: The -less ending simply removes worth; nothing is added in its place, so the gap is complete.
senses.whyCN: -less 尾缀只是把 worth 拿掉，什么也不补上，于是缺口彻底空了。

senses.title: Having no use
senses.titleCN: 无用：拿在手里也不解决问题
senses.definition: of no practical use for its purpose
senses.definitionCN: 对它的用途没有实际帮助
senses.example: The map was worthless after the old roads were closed.
senses.exampleCN: 老路封闭之后，那张地图就没用了。
senses.why: Here the value is usefulness: something that cannot do its job has lost the worth we hoped for.
senses.whyCN: 这里衡量的是用处：干不了自己该干的事，就失去我们寄望的价值。

senses.title: Of no importance
senses.titleCN: 毫无意义：不值得在意
senses.definition: too slight to matter
senses.definitionCN: 太轻微而不值得在意
senses.example: Without the data, the argument is worthless.
senses.exampleCN: 没有数据支撑，这个论点毫无意义。
senses.why: Worth also means importance, and losing it leaves a claim that convinces nobody.
senses.whyCN: worth 也有重要性之义，一旦失去，论点就说服不了任何人。

senses.title: About a person
senses.titleCN: 一无是处：人觉得对自己没信心（口语）
senses.definition: used of a person who feels or is said to be of no account
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人觉得自己或被人说成一无是处
senses.example: Nobody is worthless, however badly they have failed.
senses.exampleCN: 不管失败得多惨，没有人是一无是处的。
senses.why: The word is harsh when used of people, because it judges the whole person, not one act.
senses.whyCN: 用来说人时很重，因为它评判的是整个人，而不是一件事。

intro.en: Worthless is the old English noun worth, value, plus the privative suffix -less.
intro.cn: worthless 是古英语名词 worth「价值」加上表缺失的后缀 -less。

items.en: The noun weorth meant value or price, the worth a thing carried.
items.cn: 名词 weorth 意为价值或价钱，即一物所承载的份量。

items.en: The adjective worthleas formed early, describing what had no price.
items.cn: 形容词 worthleas 形成很早，描述没有价钱的东西。

items.en: Germanic languages regularly formed a lacking word with -less, as German -los shows.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语惯用 -less 这类尾缀造「缺失」之词，德语 -los 亦然。

items.en: Middle English kept the word and spread it from price to usefulness and importance.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个词，并把它从价钱扩展到用处与重要性。

items.en: Modern usage adds the moral and personal sense, so a person can be called worthless.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了道德与个人含义，于是人也可以被称为 worthless。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the worth- family; the near-meaning group holds adjectives of having little value.
note.cn: 形近组沿 worth- 家族；近义组收表示价值低微的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun and preposition behind the word: value, or deserving of.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或介词，义为「价值、值得」，本词的词干。

entries.definition: Deserving respect or effort; the opposite ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，尾缀正相反。

entries.definition: Worth the time spent, built from worth plus while.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得做的」，由 worth 与 while 合成。

entries.definition: The state of being without value.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无价值」，加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Cannot do its job; close but about function.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无用的」，侧重功能。

entries.definition: Without value, almost a synonym in price.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无价值的」，在价钱上几乎同义。

entries.definition: Having no purpose, said of actions mainly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无意义的」，多用于行为。

entries.definition: Of great value; the opposite pole of the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「珍贵的」，同一尺度的另一端。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the privative -less and the many kinds of worth that can be lost.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用表缺失的 -less，以及可以被丢掉的多种价值。

normal.en: Worth is value, -less takes it away: worth + less = worthless.
normal.cn: worth 是价值，-less 拿掉它：worth 加 less 即成 worthless。

normal.en: A worthless note will not buy bread, no matter what the number says.
normal.cn: 不管票面写多少，废钞买不了面包。

normal.en: Worthless without data means the argument cannot stand alone.
normal.cn: 后接 without data，指论点无法独立成立。

normal.en: Worthless and priceless look alike but are opposites in price.
normal.cn: worthless 与 priceless 长得像，在价钱上却相反。

normal.en: Calling a person worthless attacks the person, not the work.
normal.cn: 说一个人 worthless，攻击的是人，不是做事。

abstract.en: The word is a subtraction, not an insult: worth has been removed and nothing put in its place.
abstract.cn: 这个词是做减法而不是骂人：价值被抽走，空位没有填。

abstract.en: Value is always value for someone, so worthless describes a relation, not a fact inside the thing.
abstract.cn: 价值总是对某人的价值，所以 worthless 描述的是一种关系，而非物内的事实。

abstract.en: Money, maps and promises all become worthless when the world they assumed disappears.
abstract.cn: 当世界变了样，钞票、地图与承诺都会变得毫无价值。

examples.en: The shares are now almost worthless.
examples.cn: 这些股票现在几乎一文不值。

examples.en: A promise made in anger is often worthless.
examples.cn: 气头上许下的承诺往往是空话。

examples.en: He felt worthless after losing the job.
examples.cn: 失业之后他觉得自己一无是处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃思勒斯」——沃思（我思）勒斯（了死）也没想出价值：无价值的

root: 古英语名词 weorth「价值」加表缺失的后缀 -less，古英语已作 worthleas；同族词有 worth、worthy、worthwhile。

sensesIntro.en: Worthless measures price, usefulness, importance and, most harshly, a person’s sense of self.
sensesIntro.cn: worthless 衡量价钱、用处、重要性，最重的一层是对人的自我评价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soaked banknote, the number intact, no shop willing to take it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张泡烂的钞票，数字还在，却没人肯收。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the market will not pay.
branches.cn: 金钱线：市场不肯付钱。

branches.en: TOOL LINE: it cannot do its job.
branches.cn: 工具线：它干不成自己的事。

branches.en: ARGUMENT LINE: nothing here convinces anyone.
branches.cn: 论证线：这里任何结论都说服不了人。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: a verdict on a whole life.
branches.cn: 人身线：对整个人生的判决。

branches.en: CONTRAST: valueless is about price, useless about function.
branches.cn: 对照线：valueless 谈价钱，useless 谈功能。

intro.en: Worthless is a stem plus a privative suffix; its family shows the same stem with other endings.
intro.cn: worthless 是词干加表缺失的后缀，家族里同一词干还接其他词尾。

latinIntro.en: Nothing Latin here: the word is native English, and -less descends from an old Germanic privative.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分：词是英语本土的，-less 源自日耳曼语的表缺失成分。

items.example: It forms worthwhile in older spellings.
items.exampleCN: 它在旧拼法里参与 worthwhile。

items.example: It is the opposite of worthless.
It shows the stem as a preposition.
items.exampleCN: 它展示词干作介词的用法。

definition_zh: 值得做的；值得花时间的；值得花力气的；有价值的
definition_en: worth the time, effort or money spent on it
core_image: 一趟跋涉之后站在山顶，疲劳还在，心里却说不虚此行
scene: 花了三年改稿，书终于出版，作者说这三年没白费。It is worthwhile checking the figures before you send the report.
sceneCN: 这里 worthwhile 是「值得做的」（第 1 个义项：花的时间与力气有回报）；句意为发报告前把数据核一遍是值得的。爬到山顶说不虚此行的感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：值得做的、值得花时间的、值得花力气的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「价值」，是合成词的前半部分
名词，义为「一段时间」，是合成词的后半部分
副词，义为「无价值地」，属反面一支
形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，同族
介词，义为「值、值得」，常与 doing 连用

senses.title: Worth the time given
senses.titleCN: 值得做：花掉的时间有回报
senses.definition: worth the time spent on it
senses.definitionCN: 花在上面的时间有回报
senses.example: It is worthwhile checking the figures before you send the report.
senses.exampleCN: 发报告前把数据核一遍是值得的。
senses.why: The word joins worth, value, to while, a stretch of time: the value must cover the time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 worth「价值」与 while「一段时间」拼在一起：价值必须抵得过时间。

senses.title: Worth the effort
senses.titleCN: 值得费力：辛苦没有白费
senses.definition: worth the effort and difficulty involved
senses.definitionCN: 付出的力气与困难有回报
senses.example: The climb was hard, but the view made it worthwhile.
senses.exampleCN: 爬山很辛苦，但风景让这趟很值。
senses.why: Effort is a cost like money, and the word can be paid in it too.
senses.whyCN: 力气是和金钱一样的成本，这个词也接受用力气付款。

senses.title: Worth the money
senses.titleCN: 值得花钱：投入能收回来
senses.definition: worth the money paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 付出的钱能收回来
senses.example: The repairs were expensive but worthwhile in the long run.
senses.exampleCN: 修理费很贵，但长远看是值得的。
senses.why: Cost and benefit sit in the same sentence, and the word decides for the benefit.
senses.whyCN: 成本与收益被放进同一个句子，而这个词判给了收益。

senses.title: Worth doing at all
senses.titleCN: 有价值的：事情本身有意义
senses.definition: having real value or importance, said of causes and work
senses.definitionCN: 本身具有真实价值，用于事业与工作
senses.example: She found the work worthwhile even though the pay was low.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得这份工作很有意义，尽管报酬很低。
senses.why: Here the return is not money but meaning, the widest kind of while that worth can cover.
senses.whyCN: 这里的回报不是钱而是意义，这是 worth 能抵付的最宽的一种时间。

intro.en: Worthwhile is a late English compound: worth, value, plus while, a period of time, meaning worth the time.
intro.cn: worthwhile 是较晚出现的英语合成词：worth「价值」加 while「一段时间」，即「值这段时间」。

items.en: The noun weorth meant value or price, and the preposition use came later.
items.cn: 名词 weorth 意为价值或价钱，介词用法出现较晚。

items.en: The noun hwil meant a period of time, source of modern while.
items.cn: 名词 hwil 意为一段时间，是现代 while 的来源。

items.en: Worthwhile appeared as a compound in the nineteenth century, first in American writing.
items.cn: worthwhile 作为合成词在十九世纪出现，最早见于美国文字。

items.en: Modern usage often follows worth one’s while and it is worthwhile doing.
items.cn: 现代用法常见 worth one’s while 与 it is worthwhile doing 两种句式。

items.en: The word spread from business and education into general judgements of effort.
items.cn: 这个词从商业与教育扩展到对一切付出的总体评价。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the worth- family and the while compound; the near-meaning group holds words for being worth something.
note.cn: 形近组沿 worth- 家族与 while 合成词；近义组收表示值得的词。

entries.definition: Value, or the preposition meaning deserving of.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或介词，义为「价值、值得」，本词前半部。

entries.definition: A period of time; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一段时间」，本词后半部。

entries.definition: Deserving of respect or effort, used of people and causes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得的、可敬的」，用于人与事业。

entries.definition: Having no value, the negative cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无价值的」，反面的近亲。

entries.definition: Worth a lot, often in money or usefulness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有价值的」，多指金钱或效用。

entries.definition: Giving satisfaction for the effort made.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有回报的」，强调满足感。

entries.definition: Helpful for a purpose, without the cost comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有用的」，不含成本比较。

entries.definition: Not worth doing at all, the opposite judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毫无意义的」，相反的判断。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal sum inside the compound: value versus time spent.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用合成词里那笔字面账：价值对花掉的时间。

normal.en: Worthwhile is worth plus while: the value must cover the time.
normal.cn: worthwhile 是 worth 加 while：价值要抵得住时间。

normal.en: It is worthwhile doing is the standard pattern before a gerund.
normal.cn: worthwhile 后接动名词时常用 it is worthwhile doing 的句式。

normal.en: Well worthwhile adds emphasis but changes nothing else.
normal.cn: well worthwhile 只是加强语气，其余不变。

normal.en: Worthy describes people and causes, worthwhile describes time and effort.
normal.cn: worthy 说人与事业，worthwhile 说时间与力气。

normal.en: Make it worthwhile means add something so the effort pays.
normal.cn: make it worthwhile 指加点东西让这份辛苦有回报。

abstract.en: The compound hides an economics of life: every yes to one thing is a no to the hours it takes.
abstract.cn: 这个合成词藏着一门生活经济学：对一件事说「好」，就是对它占用的钟点说「不」。

abstract.en: Value here is judged afterwards as well as before; that is why we say it proved worthwhile.
abstract.cn: 这里的价值既在事前判断也在事后判断，所以说 it proved worthwhile。

abstract.en: Anything worth the while is worth it to someone, which is why the word never settles a question by itself.
abstract.cn: 值不值总是对某个人而言，所以这个词从不能独自断案。

examples.en: It is worthwhile keeping a copy of every letter.
examples.cn: 每封信都留个副本是值得的。

examples.en: The extra training proved worthwhile in the end.
examples.cn: 额外的培训最终证明是值得的。

examples.en: They made the trip worthwhile by staying an extra week.
examples.cn: 他们多待了一周，让这趟行程更值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃思外偶」——沃思（我思）外偶（外哦），外面走走也值得：值得做的

root: 由 worth「价值」与 while「一段时间」在十九世纪合成，意为「值得花这段时间的」；同族词有 worth、worthy、worthless。

sensesIntro.en: Worthwhile measures the return on time, effort, money, or the plain value of the work itself.
sensesIntro.cn: worthwhile 衡量的是对时间、力气、金钱的回报，或工作本身的价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing on a summit, tired but certain the climb was not wasted.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在山顶，累却确定这趟没白爬。

branches.en: TIME LINE: hours spent and repaid.
branches.cn: 时间线：花掉的钟点被偿还。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the effort paid off.
branches.cn: 身体线：力气有了回报。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the cost comes back.
branches.cn: 金钱线：成本收得回来。

branches.en: MEANING LINE: the work matters in itself.
branches.cn: 意义线：工作本身就有价值。

branches.en: CONTRAST: worthwhile is about return, worthy is about merit.
branches.cn: 对照线：worthwhile 讲回报，worthy 讲品格。

intro.en: Worthwhile is a compound of two whole English words; nothing is glued on with an affix.
intro.cn: worthwhile 是两个完整英语词的合成，没有使用词缀粘接。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin here; both halves are Old English nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分，前后两半都是古英语名词。

items.example: It forms worthwhileness in rare use.
It appears in older forms of the compound.
It is the full phrase behind it.
items.exampleCN: 它是本词背后的完整说法。

definition_zh: （will 的过去式）将、会；（表意愿）愿意、肯；（表推测）大概会；（表虚拟）就会、本来会；（表习惯）过去常常；（请求）请……好吗
definition_en: the past form of will, used for the future seen from the past, for polite requests, and for unreal situations
core_image: 一个人站在岔路口，看着那条没走的路
scene: 朋友邀你吃饭，你已经在忙，只回了一句下次一定。When I was young, we would walk to school together.
sceneCN: 这里 would 表示「过去常常」（第 5 个义项：过去的反复习惯）；句意为小时候我们常常一起走路上学。看着那条没走的路，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 情态动词：将、会；愿意；大概会；就会（虚拟）；过去常常；（礼貌请求）

derivatives.zh: 情态动词，义为「将、会」，是 would 的原形
缩合形式，义为「不会」，是 would not 的口语形
形容词，义为「愿意的」，与 would 同源于「意愿」
名词，义为「意志」，同源名词
形容词，义为「未来的、自称的」，由 would 加 be 合成

senses.title: Future seen from the past
senses.titleCN: 过去的将来：从过去看那一刻的将然
senses.definition: the past form of will, for a future viewed from a past moment
senses.definitionCN: will 的过去式，表示从过去某点看将来
senses.example: He said he would come back before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 他说他天黑前会回来。
senses.why: English pushes will one step back in time; the reported future keeps its shape but takes the past form.
senses.whyCN: 英语把 will 向后推一步；被转述的将来形状不变，只是领了过去的形态。

senses.title: Willingness
senses.titleCN: 意愿：愿意、肯
senses.definition: used to express willingness or refusal
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示愿意或拒绝
senses.example: She would not listen to any excuse.
senses.exampleCN: 她什么借口都不肯听。
senses.why: The original will in English meant to want; that wanting survives in would you and I would gladly.
senses.whyCN: will 在英语里原意是「想要」，这层「想要」留在 would you 与 I would gladly 里。

senses.title: Polite requests
senses.titleCN: 礼貌请求：把话说得软一些
senses.definition: used to make a request less direct and more polite
senses.definitionCN: 用来使请求不那么直接、更客气
senses.example: Would you close the window, please?
senses.exampleCN: 请你把窗户关上好吗？
senses.why: Distance in grammar is politeness: the past form stands further from the listener than will.
senses.whyCN: 语法上的距离就是礼貌：过去式比 will 离听话人更远一步。

senses.title: Unreal conditions
senses.titleCN: 虚拟：与事实相反的情形
senses.definition: used in the result clause of an unreal condition
senses.definitionCN: 用在虚拟条件的结果分句里
senses.example: If I had known, I would have called you.
senses.exampleCN: 要是我当时知道，就会给你打电话了。
senses.why: A form that is one step back from reality is perfect for describing what did not happen.
senses.whyCN: 比现实退后一步的形式，正好用来描述没有发生的事。

senses.title: Past habit
senses.titleCN: 过去常常：反复发生的旧习惯
senses.definition: used for repeated actions in the past
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示过去反复发生的动作
senses.example: When I was young, we would walk to school together.
senses.exampleCN: 小时候我们常常一起走路上学。
senses.why: Habit is a small future repeated; the word marks each occasion without claiming permanence.
senses.whyCN: 习惯是被重复的小小将来；这个词标记每一次，而不主张永久。

senses.title: Probability
senses.titleCN: 推测：大概会
senses.definition: used to state what is likely, less certain than will
senses.definitionCN: 用来陈述可能性，比 will 更不确定
senses.example: It would be about five when they arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 他们到的时候大概是五点左右。
senses.why: Certainty is softened by the past form, so the statement stays a guess.
senses.whyCN: 过去式把确定性放软，于是这句话仍然只是猜测。

intro.en: Would is the past form of Old English willan, to wish, and still carries that wish in polite requests.
intro.cn: would 是古英语动词 willan「想要」的过去式，礼貌请求里仍然带着这层「想要」。

items.en: The verb willan meant to want or wish, and had its own past tense wolde.
items.cn: 动词 willan 意为想要、愿意，有自己的过去式 wolde。

items.en: Wolde covered both past wish and past habitual action, two senses that survive.
items.cn: wolde 既表过去的意愿，也表过去的习惯动作，两种含义都留存下来。

items.en: Middle English respelled wolde as would, and the l was later silenced in speech.
items.cn: 中古英语把 wolde 改拼为 would，后来口语里 l 不再发音。

items.en: Grammarians put would into conditional sentences as the standard form for unreality.
items.cn: 近代早期语法学家把 would 定为条件句中表示非现实的规范形式。

items.en: Modern English uses it for the past future, politeness, habits and speculation, one word with many mild duties.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表过去将来、礼貌、习惯与推测，一个词担着许多温和的职务。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the other modal and semi-modal forms; the near-meaning group holds expressions of willingness and habit.
note.cn: 形近组收其他情态与半情态形式；近义组收意愿与习惯的表达。

entries.definition: The present form of would, for a future that still may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，义为「将、会」，仍是可能发生的将来。

entries.definition: A modal for future and offers, mainly formal British use.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，表将来与提议，多见于正式英式英语。

entries.definition: The past form of can, also used for politeness and possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，can 的过去式，也用于礼貌与可能。

entries.definition: The past form of may, used for a weaker possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，may 的过去式，表示更弱的可能。

entries.definition: The past of shall, but now mainly about duty or advice.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，shall 的过去式，如今主要表义务与建议。

entries.definition: The clearest way to describe a past habit.
entries.definitionCN: 半情态短语，义为「过去常常」，表旧习惯最清楚。

entries.definition: The full phrase for being ready to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「愿意做」，把意愿说全。

entries.definition: Wanting to be something, as in a would-be actor.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「想当……的」，如 would-be actor。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the idea of one step back from reality, which explains most uses of would.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「比现实退后一步」这一想法，它解释了 would 的大多数用法。

normal.en: Would is will stepped back one tense, and that step explains politeness and unreality.
normal.cn: would 是 will 退后一个时态，这一步解释了礼貌与虚拟。

normal.en: Would like to is the polite way to say want to.
normal.cn: would like to 是 want to 的客气说法。

normal.en: Would rather chooses, would sooner chooses more firmly.
normal.cn: would rather 是选择，would sooner 更坚决。

normal.en: Would have done describes the branch that was never taken.
normal.cn: would have done 描述那条从未走上的岔路。

normal.en: We would walk to school means we did it again and again.
normal.cn: we would walk to school 指我们反复这样做过。

abstract.en: Would is grammar’s way of leaving the room: it speaks about futures, habits and wishes without standing in them.
abstract.cn: would 是语法上的「抽身」：谈将来、习惯与愿望，却不站在其中。

abstract.en: Every polite request is a small fiction: the speaker pretends the answer is not yet fixed.
abstract.cn: 每个礼貌请求都是一点小小的虚构：说话人假装答案还没定。

abstract.en: One little word holds the open and the closed door at once: what would happen, and what would have.
abstract.cn: 这个小词同时握着开着与关着的门：将会发生什么，以及本来会发生什么。

examples.en: I said I would help, and I will.
examples.cn: 我说过我会帮忙，我就一定帮。

examples.en: Would you pass me the salt?
examples.cn: 请把盐递给我好吗？

examples.en: If I were taller, I would play basketball.
examples.cn: 要是我更高一些，就会去打篮球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捂的」——捂着嘴小声请求，语气软：会、愿意

root: 古英语动词 willan「想要」的过去式 wolde，中古英语改拼为 would；同源词有 will（动词与名词）、willing、would-be。

sensesIntro.en: Would works as past future, as willingness, as politeness, as unreality, as habit and as mild speculation.
sensesIntro.cn: would 可作过去将来、意愿、礼貌、虚拟、习惯与温和推测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a fork, looking down the path not taken.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在岔路口，望着那条没走的路。

branches.en: TENSE LINE: the future as seen from the past.
branches.cn: 时态线：从过去看的将来。

branches.en: WILL LINE: willingness and refusal.
branches.cn: 意愿线：愿意与不肯。

branches.en: MANNER LINE: politeness through distance.
branches.cn: 方式线：用距离表达客气。

branches.en: SHADE LINE: unreality, habit and guesswork.
branches.cn: 语气线：虚拟、习惯与推测。

branches.en: CONTRAST: will is open future, would have is closed past.
branches.cn: 对照线：will 是敞开的将来，would have 是关上的过去。

intro.en: Would takes no affixes; its shortened form ’d is the only regular reduction.
intro.cn: would 不带词缀，唯一常见的缩略是 ’d。

latinIntro.en: No Latin enters here; the modal is a native Germanic verb form.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里没有拉丁成分，它是日耳曼语本土的动词形式。

items.exampleCN: 它由 will 构成 willing。

items.example: It shows the modal as a bound form.
items.exampleCN: 它展示这个情态词的粘着用法。

definition_zh: 写；书写；写作、撰写；（给某人）写信；把……写下来
definition_en: to form letters or words on a surface, or to compose a text
core_image: 笔尖落纸，墨水留下第一道弯钩，字从笔痕里长出来
scene: 灯下一个人反复划掉又重写，纸角被手压得发皱。Please write your name at the top of the page.
sceneCN: 这里 write 是「写、书写」（第 1 个义项：在纸面上形成文字）；句意为请把你的名字写在页面顶端。笔尖在纸上留下的第一道弯钩，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：写、书写；写作、撰写；写信；记录

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「作者、作家」，加 -er 构成
名词，义为「书写、著作」，加 -ing 构成
形容词，义为「书面的」，是过去分词作形容词
名词，义为「书面命令」，法律用语，形式古老
名词，义为「笔迹、手写体」

senses.title: To form letters
senses.titleCN: 书写：在纸上画成字母和词
senses.definition: to form letters or words on a surface with a pen or keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 用笔或键盘在表面上形成字母或词
senses.example: Please write your name at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 请把你的名字写在页面顶端。
senses.why: Old English writan first meant to scratch or carve; letters are still scratches that carry meaning.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 writan 原意为刻划；字母至今仍是带意义的刻痕。

senses.title: To compose a text
senses.titleCN: 写作：把想法组织成文字
senses.definition: to compose a text such as a book, letter or report
senses.definitionCN: 撰写书籍、信件、报告等文本
senses.example: She writes for a newspaper in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她在北方一家报社写稿。
senses.why: Scratching becomes making: the verb now covers the whole labour of building a text.
senses.whyCN: 从刻字变成创作：这个动词现在涵盖构建一篇文章的全部劳动。

senses.title: To send a letter
senses.titleCN: 写信：与某人通过信件联系
senses.definition: to send a letter to someone
senses.definitionCN: 给某人寄信以联系
senses.example: Write to me when you get there.
senses.exampleCN: 你到那儿以后给我写信。
senses.why: Communication is implied by the act: writing to someone is already reaching them.
senses.whyCN: 交流被包含在动作里：给某人写信，已经在抵达对方。

senses.title: To record
senses.titleCN: 记录：把信息留下来
senses.definition: to record something in writing or data
senses.definitionCN: 用文字或数据记录下来
senses.example: The doctor wrote the prescription in a hurry.
senses.exampleCN: 医生匆匆写了处方。
senses.why: The text is short here, but its purpose is the same: to leave a lasting mark.
senses.whyCN: 这里的文字很短，但目的相同：留下耐久的痕迹。

senses.title: With particles
senses.titleCN: 短语动词：与 down、off、up 合成新义
senses.definition: used with down, off or up to mean record, cancel or complete
senses.definitionCN: 与 down、off、up 连用，分别表示记下、勾销与整理成文
senses.example: They wrote off the whole consignment as damaged.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这批货整体作为损坏勾销了。
senses.why: The particles carry the direction; the root keeps the idea of putting something into marks.
senses.whyCN: 小品词承担方向，词根仍是「把东西变成痕迹」。

intro.en: Write descends from Old English writan, to scratch or carve, a word older than paper in England.
intro.cn: write 源自英语 writan「刻划」，在纸张传入英格兰之前就存在。

items.en: Writan meant to score or scratch, and was used of carving runes into wood or stone.
items.cn: writan 意为刻划，用于把如尼文刻在木石上。

items.en: Germanic relatives include German reissen, to tear, showing the sense of cutting a surface.
items.cn: 日耳曼同源词包括德语 reissen「撕」，可见「划开表面」的本义。

items.en: When parchment replaced wood, the verb shifted to writing with a pen.
items.cn: 当羊皮纸取代木板，这个动词转而指用笔书写。

items.en: The old strong forms wrote and written survived, marking the word as very old.
items.cn: 古老的强变化形式 wrote 与 written 留存下来，说明这个词很老。

items.en: Modern usage adds typing and digital text, though nobody says the word has changed.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了打字与数字文本，但没人说这个词变了。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the writ- family and its phrases; the near-meaning group holds words for putting text down.
note.cn: 形近组沿 writ- 家族及其短语；近义组收表示落笔成文的词。

entries.definition: A person who writes; the agent noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「作者、作家」，本词加 -er。

entries.definition: The activity or the result, as in her writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「书写、著作」。

entries.definition: In text, not spoken; the past participle as adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「书面的」，过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: A formal written order from a court.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「书面命令」，法律用语。

entries.definition: To put a text or music together, more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「创作」，更正式，也多用于音乐。

entries.definition: To write a first version meant to be changed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「起草」，写的是待改的初稿。

entries.definition: To write something down quickly for memory.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「记下」，为记住而快速写下。

entries.definition: To produce text on a keyboard instead of a pen.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打字」，用键盘而非笔。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the scratching origin and the everyday phrasal verbs built on write.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「刻划」的来源，以及 write 构成的日常短语动词。

normal.en: Write once meant to scratch, and letters are still marks on a surface.
normal.cn: write 原意是刻划，字母至今仍是表面上的痕迹。

normal.en: Write down means record; write off means cancel; write up means finish neatly.
normal.cn: write down 是记下，write off 是勾销，write up 是整理成文。

normal.en: The past is wrote, the participle is written: both are old strong forms.
normal.cn: 过去式是 wrote，过去分词是 written，都是古老的强变化。

normal.en: A writer writes, writing is the work and the result.
normal.cn: writer 是写的人，writing 既是活儿也是成果。

normal.en: Write to somebody is British; Americans often write somebody.
normal.cn: write to somebody 是英式，美式常省略 to。

abstract.en: Writing began as scratching a surface so that a thought would outlast a voice.
abstract.cn: 书写始于在表面上刻划，好让想法比声音活得更久。

abstract.en: The word still carries the body: a hand, a tool and a surface, even when the surface is a screen.
abstract.cn: 这个词仍带着身体：一只手、一件工具、一个表面，即使表面成了屏幕。

abstract.en: To write is to leave a trace that someone else can pick up later, which is why it outlives us.
abstract.cn: 写作就是留下别人后来能拾起的痕迹，所以它比我们活得久。

examples.en: Write your address clearly on the envelope.
examples.cn: 信封上把地址写清楚。

examples.en: He writes a column for a weekly paper.
examples.cn: 他为一家周报写专栏。

examples.en: She wrote to thank them for their help.
examples.cn: 她写信感谢他们的帮助。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞特」——瑞（锐）特（别）认真地写：写

root: 古英语 writan「刻划」，日耳曼语同源，保留强变化形式 wrote、written；同族词有 writer、writing、written、writ。

sensesIntro.en: Write moves from forming letters, to composing, to sending a letter, recording facts and phrasal combinations.
sensesIntro.cn: write 从画出字母，走到撰写成篇、寄出信件、记录事实与短语组合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nib touching paper and the first hook of a letter appearing.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔尖触纸，第一道弯钩成形。

branches.en: HAND LINE: marks made with a tool.
branches.cn: 手部线：用工具留下的痕迹。

branches.en: MIND LINE: building a whole text.
branches.cn: 心智线：搭出一整篇文章。

branches.en: CONTACT LINE: reaching a person by post.
branches.cn: 联络线：通过邮政抵达某人。

branches.en: DATA LINE: recording, cancelling, finishing.
branches.cn: 数据线：记录、勾销、整理完。

branches.en: CONTRAST: to write letters needs a hand, to write a book needs years.
branches.cn: 对照线：写字只需一只手，写书需要许多年。

intro.en: Write is a bare Old English verb stem; English endings supply the nouns and the old participle.
intro.cn: write 是古英语动词词干本身，英语词尾提供名词与古老的分词形式。

latinIntro.en: No Latin; the word is Germanic, and script and scribe are the Latin family that English borrowed separately.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁成分，这个词是日耳曼语；script 与 scribe 才是英语另借的拉丁一支。

items.example: It appears in wrote and writ.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 wrote 与 writ。

definition_zh: 年；一年时间；年度；年级；岁（复数 years 表年龄）
definition_en: a period of twelve months, or the time the earth takes to go round the sun
core_image: 一截绳子围成一圈，两端接上，走过一圈又回到起点
scene: 墙上的日历翻到最后一页，第二天挂上了新的一本。The bridge took four years to build.
sceneCN: 这里 year 是「年」（第 1 个义项：十二个月为一周期）；句意为这座桥建了四年。走完一圈又回到起点的那条绳子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：年；一年时间；年度；年级；岁

derivatives.zh: 形容词或副词，义为「每年的、一年一度地」
名词，义为「一岁的幼畜」
名词，义为「年鉴、年刊」
形容词，义为「全年的、不歇业的」
名词，义为「年中」

senses.title: Twelve months
senses.titleCN: 一年：十二个月的周期
senses.definition: a period of twelve months
senses.definitionCN: 十二个月构成的时间段
senses.example: The bridge took four years to build.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥建了四年。
senses.why: The word copies the sun’s circle; a year is simply one turn of the earth’s orbit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词借了太阳转圈的形状：一年就是绕轨道走完一圈。

senses.title: A calendar period
senses.titleCN: 年度：日历上标号的那一年
senses.definition: a period counted on a calendar, numbered from a fixed point
senses.definitionCN: 在日历上编号的时段，从某个定点开始数
senses.example: The company was founded in 1998, a very good year.
senses.exampleCN: 公司创立于 1998 年，那是很顺的一年。
senses.why: Calendars cut the turning circle at a chosen point, so a year can start on any date.
senses.whyCN: 日历在选定的点上把圈切开，所以一年可以从任何一天开始。

senses.title: Age in years
senses.titleCN: 岁：用年来数年龄（复数）
senses.definition: in the plural, age measured in such periods
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式，用这一周期衡量年龄
senses.example: She is twelve years old and reads everything.
senses.exampleCN: 她十二岁，什么都读。
senses.why: Age is a count of completed circles, which is why we say twelve years, not twelve.
senses.whyCN: 年龄是已走完的圈数，所以要说 twelve years，不能只说十二。

senses.title: A school year
senses.titleCN: 学年：学校的一段教学期
senses.definition: the period of teaching in a school, shorter than a calendar year
senses.definitionCN: 学校的一段教学期，比日历年短
senses.example: The new school year begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 新学年九月开始。
senses.why: Schools cut the same circle at a different point, so their year starts in autumn.
senses.whyCN: 学校在同一个圈上换了个切口，所以它们的年从秋天开始。

senses.title: A long span
senses.titleCN: 很长时间（口语）
senses.definition: in the plural, a long time, often emphatically
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式，泛指很长时间，常带强调
senses.example: I have not seen them for years.
senses.exampleCN: 我好几年没见他们了。
senses.why: A plural of a unit is an easy way to say many, so years becomes a soft word for long.
senses.whyCN: 把一个单位变成复数就能轻松表示「很多」，于是 years 成了「很久」的软说法。

intro.en: Year is an old Germanic word for the turning of the seasons, related to the idea of a cycle.
intro.cn: year 是古老的日耳曼词，指季节的转动，带着「循环」的观念。

items.en: The noun gear meant year, and came from a root meaning to go or turn.
items.cn: 名词 gear 意为年，词根含「走、转」之义。

items.en: German Jahr and Dutch jaar show the same word across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 德语 Jahr 与荷兰语 jaar 展示了这个词在日耳曼诸语中的同形。

items.en: Old English poetry counted winters as well as years, both naming the cold turn.
items.cn: 古英语诗歌也数冬天，指的都是那一段寒冷时节。

items.en: Middle English spelled it yer or yeer before the modern form settled.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 yer 或 yeer，后来才定型为现代形式。

items.en: Modern usage numbers years from fixed points and measures ages by them.
items.cn: 现代用法从固定点给年份编号，并用它来量年龄。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the year- family; the near-meaning group holds other units and expressions of time.
note.cn: 形近组沿 year- 家族；近义组收其他时间单位与时间表达。

entries.definition: Once a year, or every year; the adverb and adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「每年的、一年一度地」。

entries.definition: An animal one year old, as in a yearling horse.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一岁的幼畜」。

entries.definition: A book recording one year, often a school’s.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「年鉴、年刊」。

entries.definition: Lasting the whole year, as in year-round service.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全年的」。

entries.definition: A twelfth of a year, following the moon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「月」，一年的十二分之一。

entries.definition: Ten years, a convenient block of years.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十年」，方便的年份块。

entries.definition: A hundred years, from the Latin word for hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「世纪」，一百年。

entries.definition: The cold season, once used to count the passing years.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冬天」，古时用来数年份。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the circle-of-the-sun idea and the everyday phrases with years.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「太阳转圈」的意象与含 year 的日常搭配。

normal.en: A year is one turn of the earth round the sun.
normal.cn: 一年是地球绕太阳走完的一圈。

normal.en: Year after year means again and again, without a break.
normal.cn: year after year 指年复一年、没有间断。

normal.en: Twelve years old means twelve completed turns.
normal.cn: twelve years old 指已经走完十二圈。

normal.en: A leap year adds a day to keep the calendar and the sun together.
normal.cn: 闰年加一天，让日历和太阳保持同步。

normal.en: Yearly adds -ly; years adds -s; both are regular English endings.
normal.cn: yearly 加 -ly，years 加 -s，都是常规英语词尾。

abstract.en: The year is nature’s unit and the calendar’s too, which is why it never quite fits both.
abstract.cn: 年既是自然的单位也是日历的单位，所以它总不能同时严丝合缝。

abstract.en: Counting years is counting returns: each one ends where it began, one step further out.
abstract.cn: 数年份就是数归来：每一圈都回到起点，又向外多走一步。

abstract.en: A life is not a single year but a stack of them, each with its own weather.
abstract.cn: 一生不是一年，而是一叠年，每一年都有自己的天气。

examples.en: The project has taken three years so far.
examples.cn: 这个项目到目前为止已经花了三年。

examples.en: Sales rose sharply last year.
examples.cn: 去年销量大幅上升。

examples.en: She has lived here for twenty years.
examples.cn: 她在这里住了二十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「叶」——叶子落一次就过一年：年

root: 古英语名词 gear「年」，词根含「走、转」，与德语 Jahr、荷兰语 jaar 同源；同族词有 yearly、yearling、yearbook。

sensesIntro.en: Year is a natural cycle, a numbered calendar block, a count of age, a school term or simply a long time.
sensesIntro.cn: year 是自然循环、编了号的日历块、年龄的计数、学校的学期，或仅仅是「很久」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope bent into a circle, its ends meeting and passing on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子围成一圈，两头相接又继续往前。

branches.en: SKY LINE: one orbit of the earth.
branches.cn: 天空线：地球绕行一圈。

branches.en: CALENDAR LINE: a year with a number and a start date.
branches.cn: 日历线：有编号、有起点的年份。

branches.en: BODY LINE: age counted in completed turns.
branches.cn: 身体线：按走完的圈数计年龄。

branches.en: USE LINE: a school year, or a phrase for ages.
branches.cn: 用途线：学年，或泛指多年。

branches.en: CONTRAST: the sun does not know where the calendar cuts.
branches.cn: 对照线：太阳并不知道日历在哪里切开。

intro.en: Year is a bare noun; its family is built with -ly, -ling and compounds.
intro.cn: year 是光名词，家族由 -ly、-ling 与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin here; year is Germanic, while annual comes from Latin annus.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分，year 是日耳曼词，而 annual 才出自拉丁 annus。

items.meaning: distance light travels in a year
items.example: It shows the word in science.
items.exampleCN: 它展示这个词在科学中的用法。

definition_zh: 黄色（的）；发黄的、泛黄的；形容词：胆怯的（口语）；（新闻）耸人听闻的
definition_en: of the colour of lemons or egg yolks, between green and orange
core_image: 一个切开摆在桌上的柠檬，果肉在光下亮得刺眼
scene: 秋天的银杏叶铺了一地，走过的人都放慢了脚步。The old letters had turned yellow with age.
sceneCN: 这里 yellow 是「发黄的」（第 2 个义项：颜色变旧变黄）；句意为旧信因年久而发黄。切开柠檬那种介于绿与橙之间的亮色，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：黄色的；发黄的；胆怯的（口语）
名词：黄色；蛋黄；（口语）胆怯
动词：使变黄；变黄

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「微黄的」，加 -ish 构成
名词，义为「黄色、发黄」
名词，义为「蛋黄」，与 yellow 同源的另一个词
名词，义为「金」，与 yellow 共享古老的「黄」根
形容词，义为「带黄色的」，口语，加 -y 构成

senses.title: The colour itself
senses.titleCN: 黄色：介于绿与橙之间的颜色
senses.definition: the colour of a lemon or an egg yolk
senses.definitionCN: 柠檬或蛋黄的颜色
senses.example: The leaves turn yellow in late autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 晚秋时节叶子变黄了。
senses.why: Old English geolu named this colour directly; it is one of the oldest colour words in English.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 geolu 直接命名这种颜色，是英语最古老的颜色词之一。

senses.title: Turned yellow by age
senses.titleCN: 发黄：旧了、老化的黄
senses.definition: grown yellow through age or damage
senses.definitionCN: 因年久或受损而变黄
senses.example: The old letters had turned yellow with age.
senses.exampleCN: 旧信因年久而发黄。
senses.why: The same colour becomes a sign of time, the way paper keeps its own clock.
senses.whyCN: 同一种颜色成了时间的标记，就像纸张有自己的钟。

senses.title: Cowardly
senses.titleCN: 胆怯的：口语里形容人没勇气
senses.definition: in informal use, cowardly or afraid
senses.definitionCN: 口语里形容胆怯、没勇气
senses.example: He was too yellow to say what he thought.
senses.exampleCN: 他太胆小，不敢说出自己的想法。
senses.why: The colour was attached to cowardice in old stories and the label stuck in speech.
senses.whyCN: 旧故事把这个颜色贴在胆怯上，这个标签在口语里留了下来。

senses.title: Sensational in the press
senses.titleCN: 耸人听闻的：夸张取宠的新闻
senses.definition: in phrases such as yellow press, describing sensational journalism
senses.definitionCN: 见于 yellow press 等短语，指耸人听闻的新闻
senses.example: The story was printed in the yellow press, not in a serious paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事登在耸人听闻的小报上，不是在严肃报纸上。
senses.why: In the 1890s a popular comic strip used yellow ink, and its name passed to the whole style of loud journalism.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪九十年代一份流行漫画用黄色油墨印刷，这个名字传给了整个喧闹的新闻风格。

intro.en: Yellow descends from Old English geolu, one of the words English has carried longest.
intro.cn: yellow 源自英语最古老的词之一 geolu。

items.en: Geolu meant yellow and is related to geolca, the yolk of an egg.
items.cn: geolu 意为黄色，与 geolca「蛋黄」相关。

items.en: The Germanic form gulwaz also gives German gelb and Dutch geel.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 gulwaz 也给出德语 gelb 与荷兰语 geel。

items.en: An older root related to gold and glow lies behind the colour word.
items.cn: 更古老的词根与 gold、glow 相关，藏在颜色词背后。

items.en: Middle English wrote yelwe or yelow, and the modern spelling settled later.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 yelwe 或 yelow，现代拼写定型更晚。

items.en: The word then grew figurative senses, first for cowardice, later for sensational press.
items.cn: 此后这个词长出比喻义，先指胆怯，后指耸人听闻的报纸。

note.en: The look-alike group collects colour words; the near-meaning group holds shades close to yellow.
note.cn: 形近组收颜色词；近义组收接近黄色的色调。

entries.definition: To shout loudly; only a spelling neighbour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「大喊」，只是拼写邻居。

entries.definition: The yellow centre of an egg, the closest relative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蛋黄」，最近的亲属。

entries.definition: The metal and colour, from the same ancient root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄金」，出自同一古老词根。

entries.definition: Slightly yellow; the adjective with -ish.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「微黄的」，本词加 -ish。

entries.definition: Of gold or its warm colour, richer than yellow.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「金色的」，比 yellow 更暖更浓。

entries.definition: The next colour along, warmer than yellow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「橙色」，比黄色更暖。

entries.definition: Lacking colour strength; yellow can be pale too.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浅的、苍白的」，黄也可以浅。

entries.definition: Ready to eat, often shown by a yellow skin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「成熟的」，常以黄皮为标志。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the lemon picture and the age sense that appears in old paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「柠檬」的画面，以及旧纸上出现的那种「发黄」。

normal.en: Yellow is one of the oldest colour words in English.
normal.cn: yellow 是英语里最古老的颜色词之一。

normal.en: A yellow card warns a player; a red card sends him off.
normal.cn: 黄牌警告球员，红牌罚下球员。

normal.en: Paper turns yellow because it ages, not because it was yellow before.
normal.cn: 纸发黄是因为老化，不是因为本来黄。

normal.en: Yellowish means a little yellow, with the soft -ish ending.
normal.cn: yellowish 指微微发黄，带柔化的 -ish。

normal.en: Calling someone yellow is an old insult about courage.
normal.cn: 说某人 yellow 是一句关于勇气的旧式侮辱。

abstract.en: Colour words are borrowed from things, so yellow always carries a lemon and a leaf behind it.
abstract.cn: 颜色词都从实物借来，所以 yellow 背后永远是柠檬与叶子。

abstract.en: The same colour can mark ripeness, age or fear, depending on what it is painted on.
abstract.cn: 同一种颜色可以标记成熟、衰老或恐惧，看它涂在什么上。

abstract.en: Seeing a colour is easy; the word for it is already a small history of objects.
abstract.cn: 看见颜色很容易，而给它的名字已经是一小段器物史。

examples.en: She wore a yellow coat to the party.
examples.cn: 她穿着一件黄色外套去参加聚会。

examples.en: The pages had yellowed at the edges.
examples.cn: 书页的边缘已经发黄。

examples.en: Fields of yellow flowers stretched to the river.
examples.cn: 黄色的花田一直延伸到河边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「叶落」——叶落时满地黄：黄色

root: 古英语 geolu「黄色」，与 geolca「蛋黄」相关，上溯日耳曼 gulwaz，与德语 gelb、荷兰语 geel 同源；同族词有 yellowish、yellowness。

sensesIntro.en: Yellow is a colour, the mark of ageing, a word for cowardice and a label for cheap sensation.
sensesIntro.cn: yellow 是一种颜色、衰老的标记、胆怯的代称，也是廉价煽情的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lemon cut open on a table, bright enough to squint at.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上切开的一只柠檬，亮得让人眯眼。

branches.en: COLOUR LINE: between green and orange.
branches.cn: 颜色线：介于绿与橙之间。

branches.en: TIME LINE: paper showing its age.
branches.cn: 时间线：纸露出年龄。

branches.en: COURAGE LINE: an old insult for fear.
branches.cn: 勇气线：对恐惧的旧式讥讽。

branches.en: PRESS LINE: news that shouts to be read.
branches.cn: 报纸线：大声叫卖的新闻。

branches.en: CONTRAST: yellow is the colour, yellowed is the change.
branches.cn: 对照线：yellow 是颜色，yellowed 是变黄。

intro.en: Yellow is a bare stem; -ish, -ness, -y and -er build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: yellow 是光词干，家族其余成员由 -ish、-ness、-y、-er 构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin enters; the word is Germanic, unlike colour names borrowed from French.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁成分，这个词是日耳曼的，与那些借自法语的颜色名不同。

definition_zh: 是、对、好（表示同意）；是的（回答肯定）；（用于句末）是不是、对不对；赞成票
definition_en: used to give an affirmative answer or to express agreement
core_image: 一个人点头，下巴落下又抬起，动作只有一个
scene: 桌上有人小声问「你确定吗」，对方只是点了点头。Yes, I understand what you mean.
sceneCN: 这里 yes 是「是、对」（第 1 个义项：表示同意或肯定）；句意为是的，我明白你的意思。点头那一下，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 感叹词：是、对、好（表示同意）
名词：肯定的回答、赞成票

derivatives.zh: 感叹词，义为「是」，口语里更随意的 yes
感叹词，义为「是」，美式口语，更轻快
感叹词，义为「赞成」，用于正式投票
名词，义为「唯唯诺诺的人」，由 yes 与 man 合成
副词，义为「否」，是正式投票中 yes 的对立面

senses.title: Agreeing
senses.titleCN: 同意：回答是肯定的
senses.definition: used to give a positive answer to a question
senses.definitionCN: 用来对问题作出肯定回答
senses.example: Yes, I understand what you mean.
senses.exampleCN: 是的，我明白你的意思。
senses.why: The word grew out of the old phrase gea si, so be it; agreement was originally a wish.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自旧短语 gea si「就这样吧」，同意原本是一种祝愿。

senses.title: Accepting an offer
senses.titleCN: 接受：对提议说好
senses.definition: used to accept an offer or invitation
senses.definitionCN: 用来接受提议或邀请
senses.example: Yes, please, I would love some tea.
senses.exampleCN: 好的，请给我来点茶，我很想喝。
senses.why: An offer is a question with a gift inside; yes takes the gift.
senses.whyCN: 提议是装着礼物的问句；yes 把礼物收下。

senses.title: Confirming a statement
senses.titleCN: 确认：对陈述加以肯定
senses.definition: used to confirm what someone has just said
senses.definitionCN: 用来确认别人刚说的话
senses.example: Yes, that is exactly what happened.
senses.exampleCN: 是的，事情正是这样。
senses.why: Confirming is the plainest form of yes: the speaker simply puts weight behind what was already said.
senses.whyCN: 确认是 yes 最朴素的形式：说话人只是给已经说过的话加一份分量。

senses.title: A tag question
senses.titleCN: 句尾反问：对不对、是不是
senses.definition: in speech, added at the end to invite agreement
senses.definitionCN: 口语中加在句末，以争取对方同意
senses.example: You are coming with us, yes?
senses.exampleCN: 你会和我们一起去，对吧？
senses.why: A question turns into an invitation when yes is tacked on; the asker already expects agreement.
senses.whyCN: 句末挂上 yes，问句就变成邀请：提问者其实已经期待对方同意。

senses.title: A vote in favour
senses.titleCN: 赞成票：作为名词的 yes
senses.definition: as a noun, a vote or answer in favour
senses.definitionCN: 作名词，指赞成的一票或肯定的回答
senses.example: There were twelve yeses and three noes.
senses.exampleCN: 有十二票赞成、三票反对。
senses.why: The interjection becomes a countable noun because a vote of this kind is counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 这个感叹词变成可数名词，因为这类票是一张一张数出来的。

intro.en: Yes comes from Old English gese, a blend of gea, so, with si, may it be so.
intro.cn: yes 来自古英语 gese，是 gea「是的」与 si「但愿如此」的融合。

items.en: Gea was the simple word for yes, answered to a direct question.
items.cn: gea 是简单的肯定词，用来回答直接问题。

items.en: Si meant so be it, a small wish added to agreement.
items.cn: si 意为「但愿如此」，是加在同意上的一个小小祝愿。

items.en: The two fused into gese, agreement spoken with a wish inside it.
items.cn: 两者融合为 gese，同意的说法里带着祝愿。

items.en: Middle English shortened it to yes, and kept yes and ye as polite variants for a while.
items.cn: 中古英语把它缩短为 yes，并在一段时间里保留 yes 与 ye 两种礼貌变体。

items.en: Modern usage adds the noun and the tag question, giving one word several jobs.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了名词与句尾反问，使这个词身兼数职。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other affirmatives; the near-meaning group holds ways of agreeing.
note.cn: 形近组收其他肯定词；近义组收表示同意的方式。

entries.definition: An informal yes, common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 感叹词，义为「是」，口语中的 informal 肯定。

entries.definition: A quick, casual yes, mostly American.
entries.definitionCN: 感叹词，义为「是」，快速随意的美式说法。

entries.definition: A formal yes in votes and in old dialect.
entries.definitionCN: 感叹词，义为「赞成」，用于投票与旧方言。

entries.definition: The day before today; only a spelling neighbour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「昨天」，只是拼写邻居。

entries.definition: A firm yes, with confidence added.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「当然」，加了确定感。

entries.definition: A strong yes, often enthusiastic.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「绝对」，常带热情。

entries.definition: A casual yes in speech, sometimes hesitant.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「当然」，口语里有时略显犹豫。

entries.definition: The refusal, the opposite of yes.
entries.definitionCN: 感叹词，义为「不」，yes 的对立面。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the nodding gesture and the small wish inside the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用点头的动作与藏在词里的那点祝愿。

normal.en: Yes and no together means the answer is mixed.
normal.cn: yes and no 一起用，表示答案兼有两者。

normal.en: Say yes means agree, and it commits you.
normal.cn: say yes 就是同意，而且是一种承诺。

normal.en: A yes vote counts in favour; a no would count against.
normal.cn: a yes vote 是赞成票，相反的票则反对。

normal.en: Yeah and yep are the same word with less breath.
normal.cn: yeah 与 yep 是同一个词，只是更省气。

normal.en: Yes at the end of a sentence asks the other person to agree.
normal.cn: 句末的 yes 是在请对方一起同意。

abstract.en: Yes is the shortest act of consent, and it always closes a question.
abstract.cn: yes 是最短的同意之举，它总在关上一个问题。

abstract.en: The word began as a wish, which is why answering yes can feel like a promise.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于一个祝愿，所以回答 yes 常常像是一种承诺。

abstract.en: A whole vote, a whole decision, can hang on two letters said in one breath.
abstract.cn: 整整一票、整整一个决定，可能就挂在一次呼吸间说出的两个字母上。

examples.en: Yes, the meeting is at nine.
examples.cn: 是的，会议九点开始。

examples.en: She said yes to the job offer.
examples.cn: 她接受了那份工作。

examples.en: You have finished, yes?
examples.cn: 你已经做完了，对吧？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「耶死」——耶，死了也要答应：是

root: 古英语 gese，由 gea「是的」与 si「但愿如此」融合而成，中古英语缩短为 yes；同族词有 yeah、yep、aye。

sensesIntro.en: Yes answers, accepts, confirms, invites agreement and even counts votes.
sensesIntro.cn: yes 可以作答、接受、确认、争取赞同，甚至计入票数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single nod, chin down and up again.
core.cn: 核心意象：点一下头，下巴落下又抬起。

branches.en: ANSWER LINE: a positive reply to a question.
branches.cn: 回答线：对问题的肯定回复。

branches.en: OFFER LINE: taking what is offered.
branches.cn: 给予线：收下递来的东西。

branches.en: SPEECH LINE: a tag inviting the other to agree.
branches.cn: 口语线：句尾请对方一同同意。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: a vote on the yes side.
branches.cn: 计数线：赞成那边的一票。

branches.en: CONTRAST: yes answers, no refuses; both end the question.
branches.cn: 对照线：yes 答应，no 拒绝，两者都结束问题。

intro.en: Yes is a whole word with no affixes; its shorter forms are separate spellings, not endings.
intro.cn: yes 是完整单词，没有词缀，它的短形是另立的拼写而非词尾。

latinIntro.en: Nothing Latin here; the word is native English from the earliest records.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分，从最早文献起它就是英语本土词。

items.example: It shows the word in a compound.
items.exampleCN: 它展示这个词的合成用法。

items.example: It shows the word in use.

definition_zh: 昨天；昨日；名词：过去、往昔
definition_en: the day before today, or the recent past
core_image: 撕掉一页日历，纸角还卷在垃圾桶边
scene: 奶奶翻着相册说，昨天的事好像就在眼前。Yesterday we walked all the way to the river.
sceneCN: 这里 yesterday 是「昨天」（第 1 个义项：今天之前的那一天）；句意为昨天我们一路走到河边。撕掉的那页日历，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：昨天；过去、往昔（前面的日子）
副词：在昨天

collocations.zh: 就在不久前；仿佛就在昨天

derivatives.zh: 古英语「昨天的」前缀，只见于 yesterday 等少数词
由 yester 与 year 合成，义为「往年、旧时光」

senses.title: The day before today
senses.titleCN: 昨天：今天之前的那一天
senses.definition: the day that came just before today
senses.definitionCN: 紧接在今天之前的那一天
senses.example: She called me yesterday about the tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 她昨天给我打电话说票的事。
senses.why: Old English geostran meant yesterday and dæg meant day; the two were welded into one word naming the single day behind us.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 geostran 意为「昨天」、dæg 意为「日子」，两者焊成一个词，专指我们身后那唯一的一天。

senses.title: The adverb of that day
senses.titleCN: 副词：在那一天发生
senses.definition: on the day before today
senses.definitionCN: 在今天之前的那一天（作状语）
senses.example: It rained hard yesterday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 昨天下午雨下得很大。
senses.why: The same form serves as a time adverbial because English rarely changes shape between a day-name and when it happened.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形式可作时间状语，因为英语里表示某天和表示某天发生，形状几乎不变。

senses.title: The recent past
senses.titleCN: 往昔：不久前的过去
senses.definition: the time not long ago, seen as already past
senses.definitionCN: 被视为已经成为过去的、不远的时间
senses.example: Yesterday's heroes are often forgotten today.
senses.exampleCN: 昨天的英雄今天常被遗忘。
senses.why: People turn the calendar word into a metaphor: whatever is past is called yesterday, however long ago it was.
senses.whyCN: 人们把这个日历词变成比喻：凡是过去的都叫昨天，无论隔了多久。

senses.title: A word of change
senses.titleCN: 变化之词：形容迅速过时
senses.definition: used to mark something as quickly out of date
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示某事物很快过时
senses.example: This phone is already yesterday's technology.
senses.exampleCN: 这款手机已经是昨天的技术了。
senses.why: If yesterday is the past, then calling something yesterday's marks it as behind the present, a compact way to say outdated.
senses.whyCN: 既然昨天就是过去，说某物是昨天的，就等于说它落在当下之后，是「过时」的简洁说法。

intro.en: Yesterday is a native English compound, older than any Latin borrowing in this book.
intro.cn: yesterday 是英语本土合成的词，比本书中任何拉丁借词都古老。

items.en: Geostran was the old word for the day just past; its root reached back to a Germanic base for yesterday.
items.cn: Geostran 是表示刚过去那一天的旧词，其词根可追溯到日耳曼语表示昨天的词干。

items.en: Dæg meant day, the ancestor of modern day.
items.cn: Dæg 意为「日子」，是现代 day 的祖先。

items.en: The two words were joined into geostrandæg, naming the single day behind the speaker.
items.cn: 两词合为 geostrandæg，专门指说话人身后的那一天。

items.en: Spelling shifted to yesterday as unstressed syllables wore down.
items.cn: 随着非重读音节弱化，拼写逐渐变成 yesterday。

items.en: The word gained a figurative life: yesterday now also means any recent past that is over.
items.cn: 这个词获得了比喻义：yesterday 现在还指任何已经结束的近过去。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers time words of the same yester- family or shape; the near-meaning group gathers other markers of past time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 yester- 族或形状相近的时间词；近义组收其他表示过去时间的词。

entries.definition: The years of the past, a literary synonym built on yester-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「往年、旧时光」，是用 yester- 构成的文学化同义词。

entries.definition: This day; built the same way from a time word plus day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或副词，义为「今天」，同样由时间词加 day 构成。

entries.definition: The day after today, the mirror image of yesterday.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或副词，义为「明天」，是 yesterday 的镜像词。

entries.definition: A period of twenty-four hours or the hours of light.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一天、白天」，是构成 yesterday 的词之一。

entries.definition: Before now, without naming a particular day.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「先前」，不指明具体哪一天。

entries.definition: In earlier times, used of a state that has ended.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「从前」，用于已结束的状态。

entries.definition: The night just before this one, a fixed time phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「昨晚」，是固定的时间短语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks break the word into the two old pieces it was made of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把这个词拆成它原来的两个古老部件。

normal.en: yester- is the old word for the past, and day is day: yesterday is the past day.
normal.cn: yester- 是表示过去的古词，day 是日子：yesterday 就是过去的那一天。

normal.en: The day before yesterday is one step further back, so the phrase grows longer.
normal.cn: 前天是再往回一步，所以这个短语更长。

normal.en: Only yesterday means it feels like no time at all has passed.
normal.cn: only yesterday 意为仿佛没过多久。

normal.en: Yesterday's news is old news: the word itself carries the idea of being past.
normal.cn: yesterday's news 就是旧闻：这个词本身就带着「已过去」的意思。

normal.en: Compare today, yesterday, tomorrow — three cards laid in a row.
normal.cn: 把 today、yesterday、tomorrow 摆成一排，就是三张卡片。

abstract.en: A calendar page torn off and dropped: what is gone is yesterday.
abstract.cn: 撕下丢掉的日历页：已经过去的就是昨天。

abstract.en: Time as a road behind you: the part you already walked is yesterday.
abstract.cn: 时间为身后的路：已经走过的那段就是昨天。

abstract.en: A worn word whose two halves still show, like an old coin with two faces.
abstract.cn: 一个旧词的两半仍清晰可见，像一枚两面都有图案的老硬币。

examples.en: Yesterday was the coldest day of the month.
examples.cn: 昨天是这个月最冷的一天。

examples.en: I met her yesterday at the station, and she still had the yellow umbrella.
examples.cn: 我昨天在车站遇到她，她还拿着那把黄伞。

examples.en: He speaks of his childhood as if it were yesterday.
examples.cn: 他谈起童年，仿佛就在昨天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「叶斯特 day」——叶斯特的那一天，就是昨天。

root: 古英语 geostran（昨天）+ dæg（日子）

sensesIntro.en: From a plain calendar word to a metaphor for anything past.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个朴素的日历词，延伸为任何已过去之事的比喻。

core.en: the day behind us
core.cn: 我们身后的那一天

branches.en: CALENDAR LINE: the single day before today.
branches.cn: 日历线：今天之前的那一天。

branches.en: GRAMMAR LINE: the same day used as a time adverb.
branches.cn: 语法线：同一天用作时间状语。

branches.en: MEMORY LINE: the past seen as a place behind us.
branches.cn: 记忆线：被看成身后之处的过去。

branches.en: LABEL LINE: what is out of date is called yesterday's.
branches.cn: 标签线：过时的东西被叫作昨天的。

branches.en: CONTRAST: today points forward, yesterday points back.
branches.cn: 对照线：today 朝前，yesterday 朝后。

intro.en: yesterday is a native compound rather than a Latin-based word, so its parts are listed as English building blocks.
intro.cn: yesterday 是两个更古老的部件合成的本土词，而非拉丁借词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin affixes are involved here, so nothing is listed as Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词缀，故不列拉丁条目。

items.example: It survives mainly in yesterday and yesteryear.
items.exampleCN: 它主要保留在 yesterday 与 yesteryear 中。

items.example: It is the same day we still use.
items.exampleCN: 它就是今天仍在用的 day。
它与 yester- 组成 yesteryear。

items.example: It is built on the same pattern.
Yesterday news soon becomes old news.
items.exampleCN: 昨天的新闻很快变成旧闻。

definition_zh: 产出、出产（粮食、收成）；屈服、让步；让路（交通）；名词：产量、收益
definition_en: to produce a crop or result, to give way, or the amount produced
core_image: 一棵压弯了枝的苹果树，果子垂到人手里
scene: 公路口立着一块牌子：前方施工，请让行。These fields yield two crops a year.
sceneCN: 这里 yield 是「出产」（第 1 个义项：田里长出作物）；句意为这些田地一年出产两季作物。被果子压弯的树枝，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：出产、产生；屈服、让步；让路；弯曲、塌陷
名词：产量、收成；收益、利润率

collocations.phrase: give way / yield the right of way

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「柔软的；顺从的；出产的」
在 yielding 后加 -ly，义为「柔顺地」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不屈的、坚硬的」
近义词，义为「产量」，侧重产出量而非动作

senses.title: To produce from the land
senses.titleCN: 出产：土地长出作物
senses.definition: to produce a crop, a natural product or a result
senses.definitionCN: 生产出作物、天然产物或结果
senses.example: The orchard yields a good crop of pears each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这片果园每年秋天都出产好收成。
senses.why: The oldest sense is of the earth giving its fruit; the ground hands over what it grew.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是土地献出果实：土地把长出来的东西交出来。

senses.title: To give way
senses.titleCN: 屈服：向压力让步
senses.definition: to stop resisting and accept what is stronger
senses.definitionCN: 停止抵抗，接受更强的一方
senses.example: The government finally yielded to public pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 政府最终屈服于公众压力。
senses.why: From giving fruit, the word moved to giving ground: a defended position is handed over to the opponent.
senses.whyCN: 从献出果实到让出地面：防守的阵地被交给对手。

senses.title: To let others pass
senses.titleCN: 让行：交通中让别人先过
senses.definition: to allow other traffic to go first
senses.definitionCN: 在交通中让别人先行
senses.example: Cars must yield to pedestrians at this crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个路口，车辆必须给行人让行。
senses.why: This is the road version of giving way: one driver hands over the right to move first.
