senses.whyCN: 这是「让」的道路版本：一位司机把先行的权利交出去。

senses.title: The amount produced
senses.titleCN: 产量：产出的数量
senses.definition: the quantity produced, as of crops or goods
senses.definitionCN: 出产的数量，如作物或产品
senses.example: Farmers worried about a lower rice yield this year.
senses.exampleCN: 农民担心今年水稻产量降低。
senses.why: The noun simply measures the verb: how much the land or the machine gave over.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是在度量动词：土地或机器交出了多少。

senses.title: The return on money
senses.titleCN: 收益：投资带来的回报
senses.definition: the profit or income produced by an investment
senses.definitionCN: 投资所产生的利润或收入
senses.example: The bond offers a yield of four percent.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券提供百分之四的收益率。
senses.why: Money, like soil, can be made to yield; the return is the fruit of capital.
senses.whyCN: 钱也像土壤一样能出产；回报就是资本的果实。

senses.title: To bend or give under weight
senses.titleCN: 弯曲、塌陷：在重压下让开
senses.definition: to bend, break or give way under force
senses.definitionCN: 在受力时弯曲、断裂或塌陷
senses.example: The old chair yielded under his weight.
senses.exampleCN: 那把旧椅子在他的重量下塌了下去。
senses.why: Physical giving way: a solid thing stops resisting the load and moves aside.
senses.whyCN: 物理意义上的让：坚固之物不再抵抗重量，让开了。

intro.en: Yield descends from Old English gieldan, a Germanic word for paying what is due.
intro.cn: yield 源自古英语 gieldan，是日耳曼语中表示「付出应付之物」的词。

items.en: Gieldan meant to pay, to repay, or to give up what is owed.
items.cn: Gieldan 意为支付、偿还或交出应付之物。

items.en: The noun gield named a payment or a due amount.
items.cn: 名词 gield 指一笔付款或应付的数额。

items.en: The sense widened from paying money to giving up ground and producing crops.
items.cn: 词义从付钱扩大到让出地面和出产作物。

items.en: In agriculture and trade it settled as the regular word for output and return.
items.cn: 在农业与贸易中，它固定为表示产量与回报的常用词。

items.en: Traffic rules and finance both use it: yield the right of way, and yield on a bond.
items.cn: 交通规则与金融都用它：让行，以及债券的收益率。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers Germanic words with similar spelling and sound; the near-meaning group separates the several senses of giving.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写与读音相似的本土词；近义组按「让」的不同含义区分。

entries.definition: An area of open land; shares the -ield ending but not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「田地」，与 yield 只是尾音相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: A protective piece of armour or a guard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「盾牌、保护」，形状相似。

entries.definition: An old verb meaning to castrate, from the same Germanic base as yield.
entries.definitionCN: 古动词，义为「阉割」，与 yield 同出日耳曼语词干。

entries.definition: An association of craftsmen; spelled alike but a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行会」，拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: To stop fighting and hand over control, more military than yield.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投降、交出」，比 yield 更有军事色彩。

entries.definition: To accept authority or a decision, a more formal yielding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提交、屈从」，是更正式的让步。

entries.definition: To make or grow something, the plain verb behind sense one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「生产、生长」，对应第 1 个义项。

entries.definition: The amount made; a neutral noun for yield in industry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「产量」，工业语境里是中性的同义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the farm picture to the road and the bank.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把田里的画面连到马路和银行。

normal.en: A field that gives fruit yields; the same word gives ground when you yield in traffic.
normal.cn: 出果子的田地叫 yield；在交通里让出地面也是 yield。

normal.en: To yield to pressure is to hand over your resistance like a crop handed over.
normal.cn: 屈服于压力，就像把作物交出去一样交出抵抗。

normal.en: Yield sign at a crossing: you give the right of way, not the argument.
normal.cn: 路口的让行标志：让的是先行权，不是道理。

normal.en: A bond's yield is the fruit of your money.
normal.cn: 债券的 yield 就是你的钱结的果。

normal.en: The old chair yielded: it gave up its shape under him.
normal.cn: 旧椅子 yielded：它在他身下放弃了原来的形状。

abstract.en: One idea under all senses: something holds, then lets go and hands over.
abstract.cn: 所有义项背后只有一个想法：先坚持，然后松手交出。

abstract.en: Earth gives fruit, people give ground, money gives return.
abstract.cn: 土地给果实，人让出地面，钱给出回报。

abstract.en: Picture the bend: a branch loaded with apples leans down to your hand.
abstract.cn: 想那个弯曲：挂满苹果的枝条弯到你的手边。

examples.en: The new farming method yielded twice as much wheat.
examples.cn: 新的耕作方法使小麦产量翻倍。

examples.en: She refused to yield on the question of safety.
examples.cn: 在安全问题上她拒不让步。

examples.en: Drivers must yield to cyclists at the roundabout.
examples.cn: 在环岛处司机必须给骑行者让行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一有得」——田里一有得，就是出产、有收成。

root: 古英语 gieldan（支付、交出）

sensesIntro.en: One Germanic verb of handing over runs through farm, road and bank.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「交出」的日耳曼动词，贯穿田间、马路与银行。

core.en: to give over what one has
core.cn: 把自己有的东西交出去

branches.en: HARVEST LINE: the land gives its crop and the amount is counted.
branches.cn: 收成线：土地交出作物，数量被计量。

branches.en: PRESSURE LINE: resistance stops and control is handed over.
branches.cn: 压力线：抵抗停止，主动权交出。

branches.en: ROAD LINE: one driver lets another go first.
branches.cn: 道路线：一位司机让别人先行。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: capital produces a return.
branches.cn: 资金线：资本产生回报。

branches.en: WEIGHT LINE: a solid thing bends under a load.
branches.cn: 重量线：坚固之物在重压下弯曲。

intro.en: yield is a native Germanic word, so its parts are listed as English building blocks rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: yield 是日耳曼语本土词，这里把各部件当作英语构词块列出。

latinIntro.en: No Latin affixes are involved here, so nothing is listed as Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词缀，故不列拉丁条目。

items.example: Yielding describes what gives way easily.
items.exampleCN: yielding 形容容易让开的东西。

items.example: It looks like yield but means a guard.
items.exampleCN: 它形似 yield，但意思是盾。

definition_zh: 你；你们；（泛指）人们、任何人
definition_en: the person or people spoken to, or people in general
core_image: 隔着桌子，有人抬起手指向你
scene: 老师在讲台上说：你们要记住，光靠背是不够的，一定要自己动手核对。
sceneCN: 这里 you 是「你们」（第 2 个义项：对话中被称呼的一群人）；句意为老师提醒在座的学生不要只靠背诵、要亲手核对。有人用手指向对方，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 代词：你；你们；（泛指）人们

derivatives.zh: you 的所有格形式，义为「你的、你们的」
you 的名词性所有格，义为「你的（东西）」
you 的反身形式，义为「你自己」
you 的复数反身形式，义为「你们自己」

senses.title: The person spoken to
senses.titleCN: 你：对话中的对方（单数）
senses.definition: the one person being spoken to
senses.definitionCN: 正被说话的那一个人
senses.example: You left your keys on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 你把钥匙落在桌上了。
senses.why: This is the oldest function of the word: a pronoun pointing straight at the listener.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的功能：一个直接指向听者的代词。

senses.title: The people spoken to
senses.titleCN: 你们：对话中的一群人
senses.definition: the group of people being addressed
senses.definitionCN: 正被说话的那一群人
senses.example: You all need to hand in the form today.
senses.exampleCN: 你们今天都要交这张表。
senses.why: English uses one form for one hearer or many; only context or added all shows the plural.
senses.whyCN: 英语不管听者是一个还是一群都用同一个形式，靠语境或加 all 才看出复数。

senses.title: People in general
senses.titleCN: 泛指：人们、任何人
senses.definition: any person, including the speaker, in general statements
senses.definitionCN: 在一般陈述中指包括说话人在内的任何人
senses.example: You never know what will happen next.
senses.exampleCN: 你永远不知道接下来会发生什么。
senses.why: By addressing the hearer, the speaker invites anyone to imagine themselves in the case.
senses.whyCN: 通过称呼听者，说话人邀请任何人把自己代入这个情形。

senses.title: Formal singular
senses.titleCN: 尊称：正式的「您」
senses.definition: the polite form used in older or very formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 在旧式或极正式书面语中表示尊称
senses.example: Will you be so kind as to wait here, sir?
senses.exampleCN: 先生，您可否在此稍候？
senses.why: The old polite distinction lived in thou and you; you won and now serves every level of respect.
senses.whyCN: 旧的尊称区分在 thou 与 you 之间；you 胜出，如今承担所有敬谦层次。

intro.en: You is the survival of an Old English pronoun pair, whose polite branch took over both.
intro.cn: you 是古英语一对代词中留存下来的一个，而其中表尊称的一支通吃了两者。

items.en: Þū was the singular thou for one person, familiar in tone.
items.cn: Þū 是单数 thou，用于一个人，语气亲近。

items.en: Ēow was the object form of the plural pronoun you, meaning to you all.
items.cn: Ēow 是复数代词的宾格形式，意为「给你们」。

items.en: English kept ye for the subject and you for the object, then levelled them.
items.cn: 中古英语把 ye 用作主语、you 用作宾语，后来两者合并。

items.en: French and Latin habit made you the polite form even to one person.
items.cn: 受法语与拉丁语习惯影响，you 变成即使对一个人也用的尊称。

items.en: You drove out thou completely, so one word now covers you, you all and people in general.
items.cn: you 彻底挤掉了 thou，如今一个词兼指你、你们与人们。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers pronouns of the same family; the near-meaning group gathers ways of saying people in general.
note.cn: 形近组收同一族代词；近义组收泛指人们的各种说法。

entries.definition: The possessive form, used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 物主限定词，义为「你的」，用在名词前。

entries.definition: The possessive pronoun standing alone for your things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词性物主代词，义为「你的东西」。

entries.definition: The old singular, now archaic outside dialects.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语单数「你」，除方言外已成古语。

entries.definition: The old plural subject form, now archaic.
entries.definitionCN: 旧的复数主格形式，今已成古语。

entries.definition: A formal, impersonal way to say people in general.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「一个人、人们」，是正式的泛指说法。

entries.definition: First person plural, which sometimes includes the reader.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「我们」，有时包含读者。

entries.definition: Every person without exception, more explicit than you.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「每个人」，比泛指的 you 更明确。

entries.definition: The plain noun for persons in general.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「人们」，是最朴素的泛指。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the pronoun to its whole family of forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把这个代词和它的整个形式家族连起来。

normal.en: you, your, yours, yourself: one family, four jobs.
normal.cn: you、your、yours、yourself：一家四口，各司其职。

normal.en: You threw thou out: the polite form won and became the only one.
normal.cn: you 把 thou 挤走了：尊称取胜，成了唯一的说法。

normal.en: Thank you and see you: the pronoun lives in fixed everyday phrases.
normal.cn: thank you 和 see you：这个代词活在固定的日常短语里。

normal.en: You never know: the same word quietly means anyone.
normal.cn: you never know：同一个词悄悄变成了「任何人」的意思。

normal.en: Say it aloud — it is the sound of two vowels sliding together.
normal.cn: 大声念出来：它是两个元音滑在一起的声音。

abstract.en: A pointing finger: the word exists only in a conversation.
abstract.cn: 一根指向的手指：这个词只存在于对话之中。

abstract.en: A door that opens to anyone when the speaker says you.
abstract.cn: 说话人一说 you，这扇门就向任何人打开。

abstract.en: One form replacing two: like a single key that now opens every door.
abstract.cn: 一个形式取代两个：像一把能开所有门的钥匙。

examples.en: You should read the whole page before you sign.
examples.cn: 签字之前你应该把整页读完。

examples.en: Do you two want to come with us?
examples.cn: 你们俩想跟我们一起来吗？

examples.en: You can never tell how a small choice will end.
examples.cn: 很小的选择会有什么结果，你是永远说不准的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优」——夸人先说「你很优」，you 就是你。

root: 古英语 þū（你）与 ēow（你们），均源自日耳曼语代词词干

sensesIntro.en: One pronoun grew until it took over every way of saying you.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个代词不断扩张，最终包揽了所有说「你」的方式。

core.en: the one addressed
core.cn: 被称呼的那一方

branches.en: SINGLE LINE: one hearer is named.
branches.cn: 单数线：指名一个听者。

branches.en: PLURAL LINE: the same form covers a whole group.
branches.cn: 复数线：同一形式覆盖一群人。

branches.en: GENERAL LINE: the hearer stands for anyone.
branches.cn: 泛指线：听者代表任何人。

branches.en: CEREMONY LINE: the old polite use survives in formal writing.
branches.cn: 礼仪线：旧的尊称用法保留在正式书面语中。

branches.en: CONTRAST: one word shifts between one person and all people.
branches.cn: 对照线：一个词在一个人和所有人之间滑动。

intro.en: you is a native pronoun; its forms are inflections rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: you 是本土代词，其相关形式是词形变化而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin affixes are involved here, so nothing is listed as Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词缀，故不列拉丁条目。

items.example: Your book is on the table.

definition_zh: 年轻的、年幼的；初期的、新兴的；名词：幼崽（the young）
definition_en: in an early stage of life or development; not old
core_image: 一枚刚冒出土的嫩芽，叶尖还卷着
scene: 清晨的公园里，几个孩子追着一只小狗跑过草地。She is two years younger than her brother.
sceneCN: 这里 young 是「更年轻的」（第 1 个义项：年龄较小的比较级用法）；句意为她比哥哥小两岁。刚冒出、叶尖还卷着的嫩芽，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：年轻的、年幼的；初期的、新兴的
名词（the young）：幼崽、年轻人（集合名词）

derivatives.zh: 同一日耳曼词根的名词，义为「青春；青年；年轻人」
在 youth 后加 -ful，义为「年轻的、有朝气的」
加后缀 -ster 构成，义为「小孩、年轻人」
加后缀 -ish 构成，义为「还算年轻的」

senses.title: In early life
senses.titleCN: 年轻的：年龄小
senses.definition: having lived or existed for only a short time
senses.definitionCN: 生活或存在的时间还不长
senses.example: The young trees were planted last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这些幼树是去年春天栽下的。
senses.why: The core sense is time lived: few years, therefore young.
senses.whyCN: 核心含义是活过的年数：年数少，所以年轻。

senses.title: Early in development
senses.titleCN: 初期的：新兴的、还在发展
senses.definition: in an early stage of growth or existence
senses.definitionCN: 处于成长或存在的早期阶段
senses.example: The internet was still young in those years.
senses.exampleCN: 那些年里互联网还很年轻。
senses.why: Anything in its first stage shares the picture of the sprout, even a whole industry.
senses.whyCN: 任何处于第一阶段的事物都共享嫩芽的画面，哪怕整个行业也一样。

senses.title: The offspring of animals
senses.titleCN: 幼崽：动物的子女
senses.definition: the babies of an animal, taken as a group
senses.definitionCN: 动物的幼崽，作为集合名词
senses.example: The bird feeds its young in the nest.
senses.exampleCN: 这只鸟在巢里喂养幼鸟。
senses.why: The adjective used as a noun gathers all the little ones into one class.
senses.whyCN: 形容词当名词用，把所有小的个体收成一个类别。

senses.title: Young in spirit
senses.titleCN: 心态年轻：与年龄无关
senses.definition: having the energy or outlook of youth whatever one's age
senses.definitionCN: 不论年龄多大，都有年轻人的精力或心态
senses.example: Grandpa is seventy but still young at heart.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷七十岁了，但心态还年轻。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from years to feeling; youth becomes a quality rather than a number.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从年数转向感觉：年轻变成一种品质，而不是数字。

senses.title: Inexperienced
senses.titleCN: 稚嫩的：缺乏经验
senses.definition: lacking experience in a job or field
senses.definitionCN: 在某项工作或领域里经验不足
senses.example: He was too young in the trade to lead the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这行还太稚嫩，带不了这个团队。
senses.why: Few years in life become few years in a skill: inexperience borrows the word for age.
senses.whyCN: 生活上的年数少，变成技能上的年数少：缺乏经验借用了表示年龄的词。

intro.en: Young goes back to a Germanic word whose root also gave Latin iuvenis.
intro.cn: young 源自一个日耳曼语词，其词根也产生了拉丁语 iuvenis。

items.en: The Germanic base junga- meant young, used of people and animals alike.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词干 junga- 意为年轻，人和动物都用。

items.en: Old English geong was the inherited adjective, common in poetry.
items.cn: 古英语 geong 是继承下来的形容词，诗歌中常见。

items.en: The initial consonant softened and the spelling became yong.
items.cn: 词首辅音弱化，拼写变为 yong。

items.en: Spelling settled as young; youth and youthful grew as noun forms.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 young；youth 与 youthful 作为名词形式发展起来。

items.en: The word widened to new industries and to a state of mind.
items.cn: 词义扩展到新兴行业与心态。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Germanic age family; the near-meaning group gathers synonyms with different shades.
note.cn: 形近组收表示年龄的本土词族；近义组收色彩不同的同义词。

entries.definition: The time of being young, or young people as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春；青年（集合）」。

entries.definition: A child or a young person, informal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小孩、年轻人」，偏口语。

entries.definition: Having the qualities of youth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有青春气息的」。

entries.definition: Latin-related and formal, used of the young or the childish.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「少年的」，与拉丁语同源、更为正式。

entries.definition: Recently made, stressing newness rather than age.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「新的」，强调新而非年龄。

entries.definition: Recently arrived or produced, often positive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「新鲜的、刚来的」。

entries.definition: Not fully developed, often critical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不成熟的」，常带批评意味。

entries.definition: Between child and adult, a technical age band.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「青春期的」，是技术性的年龄段。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build on the sprout image and the comparison forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子建立在嫩芽画面和比较级形式上。

normal.en: Younger and youngest: two children standing side by side, the taller one behind.
normal.cn: younger 与 youngest：两个孩子并排站，高的那个退后半步。

normal.en: The young of a bird are its chicks; the adjective becomes a group noun.
normal.cn: 鸟的 young 就是雏鸟：形容词变成了集合名词。

normal.en: Young at heart: the years say old, the smile says young.
normal.cn: young at heart：年数说老，笑容说年轻。

normal.en: A young industry is one just planted, like a sapling in a new park.
normal.cn: young industry 是刚栽下的行业，像新公园里的小树苗。

normal.en: Young in the trade: too few years doing the job.
normal.cn: young in the trade：做这行的年头太少。

abstract.en: A green shoot unrolling: time lived, not time remembered.
abstract.cn: 一卷展开的绿芽：是活过的时光，不是记住的时光。

abstract.en: Age as a measuring line: young stands at the near end.
abstract.cn: 年龄像一条标尺：young 站在最近的那一端。

abstract.en: The same word for trees, countries and hearts shows a single idea of beginning.
abstract.cn: 树、国家、心都用同一个词，说明背后只有「开始」这一个想法。

examples.en: Many young people move to the city for work.
examples.cn: 许多年轻人为了工作搬到城里。

examples.en: The young of this species stay with their mother for a year.
examples.cn: 这种动物的幼崽会和母亲待一年。

examples.en: Though he is old, he stays young by learning new things.
examples.cn: 虽然年纪大了，他靠学新东西保持年轻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「秧」——田里刚插下的秧很嫩，young 就是年轻。

root: 日耳曼语 junga-（年轻），与拉丁语 iuvenis 同源

sensesIntro.en: From years of life to the first stage of anything, and then to a habit of mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 从生命的年数，到任何事物的第一阶段，再到一种心态。

core.en: early in time
core.cn: 时间上的早期

branches.en: LIFE LINE: people, animals and plants at an early age.
branches.cn: 生命线：人、动物与植物处在幼小阶段。

branches.en: GROWTH LINE: a field or an industry just started.
branches.cn: 成长线：刚起步的领域或行业。

branches.en: TRADE LINE: too few years doing a job.
branches.cn: 行业线：做某行的年头太少。

branches.en: HEART LINE: youth as a state of mind.
branches.cn: 心态线：作为心态的年轻。

branches.en: CONTRAST: old measures time lived, not time valued.
branches.cn: 对照线：old 度量的是活过的年头，而非被珍视的时光。

intro.en: young is a native Germanic word; the affixes below are the English ones it takes.
intro.cn: young 是日耳曼语本土词，下面列的是它承接的英语词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin affixes are involved here, so nothing is listed as Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词缀，故不列拉丁条目。

items.example: He is the youngest of three.
items.exampleCN: 他是三个孩子中最小的。

items.example: It makes youth from a related stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由相关词干构成 youth。

items.example: Youth is the noun twin of young.
items.exampleCN: youth 是 young 的名词孪生词。

definition_zh: 你的；你们的；（泛指）一个人的；（用于称呼）尊称的
definition_en: belonging to the person or people spoken to
core_image: 桌上两杯咖啡，一杯被推到对方面前，杯柄朝向他
scene: 列车员查票时说：请出示您的车票。Is this your bag on the seat?
sceneCN: 这里 your 是「您的、你的」（第 1 个义项：属于对话对方的）；句意为座位上这个包是你的吗。杯子被推向对方面前，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 限定词（物主限定词）：你的；你们的

derivatives.zh: your 的名词性形式，义为「你的东西」
由 your 与 self 合成，义为「你自己」
由 your 与 selves 合成，义为「你们自己」

senses.title: Belonging to one hearer
senses.titleCN: 你的：属于对方的（单数）
senses.definition: belonging to the single person spoken to
senses.definitionCN: 属于被说话的那一个人
senses.example: Your ticket is in your left pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 你的票在你左边口袋里。
senses.why: The possessive form of you puts the hearer's ownership in front of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 它是 you 的物主形式，把听者的所属关系放在名词前面。

senses.title: Belonging to several hearers
senses.titleCN: 你们的：属于对方一群人
senses.definition: belonging to the group spoken to
senses.definitionCN: 属于被说话的那一群人
senses.example: Please take your seats before the film starts.
senses.exampleCN: 电影开始前请各位就座。
senses.why: One form covers both numbers, just as you does; only context shows the plural.
senses.whyCN: 和 you 一样，一个形式兼指单复数，只有语境能显出复数。

senses.title: People in general
senses.titleCN: 泛指：一个人的、大家的
senses.definition: of people in general, in explanations and rules
senses.definitionCN: 在说明与规则中泛指任何人
senses.example: Your average reader only has ten minutes a day.
senses.exampleCN: 普通读者每天只有十分钟。
senses.why: The hearer stands in for anyone, so your becomes a mild way of saying typical.
senses.whyCN: 听者代替了任何人，于是 your 变成「典型的、一般的」这种温和说法。

senses.title: In titles of respect
senses.titleCN: 尊称：用于称呼大人物的头衔
senses.definition: used before the titles of very senior people, as a mark of respect
senses.definitionCN: 用在尊称头衔前
senses.example: Her Majesty, Your Majesty: the title puts the person above the speaker.
senses.exampleCN: Your Majesty 这类称呼把头衔放在说话人之上。
senses.why: The possessive was once the polite way to address a superior, and it froze in ceremonial titles.
senses.whyCN: 这个物主词曾是称呼尊长的礼貌方式，后来固化在礼仪头衔中。

intro.en: Your is the possessive of you, grown from the Old English plural possessive.
intro.cn: your 是 you 的物主形式，从古英语的复数物主形式发展而来。

items.en: Ēower was the possessive of the plural pronoun you, meaning of you all.
items.cn: Ēower 是复数代词 you 的物主形式，意为「你们所有人的」。

items.en: Þīn was the singular possessive thy, the old partner of your.
items.cn: Þīn 是单数物主 thy，是 your 的旧搭档。

items.en: Your spread to singular use as the polite form replaced thy.
items.cn: 随着尊称取代 thy，your 扩展到单数使用。

items.en: The spelling settled as your while thy and thine faded.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 your，而 thy 与 thine 逐渐消亡。

items.en: Your now serves every hearer, and survives in titles such as Your Majesty.
items.cn: your 如今适用于任何听者，并保留在Your Majesty 这类头衔中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the possessive family; the near-meaning group gathers other possessives and related forms.
note.cn: 形近组收同一物主词族；近义组收其他物主形式与相关词。

entries.definition: The possessive pronoun that stands alone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词性物主代词，义为「你的东西」，可单独使用。

entries.definition: The subject or object pronoun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「你」，作主语或宾语。

entries.definition: The reflexive form for one hearer.
entries.definitionCN: 反身代词，义为「你自己」。

entries.definition: The old singular possessive, now archaic.
entries.definitionCN: 旧的单数物主形式，今已成古语。

entries.definition: Belonging to the speaker; the mirror of your.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「我的」，是 your 的镜像。

entries.definition: Belonging to other people.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「他们的」。

entries.definition: Belonging to people in general, a formal generic possessive.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「一个人的」，是正式的泛指物主形式。

entries.definition: Added after a possessive to stress personal possession.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自己的」，加在物主词后强调归属。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link your to you and to the words it must never be confused with.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 your 与 you 以及容易混淆的词连起来。

normal.en: Your always needs a noun: your ticket, your bag, your turn.
normal.cn: your 后面必须跟名词：your ticket、your bag、your turn。

normal.en: Yours stands alone: the book is yours, no noun needed.
normal.cn: yours 单独用：the book is yours，不需要名词。

normal.en: You are becomes you're; your book keeps the apostrophe away.
normal.cn: you are 缩成 you're；your book 则不加撇号。

normal.en: Your average customer is a soft way of saying the typical customer.
normal.cn: your average customer 是「典型顾客」的委婉说法。

normal.en: Your Majesty: ceremony still keeps the possessive in front of a title.
normal.cn: Your Majesty：礼仪中仍把物主词放在头衔前。

abstract.en: Your marks the hearer's side of the table.
abstract.cn: your 标出桌子对面属于听者的那一半。

abstract.en: A hand pushing a cup toward you: the object is now yours, described with your.
abstract.cn: 一只手把杯子推向你：物品成了你的，就用 your 来修饰。

abstract.en: One possessive, three uses: one person, a group, or anyone at all.
abstract.cn: 一个物主词，三种用法：一个人、一群人、或任何人。

examples.en: Please write your name at the top of the page.
examples.cn: 请把你的名字写在这一页的最上面。

examples.en: Your children can wait in this room.
examples.cn: 你们的孩子可以在这个房间等。

examples.en: Your typical student needs about an hour for this test.
examples.cn: 一般的学生做这个测验大约需要一小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诱」——你的东西很诱人，加在名词前就是 your。

root: 古英语 ēower（你们所有人的），you 的物主形式

sensesIntro.en: One possessive form covering a single hearer, a group, and people in general.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个物主形式兼指单个听者、一群听者与泛指的任何人。

core.en: belonging to the hearer
core.cn: 属于听者

branches.en: SINGLE LINE: belonging to one person addressed.
branches.cn: 单数线：属于被称呼的一个人。

branches.en: PLURAL LINE: the same form for a whole group.
branches.cn: 复数线：同一形式用于一群人。

branches.en: GENERIC LINE: the hearer standing in for anyone.
branches.cn: 泛指线：听者代表任何人。

branches.en: CEREMONY LINE: frozen in titles such as Your Majesty.
branches.cn: 礼仪线：固化在 Your Majesty 一类头衔中。

branches.en: CONTRAST: your names a real owner or a typical one.
branches.cn: 对照线：your 指真实拥有者，也指典型的那一个。

intro.en: your is a native possessive; the elements below are English inflections rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: your 是本土物主词，下面列的是英语构件。

latinIntro.en: No Latin affixes are involved here, so nothing is listed as Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词缀，故不列拉丁条目。

items.exampleCN: 它保留在 your 之中。

items.example: Your own room, not a shared one.
items.exampleCN: 你自己的房间，不是合住的。
你所有的笔记都在这儿。

definition_zh: 你的（东西）；你们的（东西）；（信末）谨上
definition_en: the thing or things belonging to the person or people spoken to
core_image: 两只一样的杯子，其中一个杯底写着名字
scene: 两个学生书包一样，翻开一看，其中一本扉页写着名字。That umbrella is mine, not yours.
sceneCN: 这里 yours 是「你的（东西）」（第 1 个义项：属于对方的东西，单独使用）；句意为那把伞是我的，不是你的。写着名字的那只杯子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 代词（名词性物主代词）：你的（东西）；你们的（东西）

collocations.zh: （不知对方姓名时的书信结尾）敬上

derivatives.zh: yours 的限定词形式，义为「你的」，后面必须跟名词
同一词族的反身形式，义为「你自己」
复数反身形式，义为「你们自己」

senses.title: The thing or things of the hearer
senses.titleCN: 你的（东西）：属于对方的物
senses.definition: the thing already mentioned that belongs to the person spoken to
senses.definitionCN: 已提到的、属于说话对象的东西
senses.example: This pen is yours; mine is the red one.
senses.exampleCN: 这支笔是你的；我的是红色的那支。
senses.why: The possessive pronoun replaces the noun entirely: your plus the object becomes one word.
senses.whyCN: 名词性物主代词把名词整个替换掉：your 加上那个东西，合成一个词。

senses.title: The things of a group
senses.titleCN: 你们的（东西）：属于对方一群人
senses.definition: the things belonging to the group spoken to
senses.definitionCN: 属于被说话的那一群人的东西
senses.example: The seats at the front are yours for the whole show.
senses.exampleCN: 前排的座位整场演出都是你们的。
senses.why: The same form covers the plural, just as you and your do.
senses.whyCN: 和 you、your 一样，同一形式也兼指复数。

senses.title: Letter closing
senses.titleCN: 信末敬语：谨上、敬上
senses.definition: a formula used to close a letter
senses.definitionCN: 写信结尾用的固定敬语
senses.example: I look forward to your reply. Yours sincerely, Li Ming.
senses.exampleCN: 期待您的回复。谨上，李明。
senses.why: The old complimentary close was literally a claim of belonging: the writer offers himself as the reader's servant.
senses.whyCN: 旧式信末敬语字面上是归属声明：写信人把自己说成读者的仆从。

senses.title: A friend of yours
senses.titleCN: 用于限制性短语：你的某位
senses.definition: used after of to single out one of the hearer's things or people
senses.definitionCN: 用在 of 之后，指出对方所拥有的人或物中的某一个
senses.example: A colleague of yours called this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 你的一位同事今天早上打过电话。
senses.why: In this pattern the pronoun works as a base for the double possessive, a very old English habit.
senses.whyCN: 在这个结构里，代词成了双重所有格的基础，这是英语很古老的习惯。

intro.en: Yours grew from your with the ordinary English pronoun ending -s.
intro.cn: yours 由 your 加上英语常见的代词词尾 -s 生长而来。

items.en: Ēower was the possessive base from which the stronger form developed.
items.cn: Ēower 是物主基础形式，后来的强势形式由它发展而出。

items.en: An -s was added to give a form that could stand alone; it is the same -s as in his.
items.cn: 加上 -s 使其能单独使用，这个 -s 与 his 中的相同。

items.en: Mine, thine, yours, hers became the standard independent possessives.
items.cn: mine、thine、yours、hers 成为标准的独立物主代词。

items.en: Yours sincerely became a fixed close in British correspondence.
items.cn: Yours sincerely 成为英式书信的固定结尾。

items.en: The word now sounds mainly formal or emphatic in speech.
items.cn: 如今在口语中，这个词主要显得正式或强调。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the independent possessive pronouns; the near-meaning group puts yours beside related forms.
note.cn: 形近组收独立物主代词；近义组把 yours 与相关形式放在一起对照。

entries.definition: The form used before a noun, never standing alone.
entries.definitionCN: 物主限定词，用在名词前，不能单独使用。

entries.definition: The independent possessive for we.
entries.definitionCN: 名词性物主代词，义为「我们的东西」。

entries.definition: The independent possessive for she.
entries.definitionCN: 名词性物主代词，义为「她的东西」。

entries.definition: The independent possessive for they.
entries.definitionCN: 名词性物主代词，义为「他们的东西」。

entries.definition: The reflexive plural of you, about the hearers themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 反身代词，指听者本人（复数）。

entries.definition: A formal close, but also a jokey way to say I myself.
entries.definitionCN: 固定短语，既是正式信末敬语，也戏称「本人我」。

entries.definition: The same idea with a noun: your own book.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「你自己的」，后面仍跟名词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks mark the line between your and yours.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子划清 your 与 yours 的界线。

normal.en: Your needs a noun; yours is the noun: your bag, or simply yours.
normal.cn: your 要带名词；yours 自己就是名词：your bag 或干脆 yours。

normal.en: Yours sincerely is literally a closing that hands the letter over to the reader.
normal.cn: yours sincerely 字面上是把信交给读者的结尾。

normal.en: A friend of yours: the -s lets the phrase name one of your friends.
normal.cn: a friend of yours：这个 -s 让短语指出你朋友中的一个。

normal.en: Swap one letter and you get ours, ours and yours standing side by side.
normal.cn: 换个字母就是 ours，ours 与 yours 可以并排站。

normal.en: No apostrophe ever: it is yours, not your's.
normal.cn: 永远不加撇号：写 yours，不写 your's。

abstract.en: A name written on the cup bottom: that mark is what -s does to your.
abstract.cn: 杯底写着名字：那个标记就是 -s 对 your 做的事。

abstract.en: Your points outward at a noun; yours points back at the thing already named.
abstract.cn: your 指向后面的名词；yours 指回已说过的那个东西。

abstract.en: Possession as a tag: the tag says who holds the object, and the object needs no repeating.
abstract.cn: 所属关系像一枚标签：标签说明谁持有，物件本身无需重复。

examples.en: Is this coat yours or your sister's?
examples.cn: 这件外套是你的还是你姐姐的？

examples.en: The first two rows are yours.
examples.cn: 前两排是你们的。

examples.en: Yours sincerely, Wang Fang.
examples.cn: 谨上，王芳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「钥匙」——钥匙是你的，加了 s 就是「你的（东西）」。

root: 古英语 ēower（your）加代词词尾 -s

sensesIntro.en: A possessive that drops the noun, and a letter-close that once meant your servant.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个省掉名词的物主词，以及一句原本意为「你的仆人」的信末敬语。

core.en: the hearer's thing, noun left out
core.cn: 听者的东西，名词省略

branches.en: SINGLE LINE: one thing meant, the noun dropped.
branches.cn: 单数线：指一件东西，名词被省掉。

branches.en: PLURAL LINE: several things belonging to a group.
branches.cn: 复数线：属于一群人的多件东西。

branches.en: OF-PHRASE LINE: naming one member from your set.
branches.cn: of 短语线：从你的一群中指出一个。

branches.en: LETTER LINE: the formal close at the end of a letter.
branches.cn: 书信线：信末的正式敬语。

branches.en: CONTRAST: yours states ownership, your modifies a noun.
branches.cn: 对照线：yours 陈述所属，your 修饰名词。

intro.en: yours is formed with an English pronoun ending on a native possessive base.
intro.cn: yours 由本土物主基础形式加英语代词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin affixes are involved here, so nothing is listed as Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词缀，故不列拉丁条目。

items.meaningCN: 使物主词可以单独使用
items.exampleCN: 它把 your 变成 yours。
